0.End: Dismissed, <Player>! <clr>Dragr Bragr<clrEnd> shall continue his career of a true maloq! Now he will try to survive inside a zinc coffin at the bottom of a volcano without oxygen. And you will be getting <Money> cr, since you managed to protect him.
0.Special: What a terrible day, <Player>! Our great warrior Dragr Bragr has perished! Yes, you heard right! After you completed your contract and left your post, the pirates got to him after all. But don't worry, <Player>. Truth be told, Dragr wasn't quite as great as he'd have you believe. Data obtained from the black box showed that he had stashed canned food on his ship, thereby violating the rules and discrediting his feat. Needless to say, his behavior was unbecoming of a true maloq! However, for the sake of Dragr's unblemished memory, we've decided to conceal this sad little fact. May he live on in our hearts a true hero till the end of time! Please take this sum of <Money> cr for your work and silence.
0.Start: Ranger <Player>, what say you about the importance of strength and endurance? As a true maloq, I will tell you that you will not be able to achieve anything without strength and endurance, whilst you will easily make do without intelligence. And our hero here, the famous <clr>Dragr Bragr<clrEnd>, is about to prove just that. He wants to try to survive inside a sealed capsule on spaceship <FullShip> without food and drink for a long period of time. The only danger that may prove his undoing are pirates. Therefore, we require a guard for this ship for <Day> days. Go, what are you waiting for? Oh yes, I almost forgot to mention that you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr for your work!

End: Very good! Of course, you are still no match for the <clr>Red Hatchets<clrEnd> mercenary squad, but you did well just the same. The brass is pleased to allocate you a sum of <Money> cr. Dismissed!

By the way, did you pay the tax for using your transport? Oh, right, rangers are exempt from paying taxes. Damn those bureaucrats and their rules! Remove them from their cushioned posts, I bet they'd sing a different tune!
1.Special: <Player>, terrible news! Turns out we were lied to! The tax collector's ship you were guarding simply vanished from the system, along with all the collected taxes, soon after your contract ended. This heist must have been carefully devised by our enemies, and we hope that the swindler will be punished to the fullest extent of the law! Now, we barely have enough money left to pay for the contract in full, but we could never besmirch our honor by backing out of our agreement. We are therefore transferring <Money> cr to your account.
1.Start: Our planet of <FromPlanet> is home to a treasury of the <clr>Interplanetary Tax Service<clrEnd> (ITS). The treasury is guarded by a SWAT team codenamed <clr>"Red Hatchets"<clrEnd>. The only living creature allowed inside is a specially appointed tax collector. He is currently collecting taxes in this system on his ship <FullShip>. As you well understand, there is always a sizable amount of money on this ship, so it needs good protection. There are <Day> days left before the end of his expedition. The maloqs order you to protect this ship throughout the entire remaining period. We will pay you <Money> cr, if everything goes smoothly. Get going, <Player>, to arms!

10.End: Jolly good, this was some excellent guard duty, and the pay is pretty good at <Money> cr. Although I personally cannot fathom how you managed to protect that ship, considering its warranty expired some 20 years ago! It could have easily fallen apart in space all by itself. Gotta love those businessmen, cutting corners to save on every last cred.
10.Special: It's you, <Player>, finally! Hey, check out my new dirt pool! The very last model, and cast out of pure gold to boot. How could I possibly afford such a luxury? Funny you should ask! When our traders' ship fell to pieces in space, just as I had predicted, I got paid the insurance money. Though we both know what really happened out there, yes? And, in hopes that the truth remains between us, please accept this fee of <Money> cr, stipulated in the contract, as a gesture of goodwill. Sealed lips all the way to the bank, <Player>!
10.Start: Greetings, <Player>! Life is all about business! If you don't work now, you won't survive later, you get me? To that end, we've got a job for you which pays <Money> cr. Your fee will be paid by a group of peleng traveling merchants who sell all sorts of junk on the neighboring planets. They ordered protection for their ship <Ship> for <Day> days. There's no time to waste, get to it!

11.End: Excellent, all the leeches are doing just fine! We are awarding you a sum of <Money> cr. What, not enough? I guess you can also take some medicinal leeches free of charge; they are an excellent treatment, if I may say so myself... You don't want them? Fine, suit yourself. But you're making a mistake!
11.Special: Excellent work, Ranger <Player>, you've accomplished the mission with flying colors! Don't worry about that ship: I've been informed that it was shot down shortly thereafter by our own people. Here is your fee of <Money> cr. By the way, are you keeping up with the latest developments in the field of futuristic medicine? No? What about alternative medicine, you ask? How is that relevant... Here, take a look at the latest invention from our nanolabs: instant pimple mega-remover! You take this here pill... Swallow it... And bam! -- skin smooth as a baby's bottom. What? My skin changed color? A minor defect, we'll fix it before the next batch. Would you like a box for yourself? No? Too bad, this baby will fetch crazy prices on the black market before you know it. Take care now, I'm going to go see how our egghead scientists are doing...
Start: Do you happen to know, <Player>, what our planet is famous for? No? Well, I'll tell you: planet <FromPlanet> is renowned throughout the Galaxy for its top notch medicinal leeches. Just recently carrier vessel <Ship> was deployed to the <InStar> system, crammed full of this natural remedy. As soon as it reached the destination system it was attacked by opponents of alternative medicine. Under threat of annihilation, the attackers demanded that all of the cargo be discharged into open space for total destruction. This time they didn't follow through on their threat, but we really don't feel like testing fate again!

Our growers who breed the leeches have pooled some money together to hire protection for their transport for at least <Day> days. If you see anybody attacking our vessel, know that it's the handiwork of the fanatic proponents of poisoning your body with chemistry, or what is still referred to as traditional medicine. If that happens, strike at them immediately! The more of those bastards you take down, the more money you'll get.

12.End: Great work, <Player>! The ship with the singers remained intact. <clr>Hash Girls<clrEnd> will continue delivering their excellent hits to the public. No producer will destroy these innocent creatures. We will pay you a total of <Money> cr.
12.Special: Whoa! Who goes there?! Oh, it's you, <Player>! I didn't recognize you. What's wrong with your ears? They're swollen? You must have been listening to our favorite girl group, Hash Girls, the whole way back. Am I right? You say they gave you a crystal with their albums on it? And all of them autographed? Why, you're rich now! And the owner of a true artifact besides! What do you mean, why? Wait, you haven't heard? The spiteful music producer made good on his promise to ruin the girls. He caught their ship in open space and shred it to pieces. When the news broke, all Hash Girls records flew off the shelves of music shops in record time, while they became our national heroines! If only you knew how jealous I am, <Player>! A crystal with a personal autograph is worth quite a bit. At any rate, I'll be transferring <Money> cr to your account, seeing as you made good on your part of the contract.
Start: Hey, <Player>, what do you make of pop music? Are you a fan? Or not really? Well, what do you make of <Money> cr then?

The <Ship> superliner is carrying two charming young peleng females, who put on human mini-skirts, kiss and sing. I'm sure you've heard of them -- their band is called <clr>Hash Girls<clrEnd>. So then, recently they ran away from their human producer who invested a whole lot of money into their career, and now he wants to punish them for this betrayal.

At any rate, don't concern yourself with the music business intricacies; focus instead on the <Money> cr that our girls will pay you for protection. At the present they are getting ready for a big tour and are in the market for a proper escort. If you're interested in the job, head on out and give the girls <Day> days of stress-free life.

End: Bravo, <Player>! Now that's what we call excellent protection. Our server safely arrived to destination, whereupon <Money> cr safely arrived into your pocket.

Wait, you still think you were guarding top-secret intelligence data? Don't be so naive, ranger! It concerned our Supreme Lyakusha: political, medical and other information of sensitive nature. His doctors have decided that he has too few enemies, which negatively impacts his ability to make destructive decisions. So we've collected a bit of dirt on him and charged <Ship> with disseminating it all over. Now our Supreme Lyakusha is forced to fend off a growing list of enemies. The political tension is escalating. When he learns of our little scheme, he will surely give out national awards to all who took part in it!
13.Special: Who is that hammering away at my doors? Oh, it's you, <Player>... Quiet down, will you! I'm watching Hash Girls in Supreme Lyakusha's pool, caught on hidden cam! Want to pull up a chair and join me? What? Where did I get the recording? Well... Err... Never mind you that, ranger. Take your <Money> cr and forget everything I said here. Deal? Let's part on friendly terms... Goodbye now!
13.Start: Welcome to the peleng ranger employment center, <Player>! Wondering what makes a peleng center different from the rest? Simple -- we demand a lot more and pay a lot less. Which brings me to my point: we have a mission for you. The <Ship> transport vessel is carrying a <clr>Pelengate-12<clrEnd> server, which contains top-secret data of peleng intelligence. I trust you know how the peleng intelligence agency operates? Countless pivotal industry secrets, intimate details from the private lives of Galaxy celebrities and other luminaries... That's just how we roll, <Player>! Needless to say, humans and maloqs would give their eye-teeth to get their hands on this info. Which is why we want this ship guarded until <Date>. For accomplishing this task we will pay you... umm, a truly exorbitant fee! <Money> cr!

End: Dear <Player>, for successfully escorting <Ship> you've earned a bonus of <Money> cr.

By the way, the strange device was delivered to our scientists. Believe it or not, it turned out to be a prehistoric maloq fuse transmitter. Evidently, the dominators are researching maloq technologies for some unknown reason. Our engineers found nothing strange about it, aside from the fact that it disappears from time to time. Yes, you heard me right. It almost seems like the transmitter responds to some sort of signal, then disappears for several seconds. The maloqs are refusing to admit any involvement with the appearance of this device. And we have little reason to doubt them, considering their race's rather modest advances in technology.
14.Special: Good day to you, <Player>! Finally, there's someone who can shed light on the mysterious disappearance of the vessel <Ship>. No, I understand that nothing happened to the ship while you were fulfilling your contract. But maybe you could speak to the enigmatic artifact that was on board? What, the artifact couldn't be detected by any means? How strange. Then it must be the reason the ship has vanished. At any rate, we will be transferring a sum of <Money> cr to your account, as per our agreement.
Start: After a skirmish with the dominators in the <InStar> system, our diplomatic vessel <Ship> picked up a very strange object, which fell out of the enemy's ship. Said object has nothing in common with any previously discovered dominator tech. It could even be an artifact of some unknown civilization!

Prepare yourself and fly to the <InStar> system, where your task is to ensure the safety of <FullShip> until <Date>. And be on the lookout for pirates -- they're drawn to strange devices like flies to dung! If you accomplish this mission, we will pay you <Money> cr for your services.

15.End: Excellent, <Player>! <clr>Natalie Saphron<clrEnd> is openly propagating a law-abiding lifestyle. Wouldn't you like to heed her advice? Take your <Money> cr and think about it.
15.Special: Ah, there you are, Ranger <Player>! How do you feel about quitting piracy and taking up priesthood? No good? A pity, for we now have an interesting vacancy for repented sinners: a lecturer to replace the late Natalie Saphron. Oh yes, her vessel was shot down shortly after you stepped down as her security guard. Anyway, here's your <Money> cr. Take care now. And remember that our doors are always open to lost souls...
15.Start: A passenger vessel named <Ship> recently took off from our planet. Aside from regular passengers, the ship is carrying a notorious criminal <clr>Natalie Sapron<clrEnd>, sentenced to 299 years in prison. She was promised a reduced sentence in exchange for delivering a course of lectures on the dangers of criminality. However, we have reasons to fear that her former partners, who are still at large, will attempt to neutralize her for betraying her criminal ideals. Therefore, we propose that you guard her ship until <Date> in exchange for a reward of <Money> cr.

16.End: Dear <Player>! Your outstanding performance under this contract has earned you <Money> cr. Also, please accept the sincerest gratitude on behalf of Beatle and Sons.
16.Special: Next! What did you say your name was, <Player>? Let's see here... Contract with Beatle and Sons... Over-enriched uranium... Now I see why you don't look so good... Plus, you're radiating a suspicious glow! Here's what we'll do, ranger. We will allocate for you a sum of <Money> cr. Take a sick leave, go see your grandma in the country somewhere, gorge on fresh synthetic milk -- you know the drill... You'll be good as new before long! Until then... Next!
16.Start: We were contacted by the representatives of a local company <clr>Beatle & Sons <clrEnd> who operates in the enriched uranium goods market. Presently the company is under extreme pressure from its competitors. Initially they were using strictly legal means of economic pressure, but eventually they resorted to outright criminality. As of today, any ship registered to this company and carrying cargo of almost any value is a potential target for the pirates hired by their competitors. <clr>Beatle and Sons<clrEnd> is prepared to pay <Money> cr to ensure protection for their vessel <Ship> for the next <Day> days. If you are interested in this contract, I suggest you head out right away -- their ship is already on the orbit.

17.End: We appreciate your excellent work, <Player>! And candidate <clr>Stephen Jackson<clrEnd> sends his personal gratitude. Are you still undecided for the upcoming election? Why, of course you must vote for my nephew Stephen Jackson! He's the right man for the job, no question about it! I'm telling you this as a totally unbiased, independent expert!
17.Special: Woe is us, Ranger <Player>! After you've completed your security contract for Stephen Jackson, an assassin hired by the opposition managed to get to him and destroy his ship <Ship>. A three-day mourning is in effect planetwide, and all national flags have been lowered. Perhaps you wish to stay an extra day or two and speak at the farewell ceremony? Something patriotic and life-asserting would be swell. Oh, no time? A pity. Thank you for your noble efforts. Please accept this sum of <Money> cr as material support from our government.
17.Start: Our candidate for the post of Galactic Council Curator <clr>Stephen Jackson<clrEnd> is about to go campaigning on all the regional planets. According to Council doctrine, the candidate's planet of origin shall bear all the security expenses. Our government has allocated <Money> cr for this purpose, to be paid for the protection of the candidate and his ship <Ship> over the next <Day> days. You come highly recommended, and we would like to offer the contract to you.

18.End: Dear <Player>, thanks for living up to the terms of your contract so well. By the way, the <Ship>'s entire payload was bought by a certain influential peleng lyakusha who purchased it for his daughter even before the cargo arrived at the exhibition. Imagine that, the girl just can't go without husking her some seeds. The planet they live on has run out of seeds, and our ship carrying a load of rare ancient seeds turned up right on time. The rich have their quirks, don't they? Oh, by the way, the <Money> cr we promised you have already been transferred to your account.
18.Special: Hello, my dear <Player>! What's that strange thing on your shoulder? A shovel? And that, in your hand? Pitchfork? Prick You brand? What a great design! Let me tell you, you are one true gardener! Did you by any chance decide to leave your ranger days behind and become a peaceful farmer? Oh, that's a present for me... Thank you, ranger, much obliged! Did you hear it on the news last night that those radical Greenie Greens had appropriated a load of seeds from aboard the <Ship> and scattered them over one of the unpopulated planets? Now that planet is a veritable farmer heaven, so your present may really come in handy. Here's your <Money> cr for a job well done. Do you agree, <Player>? Great. We'll go book you a ticket for the next flight out right away. Goodbye, ranger.
18.Start: The Never Ending Past club is about preserving the heritage of those great older generations. Our ship <FullShip> is departing for an all-Galaxy exhibition with a load of <clr>ancient plant seeds<clrEnd>, including those of watermelon, carrot and rutabaga. A diplomatic ship makes for an easy target for pirates and mercenaries, and a lucrative one too since its cargo is so valuable. That said, you -- a seasoned pilot with tons of experience -- would fit right in as an escort. Club representatives are offering you a contract for <Money> cr to provide security for the ship until <Date>; and yes, the terms are negotiable. What do you say?

End: Don't be surprised, <Player>, we've had certain changes in the government, so now you will be discussing the contract you have made with my predecessor with me. And please don't tell me you did not know anything about that lying scoundrel's shenanigans. It was you, wasn't it, who helped him fleece unsuspecting dupes collecting funds for the mythical <clr>Save the Dying Planets<clrEnd> foundation? That's exactly how your contract reads: "provide security for the ship"... Um... that's a smart piece of paper all right. I mean, a good lawyer will have no trouble proving your innocence.

Although, we do have a solution -- mentoscopy! We will be able to know for sure whether you have actually been involved in my former colleague's wrongdoing. Never mind that your personality will be completely destroyed in the process. What matters is that justice prevails! Bring in the mentoscope and prepare the operating room!

What's that with your face? Better look here and smile. This is Foolhardy Fools, and you are on hidden camera! Today Ranger <Player> is about to receive the amount of <Money> cr for his incredible poise -- right here on live TV! We'll see you after the commercial break, dear viewers. Don't go away!

Phew... Are you upset with something, ranger? I'm surprised you didn't recognize me. I am Vei-Dis Pesch, the host of the Foolhardy Fools. Then again, how would you even know? I don't think your little space jalopy is equipped with decent stereovision, isn't it? Well, okay, see you folks later; I still have to go play a trick on the local vice-premier. I'll pretend I'm the president and dismiss the entire cabinet... Now, that's a good idea!

Mentoscopy! We'll know it for a fact whether you have been involved in the murder. Never mind that your personality will be completely destroyed in the process. What matters is that justice prevails! Bring in the mentoscope and prepare the operating room!
Special: I'll be damned if this isn't <Player>! Please, come on in, make yourself at home. Seltzer? Mineral water? Regular tap water? You've had more than your fare share of it on the job, have you? I sympathize, I do. They told us here that your client, the one you were protecting, was terminated not so long ago. And we have some information -- mind you, from reliable sources -- that you have had something to do with it. We are going to set it all straight right now.

Mentoscopy! We're about to unveil the whole truth, whether you were involved in the murder or not. True, your identity will be obliterated in the process, but justice will prevail! Bring in the mentoscope, prepare the operation room!

What's that with your face? Better look here and smile. This is Foolhardy Fools, and you are on hidden camera! Today Ranger <Player> is about to receive the amount of <Money> cr for his incredible poise -- right here on live TV! We'll see you after the commercial break, dear viewers. Don't go away!

Phew... Are you upset with something, ranger? I'm surprised you didn't recognize me. I am Vei-Dis Pesch, the host of the Foolhardy Fools. Then again, how would you even know? I don't think your little space jalopy is equipped with decent stereovision, isn't it? Well, okay, see you folks later; I still have to go play a trick on the local vice-premier. I'll pretend I'm the president and dismiss the entire cabinet... Now, that's a good idea!
19.Start: Ranger <Player>, do you know of those out of control fires raging on arid planets? Our charity that goes under the name of <clr>Save the Dying Planets<clrEnd> is sending its <FullShip> ship on a fundraising mission to benefit the planets that have suffered from natural disasters. Naturally, the ship needs an escort. If you agree to provide security for the ship through <Date>, we will pay you a total of <Money> cr as soon as you get back to <FromPlanet>.

2.End: Here you go, here's <Money> cr from Playmaloq, a fine magazine all around. Oh, and by the way, here's a wee bit of bother. None of the models aboard <Ship> are featured in the magazine. No, I do not read it myself, but friends told me about it. Perhaps they were not really models but rather some kind of black market female slaves. Had to be.
2.Special: Welcome back, Ranger <Player>! Did you hear the latest news on RNN yet? No? By all means, apprise yourself. Miko Jackekso's lyakusha cutthroats did take over the liner <FullShip> and then, upon taking all the passengers prisoner, blew the ship up. But that pathetic little Miko made a big mistake! Once aboard the pirate ship, our "girls" revealed their true colors and proved it time and again what a glorious band of warriors our maloq Red Hatchets are. That's us, maloqs! Truly smart! And you, ranger, have earned your <Money> cr and heartfelt gratitude of our counterintelligence.
2.Start: Listen here, Ranger <Player>. The famous space liner <FullShip> owned by Playmaloq magazine has a group of young maloq ladies on board -- models that showcase the new military uniforms. Some wicked pirates have threatened to capture the <Ship> along with all the models. The maloqs learned that Miko Jackekso's lyakusha brigands had been showing too much interest in that ship lately. That pervert is morbidly partial to maloq women. I am sure the pirates intend to kidnap them for their leader. Not that we care, of course! But Playmaloq announced it would pay <Money> cr to anyone who would agree to guard the ship for the next <Day> days. This is a low priority order. Maloqs could use anyone, even a merchant such as yourself.

End: Please accept the sincere gratitude of all the music history fans out there, <Player>! Great job!!! The amount of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account. The defrosting procedure will be complete in the next few days while for the time being we will be watching the singer through a web-cam installed in his compartment.
Umm, the guy's got a funny complexion on him. And he's blowing his cheeks as if he is short of breath. Look, he is moving! Oh, no, I just thought he was.
20.Special: Come on in, Ranger <Player>, go on. Have a seat, have a drink of water, I have a heck of a story for you. No, no, take my word for it. You'd better sit down. <FullShip> has just been destroyed. But what is really bad is not the fact itself, but what we have discovered among the debris. It was... here, have some more water... OK, brace yourself. We have discovered an Elvis Presley doll! They are now having it analyzed to see if all these years we have been keeping a doll in the sarcophagus, or it was only recently that the miscreants have swapped the bodies and then destroyed the ship to cover their tracks. Here's your <Money> cr, all of it. I am so upset that I didn't even withhold anything for the water you drank. Goodbye!
20.Start: Ranger <Player>, you can now witness a very interesting event -- the defrosting of the famous singer <clr>Elvis Presley<clrEnd> from planet Earth who was frozen back in 1977. The technology calls for the first stage of the defrosting process to take place in space under zero gravity conditions. This will be done aboard the <FullShip>. Such procedures were covered by the singer's insurance, and you will be paid <Money> cr out of these proceeds to provide security for the ship and its precious cargo for the next <Day> days.

21.End: We've just received a communication from your colleague ranger <Ship>. <Money> cr seem to be a fairly adequate reward for your efforts.
21.Special: Ranger <Player>, come on in, come on in! Do you know who this ranger <Ship> we hired turned out to be? He was actually a vicious pirate who pretended to be a merchant to steal a valuable piece of equipment. He was loath to do it in your presence, but once your contract expired the rascal tried to escape from our observers into the asteroid belt. So we had to destroy him along with the gadget that was way too valuable to allow to fall into the wrong hands. Still, your own mission was a success, and you deserve your <Money> cr. By the way, I have this impression that you are way more surprised by what I just told you than could be expected. Or am I wrong?
Start: Our planet has a facility to produce non-traditional energy sources. It gives us a substantial competitive advantage over our less successful competitors, so they decided to hire pirates to eliminate our transports in space. The results of this asymmetric warfare are nowhere near decisive; however, we have already lost two ships.

Now we decided to change tactics. We have hired a professional commercial pilot -- ranger <Ship> -- as the captain of our transport. The second part of this great plan of ours calls for hiring another pilot -- an experienced fighter -- who would provide fire support for the merchant vessel. This is where you come into play, <Player>. You will not be told the merchant ship's final destination; the only thing we can tell you is that it will visit a number of planets. Keep your distance and only open fire in case of an apparent attack. Provided ranger <Ship> remains operational through <Date>, you will receive a bonus of <Money> cr in your account.

22.End: Space liner <Ship> is still in one piece, and <Money> cr have been transferred to your account. As could be expected, the first curia faeyan team of intellectuals has taken the respectable second place. It would have undoubtedly won the first had it not been for the traditional scheming by the peleng team.
22.Special: Good afternoon, my dear <Player>! Have you ever thought of changing careers? The vibes emanating from your brain are telling me you are interested. The government, as represented by yours truly here, has an attractive proposition for you: to coach our new plasma checkers team. The entire population of our planet has been mesmerized by your brilliant out-of-competition performance at the championship. Now, what happened to the old team and their coach you may ask. Well, that's a fairly tragic story... If memory serves me right, you have abandoned your mission when your contract expired, right before they tallied the scores, have you not? So here goes. The maloq team, upset about their loss, lodged a protest against peleng cheating. When their request to have the results reconsidered was denied, the entire team proceeded to the reactor room and shut down the primary containment system. You know these crude maloqs: for them, death is preferable to coming back home dishonored. So, ranger, are you ready to become the new coach? No? What a loss! Then we are just going to transfer <Money> cr to your account and wish you luck with your arduous endeavors.
Start: Dear <Player>, if you were paying attention these past four days, you couldn't have missed the announcement about the upcoming plasma checkers championship. This highly intellectual event is going to take place aboard <FullShip> where the greatest minds of different species will convene, including the ambassadors from several planets.
In light of these very special circumstances, we cannot afford leaving this ship without combat escort. You will be paid <Money> cr to make sure the ship proceeds safely until <Date>.

End: The transport <Ship> is still safe and sound, so you will be paid your fee of <Money> cr. High school teachers thank you for your service.

The only thing that progressive intellectuals of <FromPlanet> cannot approve is the way faeyans and humans are proposed to be tested together. Intellectual capacity of these two species in a large enough number of fields is radically different, which is bound to affect the test scores. Naturally, not to human advantage.
23.Special: It looks like a good day for you, dear <Player>! Here's you well-deserved <Money> cr. And don't you feel sorry for the <Ship>'s dead pilot. He got off easy. Just imagine, when you were away he was trying to sell the answer key to those among the humans who were willing to pay for it. Naturally, what would the fae want with them? Then, in order to get rid of the witness, the buyers blew the ship up once they laid their hands on the answers. Luckily, the police caught up with the miscreants; they have been arrested, and the answer key was safely delivered to its intended destination.
23.Start: Ranger <Player>, the glow of your brain's aura is telling me that you have forgotten anywhere from 45 to 64% of whatever they taught you in high school. For that reason, you might be interested to know that the Galactic Council has introduced a unified state exam that would be the same for both faeyan and human graduates. The answer key to that test, which is considered to be a very important cargo, will be transported aboard the <FullShip>. We are offering <Money> cr to anyone who would agree to escort the ship until <Date>. If you feel you are up to this mission, program a course to the <InStar> system into your onboard computer. This is where the <Ship> is currently at berth.

24.End: Ranger <Player>, your mission is now 89.54% complete, which is 9.22% over the minimum needed for it to be deemed a success. Oh, and by the way, it was actually a reporter for the human magazine Peeping Together who worked undercover to photograph private lives of local celebrities that had arrived for the inter-galactic Oscar awards ceremony. In any event, your fee of <Money> cr has been earned in good faith.
24.Special: Ranger <Player>, you have accomplished your mission successfully. Congratulations, and here is your agreed upon fee of <Money> cr. By the way, have you heard the news? Not to long ago, bodyguards for one of the stereovision stars attacked the <Ship> that you used to escort in the past. Apparently, in addition to stereographic and panoramic filming, there were hidden cameras installed aboard the ship that were used to take pictures of the star's private life. Those high definition pictures were specifically taken for the human magazine Peeping Together. You can check them out in its most recent issue. So in a nutshell that unfortunate paparazzi got exactly what he deserved and your conscience should be clear. It's not like you knew anything about that secret shoot, is it?
24.Start: You are being offered an escort mission to protect the <Ship> that is now conducting a stereographic and panoramic survey of open space in the <InStar> system with a view to creating new, more precise maps of the sector. A fee of <Money> cr will be paid to you as soon as our agent contacts us on <Date> to confirm that his flight is proceeding safely.

25.End: Donated organs have arrived safely to their destination to be used for their intended purpose. The amount of <Money> cr has been transferred to your account as per the contractual terms.
25.Special: Oh, so now you don't need your internal organs, <Player>! And you want to donate them to the Yellow Cross... Well... Somehow you don't seem to be affected by the three-tier mental transgulation. Chances are the constant vibration of combat must have reduced your sensitivity to our equipment. Your are very much in luck, ranger. Faeyan Academy of Science has instituted a prize in the amount of <Money> cr to be awarded to whoever survives this process. The money has already been transferred to your account. And don't you worry about the ship with the cargo of donated organs that has been destroyed. The ship was about to be scrapped anyway, and the cargo was delivered on time.
Start: Dear <Player>, a few days ago a portion of the fae society on planet <FromPlanet> experienced the three-tier mental transgulation. As a result, hundreds of faeyans of the second and third curiae suffered a lethargic collapse. For the time being, while they remain in this state, their internal organs, except for the cranial ones, have been removed and made available for temporary use by other patients.

At the moment, the International Yellow Cross ship <Ship> with a load of these organs on board is at anchor on the orbit of planet <FromPlanet> awaiting its escort. If you agree to provide security for the ship for the next <Day> days, you will receive a fee of <Money> cr from the Yellow Cross.

26.End: The faeyan government appreciates your contribution to the safety of <FromPlanet> children and will transfer the amount of <Money> cr to your account as an incentive for the future. In addition to that and much to these children's delight, you have demonstrated some great space maneuvering for them. You can check out their photographs of your ship on the Galanet at <clr>ggg.<clrEnd><Player><clr>.kiddie_talents.fei<clrEnd>.
26.Special: Congratulations on a job well done, <Player>! I would also like to apologize to you for having misinformed you when the contract was being made. Since we knew it in advance that the <FromStar> system is not safe for passage, we have planned a special cover operation using the new holographic DNDG generator. Naturally, we couldn't set our little intellectuals on their way without providing them with adequate cover. Did you see anything strange about the <Ship>? No? None of the head hunters noticed anything either, and once your contract expired they went to destroy what happened to be a mere holographic matrix, a ghost ship. All of it at while our children were having the time of theirs lives under solid military escort. Please accept these <Money> cr as a compensation for your valuable time.
Start: Ranger <Player>, the administration of planet <FromPlanet> has chosen you for a mission, which you should consider a great honor. Jointly with the humans, we have recently held an interstellar young talent contest that, naturally, young faeyan intellectuals won. As a reward, the winners will be sent on a space cruise aboard the space liner <Ship>.

However, since the <FromStar> system is not particularly secure, you have been ordered to provide security for the liner in transit until <Date>. Once the mission is successfully accomplished, you will be paid <Money> cr.

27.End: Ranger <Player>, you have lived up to all your contractual obligations; however, in order to receive your fee you must now beat me in a multiuser game of Quark with bots. That was a joke, of course, ha-ha-ha. That's human humor rubbing off on me.
27.Special: What's wrong with you, <Player>? Why are you swaying and bobbing so? What was that again? You and the <Ship>'s captain had a game of Third Quark too many? Yes, we already know about that sad affair. Still, you were lucky considering that the poor wretch had suffered a total mental breakdown. Screaming "I am gonna get you, dang bots!" he began attacking peaceful ships and had to be destroyed in order to protect thousands of innocent lives. Here is your bonus of <Money> cr. Take it and go check yourself into our best medical facility immediately. It wouldn't hurt if an experienced psychologist had a look at you. You never know.
27.Start: Ranger <Player>, your next task is not particularly difficult, yet it is still very important and requires complete concentration. A group of famous computer game developers have recently released a beta version of the <clr>Third Quark<clrEnd> game. A small diplomatic ship, the <Ship>, will be transporting a consignment of these games for testing. In light of the great public interest in this event, the amount of <Money> cr has been allocated to pay for an escort to company that ship on its voyage. If you, an independent combat pilot, can guarantee the ship's safety for a period of <Day> days, the said amount will be paid to your account as soon as the contract expires.

28.End: What a delight it is to see two rangers, yesterday's pirates, working together shoulder to shoulder! Clean space is key for lasting peace and prosperity. It is good to know that you, ranger <Ship> and many others understand this, since it is only through our joint efforts that we can bring prosperity to this Galaxy, which is our common home. Don't forget to brush your teeth every night!
28.Special: We have learned that your partner did in fact get himself whacked. Yes, we know what kind of language he used referring to you. Let me assure you that you bear no resemblance whatsoever to any of the animals he had compared you to, neither developmentally, nor in appearance. We are positive that <Ship> was altogether incorrigible. Regardless, and notwithstanding the fact that we do not believe in coincidence, we must admit that your mission was a complete success. Here's your <Money> cr, and next time please stay away from any proving grounds while military exercises are in progress.
28.Start: Oh ye wretched <Player>, a purveyor of conduct unbecoming! We are running a special project for you and other repenting criminals like yourself to give you all an opportunity to volunteer for purifying corrective labor. One of your colleagues, ranger <Ship>, participates in the program collecting and carting trash; you will serve as his security detail. By making sure that ranger remains unharmed until <Date>, you will demonstrate that you have set foot on the path to rehabilitation. Are you ready? Good luck and Godspeed!

29.End: Oh ye worthy ranger! The utterly successful completion of your mission to protect <Ship> is well worth the <Money> cr you are receiving as a reward. You have earned it honorably! Tune to gaalian channels to watch the championship opening ceremony, which in itself is worth seeing. May the stars shine upon you, <Player>!
Special: Greetings, Ranger <Player>! Congratulations on a job well done! Here is your agreed upon fee of <Money> cr. Your operation to protect the sham carrier looked very convincing. I can only imagine the faces of those rascals when they are watching the championship opening ceremony after blowing up that old barge!
You have to hurry, <Player>, or you won't be able to see it live! The championship is about to open.
Start: Have you ever heard of astral golf -- one of those athletic activities that bring one closer to understanding the higher truths? The next all-gaal astral golf championship is about to open soon, and we are really looking forward to the event. This sport has a levitating <clr>Astral Ball<clrEnd> for a mascot. It's made of antimatter.

A specially equipped ship, the <Ship>, will deliver the ball to the venue from the place of its permanent storage. However, there is a chance that some violently inclined fans of simpler physical games, such as anti-gravitational soccer, may attempt to steal this unique item, one of the most remarkable in the entire Universe. We request that you take it upon yourself to provide security for the <Ship> and hope that it will remain unharmed until <Date>.

3.End: You helped save the <Ship>. The faeyans assure us that the vaccine is almost ready. Here, take your <Money> cr and fall out!
3.Special: What a misfortune, <Player>! After you stopped escorting the transport, those damn pirates boarded it, captured the vaccine and blew the ship to smithereens. But don't let this upset you. That was no vaccine at all, but the newest mutant virus developed specifically for fighting the pirates. Once inside the body, it causes an irrepressible urge to share and give all your possessions away. Now all the stellar systems will be truly enriched. No, no, put your cash away, you will need it yourself. On the contrary, the government will pay you <Money> cr for the job well done -- net of the cost of the anti-benevolence virus shot. On second thought, why don't we pay it to you in full. Wait, what the heck am I saying? Get out of here, ranger, it looks like the virus is airborne!
3.Start: The maloq planet of <FromPlanet> is going through some very hard times. There is some virus in the air that we cannot find a cure for. We have fallen so low as to hire faeyan scientists. They have come up with a vaccine, but before it is ready to use it has to be kept at zero gravity for a while, in open space. The faeyans explained it to us why this had to be done though we didn't get much from all that arcane gibberish. Long story short, the vaccine is now being ferried back and forth around the <InStar> system aboard the <Ship>. Maloqs' enemies may try to attack this defenseless transport. We can't let this happen. To that end, I am ordering you to keep an eye on the ship until <Date>. We will even go as far as paying you <Money> cr for this job. You have your orders now.

End: Ranger <Player>, virtue is the only true way for those who set foot on the path of glory. You have successfully accomplished our first challenge guarding the <Ship>, and here's another one: try spending these <Money> cr without falling victim to consumerism. And most of all, beware of greed and indifference!
Are you still having doubts? In that case, we advise spending the money here to purchase spiritual literature to cleanse your soul.
30.Special: Ranger <Player>, it is common knowledge that charity and peace-building are the virtues that are always in short supply, even with such heroes as yourself. And we sincerely hope that your unwillingness to step in and fight the villain that had destroyed the <Ship> was not spurred by any concerns about possible costs of having your ship repaired, but rather by a wish to start on a long journey towards spiritual cleansing of your soul. As fate would have it, the ship that you had been instructed to protect was shot down after the term of your contract expired. For that reason, you are going to receive your deserved reward of <Money> cr. We sincerely hope that following in the steps of many of our fellow citizens you will donate that amount to the foundation to benefit backwards species.
Start: Ranger <Player>, we know that you resort to force to punish those who deserve it; however we want to encourage you to be more considerate in your methods. These are the methods we suggest you try right now.

The <Ship> transport that is currently making a number of deliveries in the <InStar> system requires protection. Please do your best to guard it in such a way as to avoid opening fire on any living things unless absolutely necessary, resorting instead to diplomacy and inspiration. Your mission will last for <Day> days, whereupon you may return to planet <FromPlanet>.

Oh, yes, I almost forgot. Most certainly, money is nothing compared to true values, but in this imperfect world you cannot do without. Which is why you will receive the amount of <Money> cr if you accomplish this mission successfully.

31.End: Dear <Player>, your mission is accomplished since the <Ship> has successfully reached its destination. You have proven it that you do not deviate from important principles. We will even go a step further and pay you <Money> cr to fund your continuous spiritual development.
Special: Hello, <Player>. I hope you have already heard that the ship you were protecting was destroyed shortly after your mission was over. Fortunately, a military patrol happened to be nearby and managed to save the bulk of the library; however, a number of optical scrolls have been lost, including the complete works of S. Hakespeare, the chronicles of the order of St. Devilaire and a personnel roster of the Dzuhallag secret service. We will now need to charter an entire fleet to somehow transfer the lost information to modern galomedia from the optical disks on which a backup copy of the library is stored. You can go now.
Oh, yes... You have completed your contract, so here is your fee of <Money> cr.

Are you still here? So you are proposing to install the equipment for transferring information to modern galomedia right where the library backup disks are located, isn't that right? That's a great idea! Strangely enough, it has never occurred to us before. Thank you again, and good luck to you.
Start: Dear <Player>, the liner <Ship> that has just launched from our planet has an ancient gaalian library on board. These optical scrolls are several thousand years old! In <Day> days the library will arrive at the Academy of the Spirit where its content will be copied to more appropriate modern galomedia. However, as chance would have it, a certain short-sighted peleng has gotten it into his head that one of these ancient scrolls contains a recipe for the immortality elixir. This is very unwise of him, since the gaals have long been able to reach immortality through simple genetic modification, which is what the immortality elixir is all about; however, that technology has only been developed for our own species. Apparently, this peleng is incapable of understanding this simple truth.

We were unable to dissuade this aberrant individual and now fear he might resort to violence. We would like you to fully grasp the idea that the <Ship> desperately needs protection and volunteer to guard it until <Date>.

We realize that you would have done it for free, what with the sacred nature of the task and all, but we could not in good faith take advantage of you in such a blatant manner. Consequently, once you accomplish your mission, the amount of <Money> cr will be transferred to your account. I hope you are not offended by us offering you money.

End: Dear <Player>, watching your excellent work has been a true pleasure! We have learned that the mobile zoo is no longer in danger.

Don't you feel proud of having successfully completed such an important mission? We hope that these <Money> cr, will not diminish your self esteem in any way since you have honestly earned this money.
32.Special: Greetings, <Player>. Despite all your efforts, the mobile zoo has been destroyed. Oh, come on, don't eat your heart out over it! We did manage to save all the animals! The <Ship> was downed after your protection contract expired, so I have every reason to pay you your <Money> cr for a job well done. I can tell it by just looking at your face: you feel better already!
Start: Ranger <Player>, where do you stand on the issue of animals? Our system is hosting a visiting mobile zoo that collects rare species from various planets and at the same time shows off those it already has. The zoo is based aboard a ship named <Ship> that is currently located in this system here. The thing is that right now they have a few rare venuyan lamas on board whose tusks are worth their weight in enriched strontium at some of the Galaxy's black markets.

The vessel has already been attacked by unknown ships while in the <FromStar> system, and the management is hell-bent on not taking any more risks. Under the weight of our high humanistic principles, we feel responsible for what is going on within our system and thus took the initiative to sponsor an armed effort to protect this ship. You will be paid <Money> cr if the mobile zoo proceeds safely though <Date>, much to the joy of the public that is anxious to see the amazing biological diversity of creation.

End: You have lived up to all our expectations, <Player>! Transport <Ship> is unharmed and continues its search for a suitable planet that could become this unique creature's new home. And once it finds one, all we have to do is wait and see how large the creature can grow and whether it can become larger than the planet itself one day!
Here's a modest reward of <Money> cr as a token of our appreciation. Use it for a good cause!
Special: Dear <Player>, words fail me to express how utterly flabbergasted I am about what you have done! I just can't see how such an intelligent humanoid could simply stand by watching a civilian transport being destroyed -- the one that carried the single specimen... I couldn't care less about the term of your contract having expired! It was your duty to protect the <Ship> regardless of any financial interests. We are not going to pay you for your indifference and manifest disregard for the life and well-being of this simple-minded creature.
Wait a minute! Someone is calling me on the intercom...

Yesss! What cancellation penalty? How much did you say?! OK, I got it. Well, ranger, a contract is a contract. Gaals always abide by contractual terms, so we are going to pay you the agreed upon fee of <Money> cr. I hope that your guilty conscience will not let you spend this money on anything untoward. Good afternoon to you!
Start: During one of their experiments, our biologists managed to breed a unique creature capable of previously unseen unfettered growth. This growth potential is so off the charts that even our best gene engineers couldn't do anything about it. As of this moment, the creature is over 40 yards tall and adds another half a yard daily. There is no stopping this process, so we have no other choice but to place the creature somewhere in a natural environment on one of the uninhabited planets.

<Player>, your mission and contribution to global science will consist in providing security for the <Ship> for the next <Day> days while it is searching for a suitable planet for the creature. No one must threaten the life of this cute little critter! It must be let live like every other creature in the Universe! If you do your job well, we stand ready to pay you <Money> cr for your troubles.

End: That's just horrible, my dear <Player>! It is for the second time already that the maloqs are returning an entire shipment of new equipment for warranty repairs. These are all the models designed specifically for their species, with a built-in gunnery complex intended for better stress reduction. Not even titanium triggers last those maloqs for more than 5 minutes.

If it keeps on going like this, we'll go out of business. Altruism doesn't pay the bills, you know. So, without further ado, here is your fee of <Money> cr along with our gratitude for your help promoting sports. I am sure you know that old human saying, a sound mind in a sound body.
Special: Who are you? Oh yes, now I remember, please come in, <Player>. By the way, do you know that the <FullShip> has been attacked by pirates and shot down? Are you saying no? Well, I find this hard to believe. Have a look, here's something new we came up with. You see, your seat got so much warmer and is smoking. And you know why? It's an exercise bike with a built-in lie detector. If you told a lie sitting on it, you wouldn't have been all that comfortable now, he-he. It's an incentive to tell the truth, so to speak -- a special order from peleng security services, to be used during interrogations.
By the way, would you care to check whether you are telling the truth yourself? Wait, don't you rush for the exit so soon. First collect the well deserved <Money> cr you are due under this contract.
Start: Do you play any sports, <Player>! What was that again? Well, it never occurred to me that shooting up dominators could be considered a sport. Then you are apparently unaware that our planet is home to the largest manufacturer of exercise bikes in the Galaxy. Our models are in high demand on all planets and by all species since we put the consumer, rather than our own profits, first. Thus, for the gaals, we manufacture special machines with built-in trash dematerializers that are capable of incinerating up to two tons of trash per workout.

But enough advertising; you have come to receive your orders, haven't you? We can offer you a mission to protect our transport <Ship> that will be delivering our products to consumers for the next <Day> days.

End: Ah, <Player>, come in. Careful, don't trip over that cabinet. And don't hit your hand on that window frame.
What happened? Isn't it obvious?

The maloqs delivered a wrong projectile by mistake. How could they make such a blunder, you ask? It's incidents like this that cement their reputation as the Galaxy's dimwits! You should have been here when it fired! Half the city was turned to ruin! And then there was the peleng that flew in through my window. Before I even came to my senses, he grabbed a whole bunch of valuables and hightailed it. And this wasn't an isolated incident!

To our surprise, the Tsar Cannon stayed intact after the volley. As for you, the mission was completed without reproach, and your fee of <Money> cr is well deserved. And now you must excuse me -- I've got to fetch my writing desk from the neighboring building.
Special: Ah, <Player>, come in. Careful, don't trip over that cabinet. And don't hit your hand on that window frame.

I have to note that soon after the cannon was delivered here, <FullShip> was turned to dust. I suspect that the pirates were hoping to pocket the delivery fee, but the vessel refused and fought back! Your mission, however, was completed without reproach, so please take your fee of <Money> cr, as agreed.
What happened here? Isn't it obvious? The cannon was delivered to our planet intact. To our great sorrow!

The maloqs delivered a wrong projectile by mistake. How could they make such a blunder, you ask? It's incidents like this that cement their reputation as the Galaxy's dimwits! You should have been here when it fired! Half the city was turned to ruin! And then there was the peleng that flew in through my window. Before I even came to my senses, he grabbed a whole bunch of valuables and hightailed it. And this wasn't an isolated incident!
Amazingly enough, the Tsar Cannon somehow survived the volley. And now you must excuse me -- I've got to fetch my writing desk from the neighboring building.
Start: Ah, <Player>, we have a mission for you.

As you may know, our planet will be hosting an international exhibition of prehistoric arms in <Day> days. For this purpose, an ancient museum piece -- the famous Tsar Cannon -- is being delivered here from planet Earth. We've even purchased a special permit from humans to fire one shot from this antiquated wonder during the parade that will be taking place in our capital.

The cannon is currently aboard <FullShip>. Your mission is to protect the vessel from pirates who are itching to get their paws on the invaluable relic. If the cannon is kept safe and sound for <Day> days, you will receive compensation in the amount of <Money> cr, as well as our sincerest gratitude.

End: Congratulations, <Player>! You have now completed this difficult mission. Now other righteous warriors will follow your example and little by little help free the universe of evil, sins and dark forces we are all wallowing in.

I am sure you are now feeling a rush of luminous energy and euphoria caused by your own good deeds. However, I regret to inform you that the fact that we have availed ourselves of your services means that, according to the galactic moral code, we now have to pay you the amount of <Money> cr. Money never does anyone any good, so you'd be well advised to simply donate it to the universal orphan fund. We hope you will listen to the voice of reason.
Special: It is so sad to learn that renegade <Ship> has been destroyed, especially after you have accomplished your mission so successfully and on schedule. However, I regret to inform you that the fact that we have availed ourselves of your services means that, according to the galactic moral code, we now have to pay you the amount of <Money> cr -- despite the fact that the poor renegade will never again be able to delight us with his exemplary behavior.
And remember that money never does anyone any good, so you'd be well advised to simply donate it to the universal orphan fund. We hope you will listen to the voice of reason.
Start: Dear ranger <Player>, we have to make a very special request of you. As you know, we gaals are a very peaceful species and cannot stand any violence whatsoever directed against individuals. Appeasement, search for the truth and quiet contemplation of the surrounding universe make for the key principles of our existence.

However, meeting other species has caused our compatriots to acquire some of their negative traits and clouded our crystal clear auras. In particular, this concerns piracy. As hard as it may be to admit, there are more and more renegade gaals out there. The government of <FromPlanet> has developed a new system to rehabilitate such individuals. Our scholars have concluded that up to 70% of all those wretches may be rehabilitated if a renegade gaal gets a righteous and selfless warrior for a mentor.
And that's exactly what we wanted to ask of you, <Player>.

I hereby suggest that you locate pirate <Ship> who is engaged in unlawful activities in the <InStar> system. You will need to establish contacts with him, explain your mission goals to him and continue to protect him from the corrupting influence of alien cultures for a period of <Day> days.
Successfully accomplishing this mission will help you achieve deep spiritual satisfaction and rejoice in the knowledge that you have saved a lost gaal soul.

37.End: Ah, there you are, <Player>! Today, you are our hero. Over a single week, the stock of Liga Light company has risen by one hundred and ninety points. Do you know what that means? It means that I am rich now. Filthy rich! What? Oh, your fee... Sometimes one forgets about such trifles... Here's your <Money> cr. On second thought... Listen, <Player>, how about getting paid in kind? Our goods are very popular now, and the demand is soaring. What does it mean you don't want them? It isn't a good idea at all to pass up such a great offer! All right, all right. And now that you got your money, kindly get out of my sight.
37.Special: Ah, there you are, <Player>! Talk of the devil! Are you aware that <FullShip> has been destroyed? What do you mean you don't know anything? And don't you throw your contract at me! So you are saying the ship was still unharmed on <Date>? You didn't by any chance blow it up yourself accidentally, did you? Oh, all right, I apologize, it's that paranoia of mine. You are right, you have honestly lived up to all the contractual terms. Man, we should have talked you into signing up for a longer term. Naturally, Liga Light has suffered quite a loss on this, but what is it they say, the laser pen is mightier than the vibrosword? Here's your <Money> cr. How about a drink to drown our sorrows? Oh, you are flying... Well, good luck then.
37.Start: Your age? Height? Weight? Blood type? Religious and political beliefs? Weighted average share of smuggled goods in your annual gross receipts? Aha, gotcha! But don't sweat it, <Player>, mum's the word. Oh, yes, your mission... I completely forgot. We do have a small assignment for you. The thing is that those dogged pelengs have virtually monopolized all the narcotic goods trade. The most entrepreneurial species that we are, we simply cannot ignore that segment of the market. Liga Light became the first company that took on peleng smugglers. Naturally, our goods are all certified and totally safe. Besides, it is all perfectly legal. We have lobbied for the legalization of these dru..., um, excuse me, perfectly safe medications, for hundreds of years. And we are finally there now. Of course, the pirates are not just going to sit and watch their livelihood being taken away from them. For that reason, Liga Light is willing to bear some reasonable expense and pay <Money> cr to anyone who agrees to provide protection to the <FullShip> until <Date>. Please be so kind and figure it out yourself where that ship is located. I am only an intermediary and have no intention to pay for your services out of pocket. It is up to you, of course, whether to take me up on this offer or not. Just keep it in mind, it may no longer be on the table tomorrow.

End: Oh, hey, <Player>. Wait a moment... Lick my inversion cutter, you beast!
Sorry, ranger, that wasn't for you. You can climb out from under that table. It's just me playing Space Voyagers -- the game is the bomb! As for you, here's your well-earned <Money> cr.
...let's see here... Engine upgrade - 600 creds, a support emitter - 400. Hmm... I guess I'll do the postal quests first.
Special: Hey there, Ranger <Player>. Wait a moment... Lick my inversion cutter, you beast!
Oh, <Player>, that wasn't for you... You can climb out from under that table. It's just me playing Space Voyagers -- the game is the bomb! As for you, here's your well-earned <Money> cr.

By the way, <FullShip> was actually destroyed not long ago, and the pirates did get their hands on the game. Thankfully, while you were guarding the liner, the devs managed to install the updated version of the Space Guard protection system. Meaning the pirates are out of luck.
38.Start: How would you like some security work? Singular Gamebuilders, the Galaxy's largest game development studio, is set to release their new hit titled Space Voyagers. Fans of the genre have been camping outside their offices for weeks now, demanding early release. As you can imagine, finishing a game in those conditions is hardly ideal. The final QA stages were therefore moved to a liner called <Ship>. Except now we're worried that pirates will try to steal the game and start distributing pirated copies. Your job is to protect the company's liner from pirates and any other potential danger. The game is scheduled to release on <Date>.

End: Dear <Player>, you cannot even imagine how much you have helped us. Our method has been proven to be superior and very soon it will be widely adopted by the entire industry. Everything went fine except that nothing has worked on the maloqs. They slept through the entire flight snoring terribly, thus depriving the folks from the other species of any chance to relax. Regardless, we are going to pay you the agreed upon <Money> cr for your services.

By the way, how about relaxing some after your long flights? We can find you a spot on our next flight. No? What a pity! In this case, let me simply wish you good luck with your future flights. I hope you will have plenty more of them.
39.Special: Oh, <Player>. As sad as it is, I have to tell you that <Ship> has been destroyed. However, you have completely lived up to your contractual obligations, for which reason we are going to transfer the amount of <Money> cr to your account. Testing was completed, but shortly after that the ship was attacked, which proved to be a real tragedy for all of us. Not only did innocent folks die, but faeyan-made equipment that had taken years to make was completely destroyed. Now we will have to start it all over again. But that's our problem. Thank you, ranger, I wouldn't dare holding you back any longer.
Start: What can we offer such a hotshot ranger as yourself, <Player>? Simple cargo deliveries are way below your pay grade. But don't worry, we have a mission worthy of your attention for you.

Pray tell, what do you think harmony is worth? Have you ever heard of the new relaxation method called fae-nui? No? Well, that doesn't surprise me at all since like I said this is a new method. It involves relaxation of the entire body in open space under the influence of special audio tones. No one has ever used this method before, so we and our faeyan colleagues are going to test it aboard ship <Ship>. To avoid any undue attention, the ship has been disguised as a regular faeyan liner. The testing will continue until <Date>. Volunteers from every race will participate in this journey. Since we consider it to be a very important flight, we would like you to escort the ship and ensure its complete security. Once <Ship> contacts us upon completion of the testing to confirm their satisfaction with your services, we will pay you <Money> cr. If you agree, you can get started right away. We're counting on you, ranger.

4.End: Excellent! The maloq sports federation of planet <FromPlanet> is glad to present you with <Money> cr for the great job you did protecting the <Ship> space liner. Never forget about the power of the spirit and do 200 push-ups daily. Remember -- only strength will save the Galaxy!
4.Special: Oh, it's you, <Player>... A great misfortune has befallen our nation: space liner <Ship> has been destroyed. What a blow it is for the maloq sports federation! But don't you worry, this is not your fault. The pirates shot it down after your mission was over. You lived up to the terms of your contract just fine. As agreed, we will transfer the amount of <Money> cr to your account. But wouldn't you make me company in my grief? How about a drink of some smuggled premium voodka? What? Oh, you are living healthy... You are right, ranger! You are absolutely right. In this case, fare thee well. It was nice meeting you.
Start: Tomorrow, the annual sports games will begin to commemorate yet another anniversary of our victory over the klissan. This time they will be held aboard the <Ship> space liner. The ship will host veteran families and some of the most beloved maloq heroes.

We want these games to be a thoroughly enjoyable experience, so extra security will be in place. The chief of security on board is one of the famous maloq Red Hatchets, so domestic terrorism is not going to be a concern. Where you will step in is external security. You will escort the ship for <Day> days. The liner has already taken off so you must hurry to catch up with it soon.

40.End: This is just great, <Player>! Testing went well, and the technology proved to be worth every penny we had invested in it. Of course, it wasn't ours -- we simply borrowed it from two gaal merchants... But anyway, that's not important. Now we could easily initiate a conflict between gaals and faeyans, which would make our activities on their planets so much easier. And for all of that we have you to thank! Here are your <Money> cr -- you have earned them honestly.
40.Special: I have bad news for you, <Player>. Once you took your leave of <FullShip>, it was immediately attacked by several ships whose pilots had been irradiated by the transmitter. Still, the crew managed to send a report out on the testing having been completed successfully; the ship's demise only confirms the device's efficiency. Here is your <Money> cr.
Start: Why are you rangers so impatient? All you want is new missions! Why don't you try our coffee for a change -- which, by the way, is the best in the Galaxy. Not that it matters though, one way or another...

We will sure always have something for such a famous buccaneer as yourself. The secret development service supported by Dzuhallag is about to begin the final testing of a new device called a psy-generator that irradiates brains of living creatures with waves of a certain frequency. The results are somewhat reminiscent of those produced by large doses of agressine, except the new device could induce this condition remotely over long distances. Just imagine all the prospective opportunities we will have once the Intelligence Directorate receives this device.

Except there is one small problem. Operating this prototype device that has been installed aboard diplomatic ship <Ship> may very well cause the ship to be attacked for no good reason by overly aggressive irradiated pilots. This is where we need your help. If you can ensure security of the test flight until <Date>, we will pay you <Money> cr, which I am sure you will agree is quite a large amount. But make sure you take this little gadget with you, it will protect your own brain from the rays produced by our device. So how about it?

End: Hurry up! Hurry up! Have you found the solution yet? What do you mean you don't know? It looks like it's suddenly time to leave this planet that has become quite uncomfortable. Ranger, do you have room for another pilot? I even have some experience fighting dominators. Oh, and yes, here's your <Money> cr, but let's hurry.
Quiet! What was that again, my dear Amiolis? Did you come up with it yet? Hurray! You got it, you got it!

Good, but why didn't you get rid of the hole altogether? I understand that it would be difficult to even stop it from growing now, but what is it really going to look like? It's a hole in the planet. Hold on a minute. I've got an idea. It's the only planet in the Galaxy that has a black hole smack in the middle! Think of the opportunities for tourism! We'll make a killing!
41.Special: Ranger, are you aware that some of the greatest scientists of our Galaxy were killed once you left them defenseless? This kind of poor professional judgment on your part makes us question the rationale for doing any additional business with you in the future. What if they died before they could transmit all the data necessary to pull the plug on the black hole? What would happen then? But anyway, I am not an analyst. Here's your <Money> cr. You have completed your mission in full. Goodbye!
Start: Ranger <Player>, what a great timing! Recently, faeyan scientists have selected our planet for a series of experiments with zero gravity black holes in oxygen-rich atmospheres and hard soils. Don't ask me, it's not like I know what that means. Better look out the window. Yes, that's exactly what I am talking about.

Overall, the experiment has been successful, at least on the surface of it, but once the fae left the location a minuscule black dot developed there that is now sucking in everything around it. The hole keeps growing and has now reached the size of a small town. We don't know what's inside the hole, but if you are curious you could try jumping right in. Oh, all right, don't go, that was a joke!

We desperately need that ship <Ship> with all those faeyan Einsteins aboard. We will pay you <Money> cr if you keep them safe for <Day> days. We are not going to last for much longer. If, on the other hand, the ship is destroyed...

Could you look it up in your search engine? If I remember it right, the fae did not say anything about leaving the <InStar> system any time soon, but one never knows... Hurry up then, what's all this beating around the bush about?

42.End: You came to get your money, <Player>, didn't you? Here is your <Money> cr. It's your good luck that we have made a contract, or you wouldn't have gotten any money at all. The thing is that the fearsome weapon has turned out to be a mundane microwave oven made by a modern maloq manufacturer. These microwave ovens are actively used by maloqs on many planets. Unfortunately, it may be quite difficult to tell a peaceful maloq machine from yet another new weapon they make.
42.Special: Hey, <Player>. You have lived up to your contractual obligations and earned your <Money> cr. Sad that it is, liner <Ship> is no more. Tragedy struck after your contract expired. Apparently, the fearsome new maloq weapon self-destructed and annihilated the liner. We can only hope now that it was the only copy of that device. I would also recommend that you do not land on any of the maloq planets. Having agreed to escort our ship, you challenged maloq security services, and they are not big on forgiving. So do yourself a favor: go to the pirate base right away and change your nationality. Your very survival may depend on it.
42.Start: The government of our planet is offering you a mission to escort the <FullShip>. Let me give you a brief run down: some time ago, a strange device was found on our planet, reportedly forgotten by some maloq or other. Our law enforcement sent the device to a lab right away. Upon a brief inspection, the device was determined to be a quasiexcitonic accelerator with an alternate frequency accelerator and an injector switch. It may sound a bit technical for someone from your species, I am afraid. Let me just tell you that this thing is extremely dangerous. It is even more worrisome that maloqs now have such a dangerous weapon at their disposal. The government has allocated a lot of money to ensure the device is thoroughly studied and protected properly. Maloqs are almost sure to want to cover their tracks. The study will continue for <Day> days, and if the <Ship> remains unharmed through that time, you will be paid <Money> cr -- a fairly large amount if you ask me.

43.End: Ranger <Player>, you have honorably completed your mission. Your professionalism would make any maloq green with envy. The agreed upon amount of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account. By the way, we are now recruiting crews for the ships of our newly built navy. Are you interested in a military career by any chance?
43.Special: This is the worst day ever for planet <FromPlanet>. The entire creme de la creme of the maloq race went to meet their maker. And you know what the worst of it is, ranger? The real tragedy is that the best of us have not perished in battle as every real maloq should, but rather kicked the bucket looking at those miserable doodlings. Still, you are going to receive your <Money> cr since you have completed your contract. However, you will not be able to leave here until you recall the identification markings of the scoundrel that has disgraced the government of our planet.
Start: How about a well-paid job, <Player>? Or better yet, how about <Money> cr? Even though a real ranger shall not concern himself with any miserable credits. The real important thing is to seek eternal glory. Be remembered as a true warrior! But anyway, I got carried away...

At the moment, the <FullShip> is hosting an exhibition of tattoos captured from various enemies of the maloq race. The huge collection on display includes tattoo designs by various species, including such exotic tribes as the akabos that dared to challenge our great and powerful maloq race. And how about that serial number and dominator emblem cut out of the hull of a downed terronoid urgant? It's one of the first sequential numbers of the entire series! I see that we understand each other well. In addition to the exhibits, the liner will host a great number of invited dignitaries, such as famous warriors, mercenaries, scalp hunters, retired military and other individuals that you need not concern yourself with.

This magnificent event may provoke quite a few objections from the fae and the gaals that will take exception to any exhibits made out of live body parts, or from pelengs that may want to engage in some secret activities ordered by God only knows who. And don't discount the possibility of some stray pirate eager to line his pockets with the loot from this liner. I hope you realize the responsibility entrusted to you here. The mission will last for <Day> days. You are hereby ordered to leave immediately.
The <Ship> has already left our planet. You can find its location at the information center for a couple of credits.

44.End: Great job, <Player>! Did you see the broadcast from the championship? Faeyan Antenia matched our best thinker Mo Roonie thought for thought almost until the finish line, but then he lost his marbles under stress, lost consciousness and quit. Our thinker won fair and square! Here's your <Money> cr.
Special: This is an absolute nightmare! <FromPlanet>'s reputation has been ruined forever. No, no, ranger, it wasn't your fault, it's not like you would have been able to do anything anyway. As far as we know, our great thinker Mo Roonie lost his temper and destroyed the ship with all those on board. Yes, I know that this is unworthy of the gaal race, but if I were him I would have done the same thing had I learned about the shenanigans of that faeyan swindler Antenia. Can you believe that the rascal attempted to prove the unprovable Gaussoff-Aaroff theorem in his head -- which is clearly against the championship rules!
Now, here's your <Money> cr, and please go away. Our entire planet is in mourning.
Start: Dear <Player>, we are glad to welcome you to our planet. If you are looking to make a buck and at the same time help promote spirituality and humanism, we'd be happy to offer you a contract. I see it in your eyes that you are interested. If not in serving the cause of humanism, then in making a buck for sure.

The thing is that our system is now hosting a cognothinking championship. The best thinkers of the Galaxy have come to compete in the championship. All the participants are now on board the <FullShip> where, closely monitored by precise measurement gauges, they are straining to think. He who can maintain his mental activity above a predetermined level longest will win. I hope you realize what a disturbance to such a championship all those external distractions or factors could cause -- such as pirate attacks, for example.
Should you be able to protect the <FullShip> from any pirate attacks until the championship ends on <Day>, we will pay you <Money> cr.

45.End: Excellent, <Player>! Thanks to you, not only did we manage to save the life of our poor Stupidarius, but we also picked up the trails of several RDF butchers and put them under surveillance. Here's your <Money> cr.
Special: Alas, ranger! The tormentors of our Degradation Fighters have finally caught up with the poor maloq. However, we have managed to arrest all the participants of that punitive expedition, and they are now singing like canaries giving up their co-conspirators.
Here's your <Money> cr. Sooner or later, we will pick the trail of top RDF honchos and make them sorry they have had the misfortune of being born.
Start: Good afternoon, <Player>, we are glad to see you. We have a mission for you that involves protecting a certain ship.

<Player>, you may have heard of the RDF -- Radical Degradation Fighters. This society is trying to improve primitive races by destroying their least intellectual specimen so that the dumb genes wouldn't be passed along.
