Just imagine, they are murdering intelligent creatures just because they are a little more slow-witted than their brethren.

We have learned that their next target, maloq Adyr Stupidarius, is traveling aboard the <FullShip>. As a kid, the poor guy was hit in the head with a maloq-made stool. We will not let the RDF henchmen destroy the poor wretch.
If you can keep <FullShip> safe for <Day> days, you will receive <Money> cr.

End: Great job, <Player>! Still, our experts were unable to make the patch compatible with the licensed version. But Biil Gaats wouldn't be the famous hotshot he is had he not been able to find his way out of tricky situations such as this one. He was smart enough to steal a pirated version of Nondows and release it as a legitimate one since it has no problem whatsoever downloading and installing patches.

Here's your <Money> cr. As to the licensed Nondows... Since that pirated version is now fully legit, what's the point of reinstalling? Good luck and make sure you only use certified and licensed software.
Special: Alas, ranger! Right after you left your post, some disgruntled user finally got through to <FullShip>. No, no, Biil is still alive, albeit in a coma, but as you could imagine the patch is now on hold.

You know, we've been thinking of declaring the pirated version of Nondows licensed and releasing it since it has no problem whatsoever downloading and installing patches. And you have honestly earned your <Money> cr. It isn't your fault that it has all come down to this... Good luck and make sure you only use certified and licensed software.
Start: Yes, we have something for your, <Player>! Tell me, what operating system do you use? I'll bet it's the latest version of Nondows, and a pirated one to boot.

Don't even bother trying to convince me this isn't so. First, as one of the publisher's employees I know it for a fact that you wouldn't be able to use this operating system without installing a patch. Second, you can only install the patch properly if you are using a pirated version of the software.

But we are already working on this issue. At the moment, Biil Gaats himself is testing a new patch to see if they could make it compatible with the licensed version. Testing is being conducted by a focus group of professional testers assembled aboard <FullShip>. I hope you understand that having Biil Gaats aboard makes the ship a tempting target for all kinds of lame buttheads that just don't seem to be able to make head or tail of our magnificent and convenient Nondows.

We would appreciate your help, ranger. Pretty, please! We will only need <Day> days to complete the testing, and if you can protect the <FullShip> through that time, you will not only receive <Money> cr, but also the most recent version of Nondows -- fully licensed and all patched up!

End: Excellent, <Player>! Our product has been successfully tested, and we already have an order for a shipment of new high durability hulls. We are even thinking of mass producing them. You have honestly earned your <Money> cr.
By the way, could we interest you in a high durability hull for your spaceship? We could give you a great deal on it.
Special: You heard about it, didntcha? Our <FullShip> did blow up, after all. Well, at least it happened after all the testing had been completed. To be sure, our clients from the <InStar> system pushed for an investigation, but it isn't for nothing that we have an entire gang of lawyers on staff. Otherwise, with the kind of engineers and designers we employ we would have lost our shirt on warranty service alone!
Here's your <Money> cr. By the way, could we interest you in a high durability hull for your spaceship? We could give you a great deal on it.
Start: Now, <Player>, how did you guess we could use some help and are willing to pay top dollar for it? Hey, they may have trained you rangers on purpose to sniff out lucrative deals, he-he. Maybe you could teach me too.

But let's get down to business! The thing is we have recently been contacted by some diplomat clients from the <InStar> system. Their diplomatic corps ordered a corps... I mean a hull from us, and-- What was that again?

Oh, the broken windows of heaven, ranger! That's some opinion you have of the pelengs! No, we are not talking murder at all! All they asked us for was a high security hull for their diplomatic spaceship. It looks like they are once again going to promote peace and education on some aggressive planet. To be sure, we have made them a hull, but what with the tight deadline and a limited budget... I am afraid it is not quite as durable as the clients expected.

At the moment, the clients are testing our product for durability in the <InStar> system. <Player>, if you could ensure <FullShip>'s safety for <Day> days, so that our hull would pass the test, we would pay you <Money> cr.

End: My congratulations, <Player>! Our social network is prospering, and it's all thanks to you. We already have several trillion registered members, only half of which are spambots! This is a smashing success!

Here's the <Money> cr we promised you. Moreover, <clr>Duckerberg<clrEnd> himself has promised you a thousand likes! Of course, you'll need to register on <clr>Pacebook 3000<clrEnd> before getting them. When you do, don't forget to poke me!
Special: My congratulations, <Player>! Our social network is prospering, and it's all thanks to you. We already have several trillion registered members, only half of which are spambots! This is a smashing success!

Sadly, soon after the completion of your mission, <clr>Duckerberg<clrEnd> perished in a tragic death. Rumor has it he was literally torn to pieces while giving a presentation by a rabid mob of fans. Fortunately, out social network has already taken off. You've earned this <Money> cr with honest work. When you find a minute, don't forget to register on <clr>Pacebook 3000<clrEnd> and like my new vacation pics.
Start: <Player>, be a friend and like my latest pics, won't you? You may consider it an official mission. Come on, how hard is it to like a pic? Pretty please!!! I'll like yours right back! Come on, don't be a butthole! If you don't like my pics, I'll steal all the cabbage from your farm! You have no idea what I'm talking about, do you? Figures, you rangers are a busy lot. I guess you don't have time for social sites. But we do! I mean, what else are we supposed to do at work nine through six, minus lunch? Anyway, this is about something else.

An eminent representative of our people, the great <clr>Duckerberg<clrEnd>, has recently misappropriated a new and highly promising social network from the fae, which they were planning on launching a few years from now. It is called <clr>Pacebook 3000<clrEnd>. The faeyan version started with an "f," but we're pelengs, so it all makes sense. Fortunately, the fae are still working on cleaning the software from glitches and bugs, so we can already start marketing the site all over the Galaxy.

Your mission is a simple one, <Player>: protect <clr>Duckerberg<clrEnd> as he travels aboard <Ship>, giving presentations on various planets. If he's still alive after <Day> days, we will reward you for a job well done with <Money> cr. He is currently in the <InStar> system.
Be vigilant! Our sources tell us that the fae might have hired lawyers, and those crooks won't let anything or anyone stand in their way!

End: I see that you've accomplished your mission, <Player>. Take your <Money> cr and try not to waste it on useless junk. Better yet, consider donating it to Developers of Dawn. It is by far the wisest investment you can make, for if our brotherhood collapses from lack of funds, the Galaxy shall be doomed to a quick and horrendous death.

Wondering what was so special about the ship you were protecting? Nothing, really. You see, it wasn't the ship the Secret Devs wanted to save, but you. It is for this reason that they (with our help, of course!) rewrote the book of your destiny. If you care to know, in the course of completing this quest you've successfully avoided three deaths from dominator ambushes, two asteroid crashes and one acute bout of indigestion. That's it, I've said too much already. And I'll remind you to keep mum about everything you've learned here, <Player>.
Special: I see that you've accomplished your mission, <Player>. Take your <Money> cr and try not to waste it on useless junk. Better yet, consider donating it to Developers of Dawn. It is by far the wisest investment you can make, for if our brotherhood collapses from lack of funds, the Galaxy shall be doomed to a quick and horrendous death.

Wondering what was so special about the ship you were protecting? Nothing, really. In fact, it was destroyed soon after your mission had ended, and the Galaxy is still standing. You see, it wasn't the ship the Secret Devs wanted to save, but you. It is for this reason that they (with our help, of course!) rewrote the book of your destiny. If you care to know, in the course of completing this quest you've successfully avoided three deaths from dominator ambushes, two asteroid crashes and one acute bout of indigestion. That's it, I've said too much already. And I'll remind you to keep mum about everything you've learned here, <Player>.
Start: <Player>, we have a special mission for you -- one that's of great importance for the whole universe. But first you must swear on this book of fairly mediocre poetry that you won't tell anyone about anything you've heard here. Do you swear? Very well. I'm confident that you'll keep your lips sealed.

Know that my brothers and I belong to a secret order, called Game Developers of Dawn. It is the order's mission to ensure this world follows the path of peace and prosperity and avoids the ruin of all living beings in the Galaxy. In the past our order was widely known, and our brothers widely esteemed for their knowledge of many secret technologies that could improve the world. Alas, today all this secret knowledge has been lost, and secret words like "assembler," "c plus plus," "html" and "java" have become meaningless, that is no one has any idea what they mean. Needless to say, we remain committed to guiding the Galaxy on the path of goodness and mercy. The TV in the brotherhood's secret living room is on day and night.

But you'd be wrong to think that we're completely helpless. Sometimes, when the stars in the sky alight just right, Secret Devs contact us and dictate their will! And we endeavor to implement their wishes to the best of our ability. It was the supreme knowledge of the Secret Devs that enabled us to emerge victorious in the klissan war, avoid the repeat of the Battle of Gralgar, and thwart the malicious krakorian invasion. What, you haven't heard anything about that last one? You have the Secret Devs to thank for that.

And now, let us get to the matter at hand. You, <Player>, have been chosen to be the vessel for priceless information. Don't worry, we don't mean that literally. Now listen and listen well. There is a ship called <Ship> in the <InStar> system. It is your duty to protect it for <Day> days, with your own life if need be, for on its safety rests the foundation of the entire Galaxy. Indeed, this ship represents the inviolability of faith, humanism and our innermost hopes at a bright future. Its demise will bring about holes in the time-space continuum that may prove to be the end of the universe as we know it... Don't look so nervous, <Player>!
If you're successful, you'll be richly rewarded with <Money> cr from the brotherhood's secret coffers. Now go, ranger, and remember that the fate of the Galaxy is in your hands.

5.End: Good job, <Player>! The exercise aboard the <Ship> went extremely well under your guard. Here is your <Money> cr. Very soon our boys will be able to work in space as well. All we need is another twenty or so such drills.
5.Special: Good morning, <Player>. Did you see this? What do you mean, "see what"? The pirates blew up the <FullShip>, the liner you were protecting. Oh, yes... The contract has expired by then. And not even a peep from those Red Hatchets! What kind of Red Hatchets are they anyway? Pfft! More like some wretched hatchlings... Now, you rangers are cast from a totally different mold. That's who they have to look up to! Truth be told though, it will not take us long to replace the losses suffered by this elite unit. There is no getting rid of potential candidates. And you have honestly earned your <Money> cr.
Start: The maloq <clr>Red Hatchets<clrEnd> are considered to be the best land crack troops in the Galaxy. Their stamina is much admired, even by rangers. They could crush a brick into powder in ten seconds flat. Their only weak spot is weapons skills in a vacuum. At the moment, the team is going through a zero gravity hand-to-hand combat course aboard the <FullShip>.
We cannot put the Red Hatchets at risk, so you are hereby ordered to provide escort security for the ship until <Date>. If you do well, we will pay you <Money> cr.

50.End: <Player>, many thanks for your invaluable work! The diva personally informed us that her flight had gone without a hitch, and we have to thank you for that. Of course, we do realize that your <Money> cr are more important to you than mere words, and that amount has already been transferred to your account. If some time in the future you fell like working with us again, you know where to find me. Thank you again.
Special: <Player>, can you imagine that our tour has come this close to ending in a catastrophe? Naturally, this isn't your fault at all. After your contract expired, ship <Ship> was destroyed by a group of radical fanatics. Thank God and all the saints, <clr>Xenia<clrEnd> was no longer on board by that time. At the moment, the diva is in rehab on one of the planets, recovering after these horrible tribulations. I hope she will feel well enough soon to continue her concert tour.

In any case, <Player>, many thanks for your invaluable service! The money has been transferred to your account. And remember, if some time in the future you fell like working with us again, you know where to find me. Thank you again.
Start: <Player>, what would you say if I offered you a show business job? You know, all those bright lights, camera flashes, perfect porcelain smiles of certified beauties... You dreamed about it, didn't you? I have a mission for you that could help you partake of this glamorous world. Step back for a moment and take a break from playing your usual hide and seek with death. Dominators are not going anywhere, and at the moment we need a real man who is not afraid of danger.

Intrigued? Ha-ha, I knew it. Famous human chanteuse <clr>Xenia Larionova<clrEnd> is currently visiting the <InStar> system. I am sure you have heard her songs before on numerous occasions. What do you mean you have not? How about "Good Meteorites" or "Dawn on the Orbit"? They have been popular hits on Coalition 1 Radio forever. And her most famous hit is... Come on, you can remember it! We will follow the sun to wherever it's going, to discover what's its name... No? You haven't heard it?  Well, apparently it's true what they say about you rangers, that most of you are very narrow-minded individuals. All right, all right, don't take it to heart. Still, one should know about such things.

Today is the diva's last show before she goes on a grand galactic tour aboard <Ship>. We propose that you accompany her as her bodyguard to protect her from any possible unpleasantness during her space voyage. Like pirates or some crazy fans. You don't need to be present during her shows, there will be other security for that.

If you agree, we will pay you <Money> cr at the end of your contract, i. e. in <Day> days. And remember, ranger, you will be protecting an all-Galaxy star. This is not at all like squeezing some wretched merchants for a few bucks. This is serious.

End: Thank you for completing the mission, <Player>. The classic animation proved irresistible to modern audiences! Millionaires and billionaires alike are lining up to fund our work. With their money, not only will I be able to hire additional staff and purchase top-of-the-line equipment for them to work with, I reckon I can spend at least a year relaxing at a luxury resort!
Oh, right! I almost forgot. Here's your <Money> cr. A deal is a deal. Have a pleasant day, <Player>!
Special: Nice work, <Player>! The classic animation proved irresistible to modern audiences! Millionaires and billionaires alike are lining up to fund our work. With their money, not only will I be able to hire additional staff and purchase top-of-the-line equipment for them to work with, I reckon I can spend at least a year relaxing at a luxury resort!

Unfortunately, several minutes ago I was informed that the file with the cartoon contained a terrible virus that promptly took control of the transmitting ship. The suddenly dangerous liner had to be swiftly neutralized.
In anticipation of your next question, rest assured that the staff was evacuated in time. Also, thankfully, the ship was insured. So, that's where we stand...
Oh, right! I almost forgot. Here's your <Money> cr. A deal is a deal. Have a pleasant day, <Player>!
Start: Hey, <Player>, do you like dogs? And no, I'm not asking you about Korean food. What about cats? My, that's a curious answer. Puzzling, to be perfectly frank, but anyway... Let's cut to the chase.

About a month ago our wonderful archaeologists were able to excavate a secret information storage that held one-of-a-kind visual art samples from the early XXI century. Just imagine, a massive archive of files with movies and music enjoyed by our ancestors! Never mind the separate block of data that may store secret information from those times.

Sadly, the recovered records are in such awful condition that it will take much time and effort to restore them. Sadder still, the financial department has denied our request to allocate funds for this noble cause, advising us to appeal to patrons of art and history instead. This is all in spite of the fact that our specialists have already managed to restore one of the files -- a cartoon about a mischievous cat who loves a curious dish called la-sa-gna.

Watching the cartoon only reinforced my belief that such beauty mustn't be lost in the mist of ages. I used my personal funds to hire a ship named <Ship> to tour the nearest planets, screening the cartoon to the local audiences. My hope is that someone with enough money or connections will get hooked on the content and help finance this project. As for you, I want to task you with guarding <Ship> for exactly <Day> days, which is how long the tour is going to take. If you're successful, you will earn <Money> cr -- the last of my savings. So, what do you say?

End: You've done well, <Player>! The new teaching is gaining momentum. We're seeing the number of converts grow with each passing day. Curiously enough, we get far more requests from folks wanting to administer the treatment than be on the receiving end of it. What about you -- how would you like to be treated with the wonder-working boot? You wouldn't? You know, something tells me I wouldn't either...
How about your fee? Now that answer is no surprise. Take your well-earned <Money> cr, and may the wonder-working boot be with you!
Special: That was pretty good, <Player>! Of course, it's quite the pity that <Ship> was destroyed soon after your mission was completed. On the plus side, this tragedy caused the popularity of the new teaching to soar through the roof. We're seeing the number of converts grow with each passing day. Curiously enough, we get far more requests from folks wanting to administer the treatment than be on the receiving end of it. What about you -- how would you like to be treated with the wonder-working boot? You wouldn't? You know, something tells me I wouldn't either...
How about your fee? Now that answer is no surprise. Take your well-earned <Money> cr, and may the wonder-working boot be with you!
Start: <Player>, what do you know about the "temple of the wonder-working boot"? Don't bother raking your memory -- it is a brand new gaalian teaching, proselytizing physical impact with the giver's lower extremity against the posterior of the blessing receiver's gyroscopic center.

Having studied this phenomenon, our scientists have concluded that this method is legit and actually quite effective. Upon receiving the wonder-working boot, the test subjects were sufficiently motivated to will themselves into performing work that they would never have agreed to prior to treatment. Now it is up to us, as the main proponents of this cosmic truth, to disseminate this teaching to all the other worlds. We've already hired a ship with which to perform this holy work, but we didn't anticipate one problem.

You see, the Universe is filled with individuals who are stuck at very primitive levels of development. Their aggressive behavior in particular can put the entire mission at risk. In light of this, we would like to propose that you see to the security of <Ship> for the next <Day> days. If you manage, you will earn <Money> cr, as well as the exclusive right to receive the treatment of the wonder-working boot out of turn, but no more than once per month. How does that sound?

End: Ah, there you are, <Player>! We've been waiting on you. I'm happy to tell you that Mr. L's testimony has led us straight to Limp! By the way, would you mind showing us your leg... Not that it matters! You see, this crucial testimony has revealed that Limp's true identify is that of <Player> -- a familiar name, is it not? Security, escort this ranger to his cell! Check that, wait a moment while I read this medical report that just came in... "The subject referred to as Mr. L suffers from numerous psychological disorders, causing him to foam at the mouth and spew utter nonsense." After an evaluation like that, this testimony ain't worth a dented penny.
Security, release the ranger! Dear <Player>, we hope that you will forgive us this small misunderstanding. And please accept this fee of <Money> cr as thanks for your efforts.
53.Special: Ah, there you are, <Player>! We've been waiting on you. I'm overjoyed to tell you that, after Mr. L's testimony, we can now unequivocally say that you, <Player>, are definitely not Limp! You knew this all along, but we weren't sure until now. It's a pity poor Mr. L bought the farm without ever learning the truth. Did you notice how he shrank from you? Clearly he suspected you were the culprit. At any rate, you upheld your end of the deal and earned your fee of <Money> cr. Please sign here and initial there.
Start: <Player>, have you heard about the maniac blowing up spaceships nicknamed Limp?

We've got hundreds of criminal suits against this fella, but nobody can give us accurate intel about him -- everybody's paranoid that the nut will pick them as his next target. Just the other day we've finally managed to track down a witness -- let's call him Mr. L -- who's willing to tell us what he knows in exchange for protective custody. Your mission, <Player>, should you choose to accept it, is to guard this crucial witness in the case of the People of Planet <FromPlanet> v. Limp for the next <Day> days. Mr. L is currently aboard <Ship>. If successful, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr.

54.End: Good to see you, ranger! Your reward of <Money> cr has been collecting dust. Our national hero was so overwhelmed with gratitude that he autographed every single bill of your compensation. Unfortunately, our Ministry of Culture immediately confiscated the money as national treasures, so we're forced to pay you with regular credits. But don't worry, we're already planning the next event for our two qillionth citizen! Who knows, you might get luckier with that one.
54.Special: Good to see you, ranger! Your reward of <Money> cr has been collecting dust. Our hero Dron was unable to take part in the award ceremony for a totally legitimate reason. Thankfully, we had a plan B and used his double instead. To keep things authentic, the double put Dron's autograph on every single bill of your compensation. Unfortunately, our Ministry of Culture immediately confiscated the money as national treasures, so we're forced to pay you with regular credits. But don't worry, we're already planning the next event for our two qillionth citizen! Who knows, you might get luckier with that one.
54.Start: Dear <Player>, do you know where the happiest humanoids in the universe happen to live? No, not in penthouses -- you're thinking way too narrowly. According to the latest findings of our Statistics Committee, the population of planet <FromPlanet> is hands down the happiest in the universe. Just recently, as part of the HIP (Happiness Improvement Program) initiative, a decree was passed to award a large financial prize to our planet's qillionth citizen. The lucky sun of a gun ended up being one Dron Bellyach, captain of <Ship>. In addition to his prize, Dron will be granted the honor of giving a live interview in prime time, featured in a weight loss commercial, and selected as a participant in several reality shows, such as Who Wants to Be a Legionnaire?, Very Big Brother, Fix Factor, and others. The contracts are all but signed, a heck of a lot is riding on this, and we cannot afford any snafus. That is why you, <Player>, must provide security services for Dron until his award ceremony, which is scheduled for <Date>. Provided that planet <FromPlanet> gets to see its hero safe and sound at the end of this term, your account balance will increase by <Money> cr.

55.End: Hmm... The furniture zoologist resolved the problem in the simplest and most original way possible: by popularizing furniture cooking among pelengs on planet Rakhish. Moreover, he made quite a bit of money on his bestseller "Dining On What You Sit On." In any event, the planet has been saved from the inflow of amphibian water heaters and carnivorous desks; and you'll get your <Money> cr.
Special: Alas, our furniture zoologist died during your mission -- he was squashed by cargo that had fallen from a komodo shelf...
But this happened after your contract had expired, so, Ranger <Player>, you officially completed your mission and we're obligated to pay you your fee of <Money> cr.
Start: <Player>, have you heard the latest news? There's an ecological catastrophe on planet Rakhish! It was caused by rash experiments with various species of genetically modified amphibians and reptiles. As is known, the pelengs are famous for their unimaginable avarice... And it moved them to implement the most absurd idea -- to create new animal species by making them like... furniture and home appliances! Yep, that how we got the frogvisors, viperpots, recordodiles, and an armchair with hips. Breeding these so-called animals lightened the burden on planet Rakhish's consumer goods industry, but everything got out of control when the half-beast, half-appliance creatures began multiplying too quickly and escaped the factories into wild swamps and flatlands. Then entire prides of cooking implements began to form, along with flocks of audio- and video equipment and herds of beds. Fortunately, a scientist was found who calls himself a furniture zoologist, who says he knows how to regulate the population of these specialized creatures of the pelengs.
The furniture zoologist is working aboard the ship <FullShip>. Your mission is to ensure its safety for <Day> days. Accompany it and we will reward you.

56.End: Excellent job, <Player>! Our genius is safe, and he's rumored to be working on some updates for our favorite social network. We'll be able to do surveys to pick the most popular pirate and grab money from the accounts of those dupes who didn't take enough care to get high-level security for them!
Special: Excellent job, <Player>! Our genius is safe, and he's rumored to be working on some updates for our favorite social network. We'll be able to do surveys to pick the most popular pirate and grab money from the accounts of those dupes who didn't take enough care to get high-level security for them!

By the way, the <FullShip> was brought down all the same, but by then <clr>Zackerburg<clrEnd> had managed to settle on one of the planets that the liner was passing by. Now those military guys are probably gonna commit suicide, since we've provided all of the main news channels with the information that they brought down a civilian ship! I think that's worth celebrating, <Player>. Take your <Money> cr. and have fun till you drop!
Start: Seems like we can trust you, <Player>, can't we? You have honor and respect among the pirates. We've got a job for you. The Peleng <clr>Zackerburg<clrEnd>, a distinguished representative of our race, has created the newest and most innovative social network for pirates. It's almost the same as that interstellar network called Phazebook, only cooler, since bosses can ban newbies and it's got lots of gambling applications. Anyways, not so long ago he was having a rest on his personal ship in the <InStar> star system when he accidentally ran into some warship along his way. It was coming back to the hangar of its native planet after a fierce battle, and the collision was fatal to the ship. <clr>Zackerburg<clrEnd> was seized, and they wanted to try him in court and imprison him, but our people got him out of the lockup and put him aboard a passenger ship called <Ship>.

The colleagues of the slain military bigwig are burning for revenge, but they can't dispose of him themselves, since that would leave an indelible mark on their reputation. However, they are able to hire someone who could secretly destroy the ship with <clr>Zackerburg<clrEnd> aboard. That's why we're asking you, <Player>, as an exemplary bad guy who firmly believes in the ideals of piracy, to guard the ship with our genius aboard for <Day> days until he finds a peaceful planet where he can hide and sit on the fence while living in luxury and denying himself nothing. If you do us this favor, you'll get <Money> cr.

57.End: While you were working, <Player>, <clr>Lyakusha Cepelis & Partners<clrEnd> went to the dogs. They got into an awful, awkward situation where one of the pirates working for them failed to keep himself from robbing the ship that he was guarding. Don't worry about getting paid for your efforts: the money has already been transferred to your account. The Lyakusha Cepelis himself singled you out as an honest employee in his last interview.
57.Special: While you were working, <Player>, <clr>Lyakusha Cepelis & Partners<clrEnd> went to the dogs. They got into an awful, awkward situation where one of the pirates working for them failed to keep himself from robbing the ship that he was guarding. Don't worry about getting paid for your efforts: the money has already been transferred to your account. The Lyakusha Cepelis himself singled you out as an honest employee in his last interview. Of course the journos fought, yelling that the <FullShip> that you had guarded had been brought down. But we were able to prove that that occurred after your contract had ended, so your black pirate reputation never suffered.
Start: I got a job for you, <Player>. The pirate cause is continually growing throughout the galaxy. Now we have the first pirate security company, called <clr> "Lyakusha Cepelis & Partners"<clrEnd>. Right now they're running a promotional event: Cepelis himself opens the Register of Civilian Vessels and pokes his finger into it without looking. The ship that he selects this way is provided with free services for a time.

The problem is that right now they don't have any available ships during the promo event, and the ship <Ship> needs security. That's why they asked me to find a respectable person to perform the security mission. You suit them quite well, so if your desire to moonlight a little bit more hasn't gone out yet, I'm asking you to fly to the <InStar> star system and guard the <Ship> from every possible threat until <Date>. The company's reputation is at stake, so if you're successful, be ready to see <Money> cr. added to your account.

End: <Player>, something irreparable has happened. The killer never appeared to attack the ship, and not because you scared it off but because there was no mother of our future leader aboard that ship! It turns out that those damned steel bastards sent a cyborg thirty years back into the past and managed to zap the leader's granny before she even gave birth to his mother! Now we all are doomed, and there's no hope for salvation.

You gave us no cause for complaint, though. You did your work well, and the money you've earned has already been transferred to your account. Now go to a bar and please drink to the salvation of our sinful souls.
Special: <Player>, something irreparable has happened. The killer never appeared to attack the ship, and not because you scared it off but because there was no mother of our future leader aboard that ship! It turns out that those damned steel bastards sent a cyborg thirty years back into the past and managed to zap the leader's granny before she even gave birth to his mother! Now we all are doomed, and there's no hope for salvation.

You gave us no cause for complaint, though. You did your work well, and the money you've earned has already been transferred to your account. Of course the ship that you were guarding was brought down in the end, but what does that matter now? Don't sweat it; just go to the bar and please drink to the salvation of our sinful souls.
Start: Let it be known to you, <Player>, that organic races are on the verge of extinction, even though it doesn't look like that from an outsider's viewpoint. The rise of the machines predicted by the prophet Mara Horror already happened, and soon all inhabited planets of our branch of the galaxy will turn into lifeless, radioactive blocks of rock or begin to boil like the huge cauldrons on Judgment Day, and the pitiful remnants of the races of the former Coalition will hide underground wherever possible and carry on an imbalanced struggle against the soulless robots. The temporary successes in our struggle against the Dominators must not confuse you, since it's all nothing more than a part of their cunning plan.

Fortunately, we'll have a charismatic leader in the future, one who will unite all organic creatures able to hold a rifle with their extremities (and able to know which end it shoots from) to fight the machines. He hasn't been born yet, but his mother is currently aboard the ship called <Ship>, which is flying through the <InStar> star system. The insidious machines used a future technology to send a specially trained, ruthless killer cyborg to our time to zap the mother of our future leader before he was even born.

It doesn't matter if you're a pirate, a fighter, or a despicable huckstering merchant: your most important mission, just like that of all of us, is to protect our future! So get to your hangar quickly and fly off to save the <Ship>! This mission ends on <Date>, since then, according to the information we have, the killer cyborg's charge will run down and it will self-destruct. If you're successful, you'll get <Money> cr., in addition to moral satisfaction and praise from everyone as a hero!

6.End: Ranger <Player>, you have saved the life of a witness. It is very noble of your indeed. What is important is to make sure he lives until the investigation is over. Here is <Money> cr for your troubles.
6.Special: Good morning, <Player>, you have really aced your mission! Of course, we are aware that <FullShip> was subsequently destroyed, but that's how our special services wanted it to begin with. Let me share a little secret with you: this is how we identify information leaks. It looks like someone within our organization is working for the criminals, and with your help we are about to pick up he traitor's trail. By the way, here is your <Money> cr.
Start: In case you are still wondering, we maloqs have adopted that human idea for a witness protection program in our own police work. Now, listen to this. There was this maloq guy exercising in a park near the gaalian embassy. Then all of a sudden here's their ambassador falling out of a window. Oh, and there is a hatchet stuck in the poor bugger's back. And right after that, a maloq in pink jumps out. He strikes the ambassador once again in the head with a hatchet -- just to make sure, I guess -- and takes off.

Now, our witness saw it all and will be able to identify the assassin. The witness is now traveling aboard the <Ship> -- a specially equipped police transport. Your orders are to to guard that ship until <Date>. If you do a good job of it, we will pay you <Money> cr for your troubles.

7.End: Good job <Player>, good job! Our plan proved to be such a great success that we are now going to lease this bait ship out to the neighboring systems that are also crawling with pirates. Hey, we may even get a buck or two out of it. We could also recommend you to them as the only experienced specialist in the Galaxy who had already mastered the new method. Here is your well-deserved <Money> cr.
7.Special: Ah, come on in, <Player>, come on in! Don't be shy. Here's the <Money> cr we promised you. That's for your help defending and then destroying <FullShip>. Yes, you heard me right. The ship is gone, and you are getting paid... Truth be told, we first wanted to withhold your bonus, but then our managers had those ragobam bullfrogs talk some sense into the neighboring system's government from whom we had leased that wretched ship. There's very little a few cups of good old mulled wine wouldn't be able to do, so we redrafted the lease as a scrap metal recycling agreement. In the end, we even made a few bucks on the deal. Next time you are passing by feel free to drop right in.
Start: Ranger <Player>, how would you like to make <Money> cr? No? Not interested? Or are you? We have these wicked pirates that have adopted our system for a home and are now a major nuisance for the through merchant traffic. It wouldn't be so bad if there weren't so many of these buggers around. As it is, our system has been unofficially named the most dangerous in this sector. This just isn't good. No, not good at all.

So we came up with a trick: we are going to use the <FullShip> as bait, ostensibly loaded to the brim with real treasure. The pirates will bite and come rushing in, and we'll have us a duck shoot. So this is the plan we have for you for the next <Day> days. But remember -- the ship must remain intact since we leased it from a neighboring system.

End: Thank you, <Player>! You did a great job protecting the <Ship> and thus it could deliver mulled wine to several planets where they had never tasted it before. We have received plenty of thank you notes.

And here's the <Money> cr you were craving! Here it is, all yours. Enjoy! Make sure you visit our gamma-bar. where the air is filled with the intoxicating aroma of chakhara and the exciting scent of beautiful peleng dancers.
8.Special: Hey, Ranger <Player>, long time no see! Where have you been all this time? And what's that nice smell coming from you? You found that famous mulled wine, didn't you? Now thanks to you and that advertising agent of ours, God rest his soul, it is known all over the Galaxy as the best premium mulled wine of all times. We have installed a hidden wireless kinetomatrix camera aboard the <Ship> -- one of the latest Dzuhallag models by the way, very long range -- and shot us a first rate commercial. The tag line is "Sacrificing Your Life Ain't Worth Mulling Over -- Not With This Kind of Mulled Wine!" And here's your bonus of <Money> cr. We are business partners, aren't we?
Start: So, Ranger <Player>, do you like this signature mulled wine that we make here on this planet -- and nowhere else? Do you like it or not? Tell me. For a gaal, this mulled wine is a great source of joy, and humans find it to be very nutritious. A number of other species have also expressed quite a bit of interest in its beneficial qualities.

We hired ranger ship <Ship> to make a promotional tour and bring this drink to other planets. The job we are offering you is escorting the ship for protection. Easy money, if you ask me. A nice sum of <Money> cr is sure to find its way into your pocket if this ranger with his load of mulled wine stays alive and kicking until <Date>.

9.End: Wonderful, just wonderful! We were right betting on our own guy aboard the <Ship>. Now the maloqs owe us a nice chunk of cash, part of which -- <Money> cr -- is yours.
9.Special: Damn it! A thousand dead Pkhedok leaches on a dead man's chest! Sorry, ranger, that wasn't for you. You actually did a great job protecting the <FullShip> and even graced billions of TV screens all over the Galaxy in your capacity as a rising show business star. This is what we are going to pay you <Money> cr for. What concerns the <FullShip>'s pilot though, we'd penalize him for being so greedy if we could. Unfortunately, he died while we were shooting the second installment of the TV series. Cocky bastard, he simply got careless under your vigilant tutelage. Served him right, didn't it, <Player>? By the way, would you be interested in starring in that show as one of the victims so to speak... I mean lead characters? No? Well, let me know if you change your mind.
9.Start: It's terrible, <Player>! Our <FullShip> went for a quick buck taking part -- as a victim! -- in Kill or Lose, a cruel reality show staged for real in open space. Of course we will try to protect the poor wretch. That's what we want to hire you for. Be so kind and make sure the <Ship> remains in one piece for the next <Day> days -- that's when the show ends. We are offering a very generous reward -- <Money> cr. Yes, I kid you not!

DefShip.AddText: On behalf of the advertisers: the search service in the information center is only <clr>3<clrEnd> cr!

0.End: Good job! Thanks to you the general will keep his straps and was even promised a bonus. And you will receive the promised <Money> cr. And no arguing, these are the old officer's personal savings!
Start: Ten-shun! I am speaking on behalf of Brigadier General <clr>Berk Mandopolis<clrEnd>, who is responsible for the military detachments in the <FromStar> system. Just recently the Supreme Command staged a raid codenamed "Werewolf-Generals." In the course of the raid it was revealed that the general took bribes and did more to further the bandits' interests than those of his homeland. And that's after 50 years of loyal service on planet <FromPlanet>!

The general claims he was set up! To prove this, he wants to demonstrate that the system entrusted to him operates without flaw. Basically, the general will pay you a total of <Money> cr from his personal savings for ensuring security in the system until <Date>. The general believes in you, do not fail his trust! Execute!

1.End: Ah, there you are, <Player>! You fought like a couple of red-bellied wimps! I was watching you and remembering my father, who could engage a dozen pirate ships and rout them in no time. Now that was tenacity and heroism! Not a sissy like you. Oh yeah, don't forget to upgrade your weapons with your fee of <Money> cr.
1.Start: If you're asking, it means you're ready for a task of any difficulty! Very commendable, indeed! Our <FromStar> system has been hit by disastrous space tornadoes. They cloaked the planet and the satellites that were in its orbit at the time. Needless to say, all the military ships on the orbit are now in dire need of repairs. But it's still war out there! I order you to declare war on the pirates of this system on behalf of all maloqs. If you make sure that no civilian vessel gets destroyed in our system from now through <Date>, you will be named the hero of planet <FromPlanet>! And they will even pay you <Money> cr!

10.End: Erm... Excellent work, <Player>, you are an amazing fighter. Take your fee of <Money> cr for protecting the <FromStar> system from pirates. This year's harvest of frunties has been safely delivered to our clients. Now they will just have to cook them right: add some swamp spices and put 'em to ferment for several weeks in bochokhashas till total oxidization. Peleng kvass is always high class!
Start: Ranger <Player>, we have an urgent task for capable individual such as yourself. We have just harvested a crop of frunties for export. You don't have anything against fruit, I hope? Good, because the local pirates are long-time cronies for the Carnivore Coalition, and every year they aim to destroy our transports carrying fruit crops. They're ruthless, even shooting down liners carrying agronomists!

Normally, we have to the utmost respect for the pirate trade, but in this particular case a crop of valuable fruits trumps good relations with our pirate neighbors. And this season we need especially reliable guards escorting the transports. So then, if no civilian transport falls casualty in this system through <Date>, we will make it worth your while -- you have my word as a peleng! What? You want to know how much, exactly? Oh, umm... As much as <Money> cr! That should be sufficient, yes?

End: Excellent, <Player>, a real fine job! With you by our side, the situation in our system was calm and peaceful. Please accept this fee of <Money> cr as a reward for your fearsome reputation.

Although, truth be told, you overdid it a bit. Next time try to be a bit more gentle with the pirates; after all, they are still respected members of our society! On the other hand, any pirate who's unable to defend himself isn't really a pirate but a sorry excuse for one... All in all, I'd say your methods have been fully justified. The pirate community should be thanking us for cleansing their ranks of such mopes! Only the strong and the cunning must survive.
Start: Ranger <Player>, feel like making <Money> cr? We have received alarming news: several mob clans are congregating in our system with plans to conquer it and divide the spoils; in other words, we're about to see an all-out gang war. Sure, this information may be false, but what if it's not? We're always being accused of neglecting our system's security.

So here's an excellent opportunity for you to cut a quick buck, or <Money> cr, to be precise. Ensure the security of all civilian ships in this system for the next <Day> days, and this money is yours, pilot!

12.End: You, <Player>, have earned a reputation of a top-class combat pilot. The entire <FromStar> system enjoyed <Day> days of peace and prosperity, and we owe it all to you. A sum of <Money> cr has been transferred to your personal account. Please, check your balance.
Start: We are planning on opening a new business center in our system, and are expecting the arrival of investors, sponsors, journalists and other interested parties. In order to avoid any unpleasant incidents at the project's launch, security in the <FromStar> system must be increased.
You are invited to assume combat duty and guard all civilian ships in the system for the next <Day> days. If you're successful, your fee will be <Money> cr.

13.End: Thankfully, the Rotfather ended up choosing a neighboring system to set his "record" in. And it appears that he was successful. I want to emphasize that his success came in no small part because our neighbors didn't have a valiant protector like you, <Player>. At any rate, you have fulfilled your end of the contract; in turn, we've already transferred <Money> cr into your account.
Start: I've always known that pirates were showboats, but it's amazing how far they're willing to go! One of the mob bosses named the Rotfather has decided to set a record for ships shot down in space! What is more, he's recording it all so as to get into the Briggs Book of World Records. Our intel says he might set his sights on our system, terrorizing all passing transport and passenger vessels. The entire <FromStar> community is exasperated with such a display of cynicism from the underworld!

<Player>, we propose that you get involved and support out armed forces in repulsing these vile attacks. Make sure that no civilian ships get taken down for <Day> days in our system, and you will be compensated <Money> cr upon your return.

14.End: On behalf of the <FromPlanet> government and myself personally I would like to congratulate you on the successful completion of your combat patrol mission! A total of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account in accordance with contract terms.
Start: Ranger <Player>, sad as it is, due to the unending war with the dominators the <FromStar> system is virtually bereft of soldiers capable of wielding a weapon. Only women and children are left. We have no other choice but to ask independent pilots to join the defense operations in this system.

Your fee will total <Money> cr if no civilian ship is shot down in this system over the next <Day> days. Time is of the essence, so we ask that you make your decision swiftly. Civilian vessels require assistance here and now!

15.End: Dear <Player>! On behalf of the <FromPlanet> government, I would like to extend our sincerest gratitude! Please accept this reward of <Money> cr for your assistance to our law enforcement.
Start: For your information, <Player>, customs fees in the <FromStar> system were recently reduced. As a result, there has been a sharp increase of interplanetary cargo transport, which pleases us greatly. However, the equally sharp rise in space crime we find far less pleasing.

We are prepared to pay you a total of <Money> cr for your assistance in fighting crime alongside our orbital forces over the next <Day> days. We will deem the terms of your contract completed if no civilian ship in the system becomes a pirate casualty throughout this period.

16.End: Congratulations on the successful completion of your patrol mission! The <FromPlanet> government has transferred a fee of <Money> cr to your account. Good luck in your future endeavors!
Start: Would you like to score a contract? Well, in accordance with the military doctrine of planet <FromPlanet>, only independent pilots with a license to operate a combat vessel are allowed to undertake space patrol missions.

Your license checks out, which means we can offer you the job. Essentially, your objective is ensuring security of flights in this system until <Date>. If no civilian death is registered over the time of the contract, our government will pay you a fee of <Money> cr.

17.End: Dear <Player>, you have lived up to 79% of our expectations concerning your patrolling! Judging by your exemplary work, the <clr>Rangers on Guard<clrEnd> project appears to be quite promising. A fee of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account.
Start: Ranger <Player>, you have been given the great honor and privilege of patrolling the <FromStar> system as part of the <clr>Rangers on Guard<clrEnd> project. The decision to trust rangers with the security of our system came as a result of a 14-hour comprehensive analysis by the Supreme Chamber of planet <FromPlanet>. The vacancy is now open to all interested rangers.

Please concentrate all your mental faculties on making sure that our server receives no reports on the demise of civilian ships in our system until <Date>, whereupon a fee of <Money> cr will be transferred to your account without delay.

18.End: Unfortunately, our information services were mistaken. As it turns out, Amalcus Pheophane never did escape from his prison. Rather, he simply led an armed assault on the prison cafeteria. Due to the ensuing chaos, the local news networks interpreted the developments as a full-on escape, and so the story spread across the communication channels. At any rate, you have completed the terms of the contract in full, so we'll be transferring a sum of <Money> cr to your account.
Start: Ranger <Player>, mobilize your analytical facilities to assess the following situation. Two years ago one <clr>Amalcus Pheophane<clrEnd>, a category II criminal, was exiled to one of the penitentiary planets unbefitting a faeyan intellectual. We have received reports that he has escaped and is on his way here with vengeance in mind.

If our sources are correct, flight security in our system may drop by a whopping 38-44%. The risk is too high to ignore, so we've allocated additional funds in the amount of <Money> cr in the interest of flight security. These funds will be transferred to your account if no civilian ship casualties are recorded within the confines of this system in the next <Day> days.

End: Ranger <Player>, you have brilliantly coped with the mission imposed upon you, for no faeyan dog owner in the <FromStar> system has been harmed!
We are transferring the agreed upon sum of <Money> cr to your account; moreover, for a nominal fee we can help you upgrade your own pet!
Start: Dear <Player>, recently several clans of faeyan intellectuals from planet <FromPlanet> have taken interest in a typically human hobby of cynology. In layman's terms, they have become dog owners. Their efforts have resulted in the first faeyan cyberdog breed, dubbed Faeterrier. Unlike its human counterpart, it comes with a built-in neuron processor, capable of carrying out ten billion operations per second. Seeking to demonstrate this new breed and network with colleagues from other planets, the Faeyan Dog Owners' Club has announced the <clr>First Faeyan Cyberdog Festival<clrEnd>.

With all the guests invited to the festival, the club now wishes to bolster flight security in the <FromStar> system. It was decided that a sum of <Money> cr shall be paid to the ranger who can ensure the security of civilian ships for the next <Day> days.

2.End: That was a blast! With heroes like you the <FromPlanet> system is protected 27 hours a day! Here's your <Money> cr. Be sure to come visit <FromPlanet> more often. Maloqs love our heroes.
2.Start: Would you like to receive an order, <Player>? We maloqs know that everybody needs medals, even rangers! And we also know that rangers need money. To that point, if no civilian ship is killed in our <FromStar> system through <Date>, you will be awarded both! Now go and sow murder and mayhem!

End: You have ensured total security within the confines of the entire <FromStar> system, which logically resulted in your account being credited <Money> cr.

What was that? You're wondering what happened to the aforementioned wonders of faeyan technology? Isn't that obvious? For security purposes they were cloaked by Z-shields, providing full invisibility in the standard visual spectrum. Special Z-glasses were required to watch the parade, which were issued to authorized spectators. Forgive me for not providing you with a pair. The probability of a faeyan forgetting something is truly negligible, but that's exactly what happened here.
Start: Dear <Player>, our system will soon be holding the annual parade of technologically superior vessels, as designed by top faeyan technocrats. The parade will feature exclusively experimental ship models, too complex and conceptualized to be used for everyday operations.

At any rate, the <FromStar> system will be instituting additional security measures, and we propose that you, a licensed free pilot, head up this effort. The condition is simple: no civilian ship can be destroyed in the system through <Date>. If you fulfill this condition, you will be paid a sum of <Money> cr. Furthermore, you will get the unique chance to behold a new generation of experimental spacecrafts, which are the pinnacle of faeyan technological advancement.

21.End: Congratulations, <Player>! Thanks to your efforts, <FromStar> now enjoys the reputation of a safe system. We are crediting your account with <Money> cr. Additionally, please be advised that the <clr>Ioshu Buyaro Theater Company<clrEnd> will be demonstrating their unique art to the faeyan public when the next galactic theater season rolls around.
Start: Earlier today on planet <FromPlanet> there was a performance of an elite gaalian <clr>Ioshu Buyaro Theater Company<clrEnd>. The company is distinct in that its stage and all performance props don't actually exist in real life, but are projected directly into the audience's consciousness on an astral-mental plane. At least that's what they claim. A more sober outlook on things would suggest that they're using next generation holographic projectors. Our scientists forecast the production of similar machines in the next few years.

Anyway, let us get down to the matter at hand. Now that the performance has ended, many of the Galaxy's celebrities will be departing from planet <FromPlanet>. In light of this fact, we must implement heightened security measures -- not only in the planet's immediate vicinity, but ideally throughout the entire <FromStar> system. This will be your mission. Each ship cruising through the system is to be under your protection. If all the ships are ensured safe passage over the next <Day> days, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr from our cultural fund.

End: Sit, err... I mean lie!... Forgive me, I'm getting all mixed up with these animal commands. It's high time their software got upgraded.

Dear Ranger <Player>. You have successfully accomplished your mission, and we are happy to pay you <Money> cr. And if you have pets of your own, make sure to give them to us. With our chip integrated in them, they'll become 300% smarter. Impressed? That's nothing compared to some of our other breakthroughs, but a matter of pride just the same!
Start: <Player>, our system is generally considered fairly quiet and peaceful, which is why zero gravity animal acts are held here regularly. However, there's been a leak in the mass media that a group of pirates is planning a series of attacks on ships in our system. The reason for this is that a number of wealthy peleng and human private collectors are willing to shell out large sums of money for the right to own our wonderful modified creatures, namely their hides, horns and neurochips, so as to hang them on the wall for decorative purposes. I trust you're with me when I say that their heinous plans must be foiled!
Our mission for you is to protect all civilian ships in the system through <Date>. A fee of <Money> cr shall be paid to you from the Cyber-Animals Incentive Fund at the term's completion.

End: Dear <Player>, you have accomplished your patrol mission. A sum of <Money> cr has been transferred to your account.

Should you be curious to learn more information on this topic, know this. The Galactic Council has re-instituted the ban on gambling, originally ratified under the Convention. We wholly support and stand behind this decision. Now we in the Council will lobby to allow experiments on representatives of other races -- with their consent, to be sure. And really, <Player>, you wouldn't refuse an intravenous neuron impulsator that would allow your body to work around the clock without ever needing to sleep or rest, now would you? That's what I thought!
Start: Ranger, a vexing development has taken place through the fault of the Galactic Council. Until yesterday, the internationally ratified Space Security Convention explicitly prohibited gambling and betting on pirate battles in outer space. It was considered that such events could result in casualties of civilian ships.

Yesterday, however, several amendments to the Convention were passed, among them the repeal of the gambling ban. The faeyan analytical council is of the opinion that this decision only partly serves civilian interests, seeing as it can greatly undermine established space security standards. We forecast the scenario in which disjointed bands of maloq hunters will return to wage epic battles with pirates for the money of peleng bookies and the cameras of human reality shows. We are absolutely certain that this situation will not serve the interests of the general public; consequently, we prudently increase the funds allocated for upholding security in space. You, <Player>, shall be paid a fee of <Money> cr if you can guarantee safe passage of all civilian ships in the <FromStar> system over the next <Day> days.

24.End: That is exactly the conduct that makes a ranger, <Player>! Don't you think that working for peace and prosperity is far superior to sowing lawlessness? We are glad that you've finally realized this truth; may this fee of <Money> cr bolster your new aspiration toward these highest of principles.
Start: Oh, <Player>, even a rotten criminal such as yourself gets the occasional chance to serve the common good. Our system will be hosting a wonderful humanitarian event -- a peace rally. As you well understand, children are the flowers of life and the future of our Galaxy, necessitating special, heightened security measures.

We are entrusting this mission upon you with hope that you will strengthen the spirit of peace throughout the universe, sowing kindness and humanism. Please save violence for the very last resort, when the aggressor absolutely cannot be assuaged from attacking civilian vessels. Serve with honor through <Date>, and then come back. Godspeed!
By the way, to prove to you that money can be earned without resorting to criminality, we intend to pay you <Money> cr for completing this mission.

25.End: We expected no less from a renowned ranger like you, <Player>! According to the updated security ratings, the <FromStar> system has risen by several tiers, which fills our hearts with hope and optimism. And though security is ensured via brute force at this time, we firmly believe that one day it will all change, and all intelligent creatures will abandon the path of violence once and for all. And may this reward of <Money> cr serve as a reminder of this imminent day.
Start: The Galactic Bureau of Statistics has published its rating of the Galaxy's safest systems, and the <FromStar> system came in at the very bottom! Does this fact sadden you as it does us, <Player>?

If so, then you have a wonderful opportunity to do your part and help our services correct this unfortunate situation. We think that a famous warrior such as yourself can easily withstand the onslaught of hostile ships in the next <Day> days. It is incumbent upon you to actualize the principles of ethics and high morality by serving as an indestructible wall between civilian ships and the chaos of destruction! And let the <Money> cr that our government intends to pay you for completing your mission be a pleasant bonus to the moral satisfaction you will surely achieve by bringing peace and harmony to the world...

26.End: May your name live on forever and ever, Ranger <Player>! The peace and serenity you've attained while protecting the innocent is a far greater reward than this <Money> cr. May you be ever as pure in your aspirations going forward!
Start: Merchant <Player>, is there anything better for an intelligent creature than peace and prosperity? And yet, the sorrowful fact is that the Galaxy is still full of those who have yet to realize this simple truth and for whom violence is a way of life. Sometimes they even visit our peaceful system, causing us great distress! Perhaps you could help us amend this situation?

Take up the banner of law and humanism within the <FromStar> system and keep order within its borders for <Day> days, making sure no civilian vessel falls victim to the aggressors. This will glorify your name for all eternity, <Player>! And don't worry, we have allocated a fee of <Money> cr to compensate for all the trade opportunities lost while working for us.

27.End: Dear <Player>, your selfless labor in the name of Harmony merits all manner of praise. Not a single civilian vessel perished in the time you patrolled the system, providing us with the opportunity to conduct a whole battery of tests. We are happy to present you with <Money> cr for your assistance in measuring the total harmonic field of the Galaxy. Oh yes, we do mean the whole Galaxy -- a massive research program is underway, of which this was only the first step.
Start: Our scholars and scientists never rest on their laurels, <Player>! Recently they invented a one-of-a-kind device to measure the inner Harmony of sentient creatures. We plan to start the testing phase in the <FromStar> system, measuring the level of Harmony for all its residents... With the obvious exception of aggressive characters like pirates and the military. Unfortunately, emotions like fear and mistrust distort the measurement data, which is why we must ask you to help us to test the device by ensuring safety for all civilian ships through <Date>. That way we can get the most accurate results, uncorrupted by negative emotions.

Provided that all civilian ships in the system are assured safe passage, we will be more than glad to pay you a reward of <Money> cr for your services. However, we don't want the money to be your sole motivation for this mission; indeed, greed is another extremely negative emotion that could seriously distort the measurement data.

End: It was so inspiring to see you in action, <Player>! Aside from our gratitude for ensuring security in the system, we are happy to pay you a monetary reward of <Money> cr.
By the way, could you help me solve an equation for the Olympics? (z2-z3)^2 = 4(z3-z1)(z1-z2) sin^2 alpha/2... Oh, but I mustn't delay you any longer. You have other great feats to accomplish!
Start: Have you ever had the chance to participate in Interstellar Olympics? The <FromStar> system is about to host the Olympic Games for the Galaxy's middle and high school students. In light of this, skimping on security would be downright criminal. Besides, young minds are very impressionable, and we fear that reports of victims of pirate aggression may disturb the participants and negatively affect the results.

Which is why we are appealing to your conscience and sense of duty. From now till <Date>, you must do whatever it takes to ensure that instead of reporting on the tragic demise of helpless merchants, the media will buzz with only one narrative -- that of the heroic exploits of a valorous warrior for justice! And by that we mean you, <Player>!
Oh yes, I almost forgot. A sum of <Money> cr will be your reward if you manage to complete this mission. No, no, don't even try to argue -- it is a gift from the heart!

29.End: Businessman <Player>, the Power is with you! What I mean is that you are indeed powerful against the forces of darkness. We have been so impressed with the peace that spread throughout our system over the period of your patrol duty that we would like to reward you with <Money> cr. We trust that you'll be wise and follow in the ways of Riolka and Sympha, his avatar.
Start: Merchant, do you feel the Power within? What I mean is, do you feel the power to resist evil and lawlessness? If so, we have an excellent opportunity for you to prove it, by guaranteeing peace and stability in our system for the next <Day> days.

We have the utmost faith in your abilities, <Player>, and we're confident that not a single civilian vessel will suffer at the hands of aggressors in the <FromStar> system. Our government is further prepared to pay you a fee of <Money> cr for coping with this uneasy task. After all, there must be proper recompense for all our actions, both good and bad! Don't you agree?

3.End: You are one brave ranger, <Player>! At first I thought you were just another cowardly pup, but you've certainly proved me wrong. The space orientation competition went off without a hitch. Well, almost without a hitch. Two of the participants are still lost somewhere in space. But whatever, it's their damn fault. Here's your reward of <Money> cr, which you can use to upgrade your weapons.
Start: The order is simple but worthy, like a maloq stoak club. Tomorrow marks the start of the space orientation competition in this sector of the Galaxy. Our system is in need of heightened security.
If no civilian ship gets shot down in this system over the next <Day> days, you will earn <Money> cr and all manner of merits. Now get to it!

End: Congratulations, <Player>! Now you are our very own stereovision star! No one before you could ever put up such a great performance on our local Masquerade reality show. Until now, this regular show has never brought in that kind of huge profits, and now we are planning to run it more often. The gist of the matter is that for the duration of the shoot we make all pirates acquire peaceful ship hulls, and, conversely, have all diplomats and merchants buy pirate ships and fly them. You have already had a leading role before, and your coolheaded actions helped us film some great material. By the way, the show runs under the auspices of our beloved Dzuhallag organization, so there's no need to worry. No rumors ever leave our system.

I hope you are not too upset about having been used in this way. I am not concerned at all. My conscience is clean since I never use it. In any case, these <Money> cr should restore your great moral spirit.
30.Start: I'll bet you <Money> cr that even such a famous ranger as yourself will not be able to accomplish this mission. Wanna bet? Great! Then let me give you a general idea of what's required of you: all you need to do is protect peaceful ships from destruction in our system until <Date>. And an additional request from me personally: get rid of as many of those disgusting lyakushas and their yes men as possible. Us pelengs, we only seem to be slippery. In fact, we are soft and furry and just can't stand pirates.

End: Ah, <Player>! You can relax.

We have been saved! Ha-ha, it now appears that our system has never been in danger to begin with. All it was is that some learned egghead incorrectly divided one number by another, and the result came out wrong. Consequently, the conclusion he made was also wrong. Funny, huh? One wonders why we have picked up this faeyan fad for conducting scientific research. War is the only true science. All the rest is just lies and smoke screens!

By the way, <Player>, how about another mission? We need to send the caged former head of our research center to the uninhabited planet Throawaya. But it's all right, you work too much anyway. Here is your <Money> cr, and go have some fun.
Start: <Player>! Somebody help!

A have just been informed by the head of the only research center of <FromPlanet> that we are just days away from Acopal... Apolac... Yes, that, Apocalypse. In a nutshell, we are all going to meet our maker soon.

Because of the frequent use of hyperengines in space, our <FromStar> system is very unstable now, and any strong energy upsurge, such as the explosion of a large spaceship, can upset the precarious balance. A gru.., no, gra... well, whatever collapse it is may happen and then a giant black hole will open and suck in our star and all the planets around it, <Player>, along with millions of their inhabitants, including quite a few brave maloqs.

You studied physics in school, didn't you? Excellent, that means you'll be able to handle your new mission. Scientists asked for more time to let them study the situation. We are certain they will be able to come up with something before <Date>. But until then it will be you mission to prevent ships in the <FromStar> system from exploding. You do not need to concern yourself with pirate rust buckets since they are way too small and cannot produce sufficient energy when exploding. Furthermore, those bandits do not deserve you saving their hides, do they?
There is no time for fruitless deliberations. Say yes, <Player>! If everything goes well, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr for your work.

32.End: Look! Look at these photos! They are just perfect! What a triumph of light and transforming matter! Except there was this ranger ship bustling about vigorously in front of the camera. It came from God only knows where and blatantly derailed our entire effort to film the exploding outer layers of the gas giant No. C2H6OJJT. Do you by any chance remember who was located there at the time? What about the navigation system data? Erased? Oh, you are saying you dropped your toast caviar down on the sensor panel? Purely by accident? What a pity! There goes another mission we could give you. It's all right though. It's not like it has anything to do with you. Or is it? Here is your well earned <Money> cr. You were quite useful.
32.Start: Dear <Player>, we anticipate a potential horrible catastrophe in the dust cloud in our neighboring Galaxy. Three quasars are expected to explode there one after another. You don't know what a quasar is? What's that line from a song, "Light, dust and quasars..." cough... excuse me, there's something wrong with my voice. Anyhow, our system is considered to be an ideal location for observing this unique event. We have spent two months cleaning it of stray asteroids, meteorites, ship debris and other junk so that a stray piece of trash wouldn't accidentally interfere with our observations. However, there is one problem. Those dang pirates are in the habit of stripping captured ships for parts all the time. We are sick and tired of all these emergency scrambles in the middle of the night, vacuums at the ready, to go clean up battle sites. For this reason, we have put our heads together and decided to tap you as our system's temporary guard. It will be your mission to patrol the system and preserve the delicate balance between pirates and their victims through <Date>. During this time no peaceful ship may be destroyed for fear it be turned into a giant pile of trash. This is all the more important since numerous GSA observers will be present in the system aboard their ships. That's Galactic Society of Astronomers, in case you are wondering. Pirates, on the other hand, are fair game, and you are free to deal with them as you see fit. That's one of the reasons we have selected a merchant such as yourself: we are certain that your good business acumen will not let you leave any valuable debris behind. GSA has allocated <Money> cr as a reward that you will receive upon successful completion of your mission. I wouldn't advise you to refuse. So what is your decision going to be?

End: Star!!! Give me an autograph. That's some way you handled them... By the way, 1.25% of the profits equals exactly <Money> cr. Yes, absolutely, it's all yours. You deserve it.

By the way, we have a blockbuster shaping up here, Little Titanic. Well, it's about a spaceship getting sucked into a distorted black hole with no way out, and there are two few escape pods available, but plenty of love, and there's only one hero rescuer -- you! We'll even order you an actress straight out of the Playhumanoid magazine. Here, have a look at the cover. Miss February! You like her? Well, it's not like I haven't seen maloq girls before... But at least no one is going to get into the escape pod with you.
Where do you want to go?
Start: Well, Ranger <Player>, we kind of started thinking you'd never ask... We have some business to discuss.

The pirate community of our system has been making a new reality show, Tough Guys. They pick one pirate or other to be the bad guy of the month, and he goes about his favorite thing in the world, wreaking havoc, right there on camera. As an experienced pilot, you know what I mean. The show is carried by transgalactic TV and is broadcast all over our huge Galaxy. The ratings are very much commensurate with the profits ripped by those pirates, and both are out of this world. We just couldn't sit still and simply watch all that mischief. No, I don't mean the destruction of peaceful ships. We ain't no dummies here, we want a piece of show business too.

Yes, we have created our own project -- an anti-drama of sorts. Tough Guys Get Their Butts Whipped. But here's the problem we are having: all tough pilots have gone pirate, the military is busy with their war, and we simply have no suitable candidates to star in our show. At first we tried to recruit some tried and true tough pilots, stars in their own right so to speak -- leaders of dominator groups: Keller, Blazer, Terron. But they wouldn't even talk to our managers, period, let alone participate in the show. All you would here from them would be: "Unidentified object..." "Stand by for being transformed," or some unintelligible garble altogether, like g4gkjrepe egke a44yukl95p... Man, what a waste of talent!
So now we want to offer the leading part to you. I think you are going to do just fine. All the more so since you are a darling of our entire Galaxy now.

You are almost a star in your own right. A little make-up, a shave, some cool duds... And stop hunching your shoulders! Our screenwriters have already started writing sound bites for you, like "Stand in awe, here I come...", "Hide or face the music" and some such.

Long story short, all you have to do is spend <Day> days saving a few civilian ships and, if you feel like it, maybe send a couple of pirates to meet their maker. But that's up to you, of course. Naturally, you will be getting a percentage of profits here. And don't forget -- smile, always smile, it is so becoming.

End: Thank you, <Player>, for protecting our system so well. Fortunately for us, Galaforecast -- the Galactic Forecast Center -- made a mistake, and the dominators chose another system for their attack. Not a single peaceful ship has been harmed while you were patrolling the orbit. Here is your well-deserved <Money> cr. You have completed your mission so successfully that we are not even sure we want to let you go at all. Don't go just yet, a new report by the Galaforecast is being broadcast on stereovision as we speak.

"... and dominators from distant Gralgar will open a front in this sector... It will bring high dominator activity to the region. Unexpected dominator attacks are likely throughout the <FromStar> system in the short term."
So, should we hire you or not? All right, you can go, our budget is overstrained as it is. All available funds went to pay for Galaforecast reports.
34.Start: We will always have a job for you, <Player>. Galaforecast predicts that our system will be attacked by dominators in the immediate future. Naturally, we are not crazy about these damn tin men roaming our planets. It will be your mission to protect us for <Day> days from dominators -- and while you are at it, from all other calamities as well. If no peaceful ships are destroyed in our system during this time, you will be paid a substantial fee of <Money> cr.

End: Dear <Player>, on behalf of the entire planet <FromPlanet> let me congratulate you on the successful accomplishment of your mission. Please accept these well-deserved <Money> cr. From now on, you will always be a welcome guest on our planet.

By the way, we have recently caught the end of a previously aborted message: "... the scout will be proceeding under guard by a pirate ship..." So now we need to ask you if you have by any chance destroyed any pirates in our system during this time. No, no, we are not accusing you of anything. We hope the Committee will actually issue us a free trade permit. I wouldn't dare holding you back any longer, ranger. Once again, thank you for your service.
35.Start: Dear ranger <Player>, you couldn't have asked about it at a better moment! We have another important mission for you. Our planet <FromPlanet> is reaching a new level of trade relations with planets in other systems. However, in order to receive a permit to engage in global intersystem trade we need to meet all the requirements set forth in the Galactic Trade Committee Treaty.
