We have already met all of them except one. Now we need to prove it to them that cargo ships will enjoy safe transit across the <FromStar> system. We have received the following message from the GTC: "... an associate of ours is being dispatched to your system and will remain there until <Date> to verify that trade traffic in the vicinity of your planet will encounter no security issues..." That was all we have managed to get since our sector of the system is now experiencing wave storms, and the hypercommunications are not altogether reliable. If we understood it correctly, their mystery visitor will be making observations disguised as a regular ship. We wouldn't be overly concerned, but recent increases in the pirate activities by some of the buccaneer fleet keep us on edge. This is the reason why we are turning to you since unlike anyone else you are capable of realizing the serious nature of this situation and offering help. The mission would involve making our system secure and preventing any peaceful ships from being shot down until the said date. If you successfully abide by those terms, we will pay you <Money> cr. If you agree, you can get started right away.

36.End: You have done a great job, <Player>! All the surviving competitors are saying that they have never had their attacks repulsed so vigorously. The winner said he was looking forward to seeing you among some of the most dangerous pirates. <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account.
36.Start: Yes, <Ranger>, we happen to have a fairly unusual job for you. The thing is that our system will host an annual pirate competition soon. The competitors will attempt to evade military patrols and rob as many ships as they can. Unfortunately, our navy is now busy conducting an operation against dominators, and we have no one available to protect merchants from attacks. If you agree to help us and play a military patrol, once the competition is over you will be paid a substantial fee of <Money> cr. There is one condition though. This is going to be a very high level event with participation by some of the sector's most esteemed lyakushas, so you really have to show us quality work. To earn your fee, you will have to prevent the competitors from destroying peaceful ships until <Date>. Are you game?

37.End: Dear <Player>! On behalf of the Chief Health Minister of <FromPlanet>, let me thank you for your service. The agreed upon <Money> cr have already been transferred to your account. Personally, I only have one thing left to do -- to wish you good ironclad maloq health.
Start: Dear Ranger <Player>, you couldn't have asked about it at a better moment! The problem is that for many years our planet has been plagued by a terrorist sect that calls itself Duck and Cover. Traditionally, this month is their favorite for doing something nasty. But this time the terrorists went above and beyond -- quite literally too, going outside the confines of our planet to wreak havoc. They have released a biological agent into the ventilation shaft of our main spaceport. As their weapon, they have chosen a gas that causes holy fanaticism -- a disease I am sure you have heard of. I am not going to go into medical particulars here, but let me just say this is very unfortunate. While we managed to nip the epidemic in the bud on our planet, there are still some renegade pilots out there in our system that have refused to undergo necessary urinotherapy and may present danger to others. For the most part, they were all sleazy characters, pirates and such that had always flaunted the law.

Therefore, ranger, this time your mission is to protect this system for a period of <Day> days while our medical teams and special service operators track down, detain and forcefully treat every carrier of the D16M04 virus. You will receive a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Yes, yes, make the agreement! Get five hundred containers right away! And the explosives, the more the better.

Who are you? What are you doing here? Oh, Ranger <Player>, is that you? You came to get your money, right? By the may, we did find one good use for this culture thing -- the performance can be used by our soldiers in lieu of Phys Ed. Did you see the drummers? Now, what if we gave their drums a lead padding? And give them sticks of cast iron? There's a great way to promote physical strength! But why do I bother, none of this is your business anymore. You have accomplished your mission. Here is your <Money> cr, and you are all free to do as you please.
38.Start: Yes, we have a mission for you, <Player>! It will suit your venal merchant nature to a tee. The thing is that to promote our arms trade our planet is interested in joining a certain economic treaty with participation by some gaal and faeyan planets, among others. And so all those sissies, hell bent that they are on throwing a monkey wrench into our plans, came up with a condition: they now want to assess the culture of the new member planet! How about it, huh? Culture, my ass! Strength, that's what matters. Then again, what do you wheelers and dealers know about such matters? Anyhow, for <Day> days observers from these planets will be visiting our system. For the duration, you have to protect our system, so that no one would get shot down. Got it? All right, then what are you still waiting for? Money?! Money is all you can ever think about! <Money> cr should be right on the money! And now off you go and get on with your mission.

End: Great job, <Player>! You have done a noble deed worthy of a true humanist and aficionado of high culture. You have earned every penny of your <Money> cr. Very much unlike those peleng hustlers too!

Just imagine, a group of these peleng slicks got around our IQ detector and tried to talk their way into a casino posing as gifted students (with IQs as high as 210) and arguing that the place was the seat of education and culture. What blatant impudence, huh?

You may wonder if these pelengs have exhibited any real genius. Well, see for yourself. It appear that the device we use displays the sum total IQ of all those in the test booth rather than the average. And there were three pelengs in the booth being scanned at the same time. So here's a simple problem: what was each peleng's average IQ if the device's calculations are accurate to 1.2% per every 10 IQ units below the mean parametric Urgol ratio, which, as I am sure you know, equals half the square root of the Figure-Psy constant.

Ranger? Hey, Ranger! Man, you have almost gone catatonic trying to solve this problem! It's very strange, how difficult could it be? By the way, would you care to have your own IQ measured by our device? Oh, you are in a hurry... What a pity!
Start: Dear <Player>, we are glad to welcome you to our planet. If you would like to make use of your comprehensive skills as a combat pilot, we could offer you a job. No, no, there will be no destroying involved; on the contrary, we would like to offer you a contract to protect the innocent.

The thing is that our government has launched a massive tourism program for the most gifted students. Students of genius with an IQ of at least 191, regardless of their race, will be able to visit cultural and historical monuments of interest located throughout our entire system absolutely free. Many thousands of smart students from all over our Galaxy are already taking advantage of this opportunity to travel the length and breadth of our system and enjoy the benefits of this no holds barred effort to promote education and culture. We simply must keep up the good work. There must be no incidents, let alone casualties, among our guests. Ranger, we would appreciate your help with this. If <Day> days go by without any peaceful ship being destroyed in our <FromStar> system, we will pay you <Money> cr.

4.End: We were right to trust you, <Player>! You're a fine example for all maloq youth! All the pirates ran like whipped puppies! We might even propose moving regular space routes into our system. We maloqs will now pay you <Money> cr. Spend it wisely, like on new weapons for your ship!
Start: Ranger <Player>! The maloq rumor mill has it you know how to deal with your enemies. And we just happen to have an urgent mission for one such as you. A space highway that goes through a neighboring system has been temporarily shut down. Thus, the bulk of the traffic will be going through our system.

You must fly out at once and start patrolling! Not a single civilian ship may perish the next <Day> days or your name will be dishonored on all the maloq planets! What are you waiting for?! Right, the job pays <Money> cr.

End: We did it, <Player>! All superfuel has been recovered, and no one got hurt. Here is your well-deserved <Money> cr. Yes, olachemorg's combustion rate is way too high for it to be used as a fuel. On the other hand, it could be used as a very powerful weapon. We could crush planets and entire systems! The maloq race could put everyone else on their--
Hmmmm.... Still here? Don't you think it's time for you to get out of here? Take my advice on this one too and keep mum about everything you have seen or heard here.
Start: Oh, <Player>, have you heard that horrible explosion? How could you possibly not hear the explosion if it had caused our poor planet <FromPlanet>'s orbit to shift by a quarter inch, and our neighboring planet lost two satellites that got ejected outside the system? Let me tell you, you sleep like a baby!

And that's just the beginning of it, ranger! If nothing is done urgently, a series of such explosions could simply destroy our system... ... with plenty left over for our neighbors if we don't stop the spread of our olachemorg. Oh, yes! I almost forgot! You may have heard of our new superfuel called <clr>olachemorg<clrEnd>. Unfortunately, this cheap and effective fuel turned out to be an unbelievably powerful explosive. But, alas, we have learned this too late, and hundreds of ships have already been fueled with our super propellant. All it takes for a ship so fueled is to heat up, and then everything goes boom!

<Player>, I beg you, please help us while our special services apologize to pilots and refuel ships. All it takes for olachemorg to detonate is firing a few shots at the ship that has been fueled with it. If you undertake to protect peaceful ships in our system from pirate attacks, we will pay you <Money> cr. It should take us no more than <Day> days to withdraw olachemorg completely. Fortunately, pirates and the military refuel at their own bases that have had no superfuel deliveries yet, so it is only civilian ships that you need to protect.

End: Wonderful, <Player>! This malfunctioning filter helped us get truly amazing results. It appears that there are certain formulas and fundamental laws that govern propagation of thought in vacuum. It is now obvious that propagation rate isn't at all constant! You have honestly earned your <Money> cr and a mention on the list of project researchers.

By the way, do you want to know which of the thoughts happened to be the slowest? There were two of them, and they were both maloq: "What did you call me, huh?" and "Two plus two is... seems to be equal to... two plus two!" And the fastest? No! Not the faeyan "Somebody help me, please!", and not even the human "What's in it for me?", but the peleng "Shucks, this is <Player> again!" I told you, the results are incredible.
Start: <Player>, I am glad to welcome you to our flourishing planet that is a true epitome of scientific thought and progress! Everyone knows that it is here, on planet <FromPlanet>, that the most significant cutting edge scientific research is taking place.
Would you like to help promote scientific progress to benefit the entire galactic community? If your answer is yes, then we invite you to participate in our new project.

You may have heard of such fundamental constants as the speed of light, hyperimpulse and thought in vacuum. At the moment, our scientists are trying to weed out the errors in their calculations of the last of them, the so-called constant. They are doing it because we believe that such thoughts as "I could use a bite" and "I am starving" propagate at different rates of speed. If we manage to prove a significant difference between the two experimentally, psy-science will reach a new level.

At the moment, our system has a few dozen operational satellite receivers of telepathic radiation from intelligent creatures. Unfortunately, the high level of mental noise around the inhabited planets prevents us from taking measurements with required precision. For that reason, we are now particularly interested in lone space travelers, such as pilots and passengers traversing the system aboard their ships. Knowing the locations of our sources, we can easily calculate the speeds of the thoughts we receive. In accordance with the existing research schedule, at the moment our listening devices are calibrated to record peaceful thinking, for which reason we need to filter out various panic and anxiety thoughts. And that's where we need your help.

To obtain convincing data, we would need to take several thousand measurements, which could be difficult because of the threat of pirate attacks. On the one hand, such attacks promote panic among civilian ships and cause them to call for help (which puts our filters under additional stress and, consequently, increases the level of mental noise), and on the other the mental activity of dead pilots stands at zero, which is unacceptable for our experiments. If you help ensure that no peaceful ship gets destroyed in our system until <Date>, we will pay you <Money> cr.

42.End: Wonderful, <Player>! Have you already seen the set designs created by my people? Oh, yes, I forgot. The real stage set was assembled at a different place altogether, and these here are all fakes, make-believes whose only purpose is to throw meddlesome paparazzi off the right track. Regardless, you have honestly earned your <Money> cr.
Start: What if... Say, ranger, do you like the movies the way I like them? The thing is that I am now funding a remake of a historical thriller, Surrogates in Space, based on an ancient human story about the Surrogate Sea. There was, as the story goes, this sea where the currents took every vessel to one huge island littered with dead ships, a cemetery really. So, that's where it all happened, on the island made of nautical detritus.

Now we are putting together a stage set -- a huge planetoid made of ship debris. Of course, it's a prop all around. Although I am sure you understand that the media only needs an excuse here. They'll be all too happy to accuse me of destroying peaceful ships to get these debris for my stage set.
That's where I need your help. If you help ensure that no peaceful ship gets destroyed in this system until <Date>, no reporter will be able to accuse me of anything, and you will be paid <Money> cr.

43.End: All right, <Player>, let me shake your limp merchant hand. Don't worry, I am not going to squeeze hard or your hand joints will all pop out of place. You have successfully proven it that even the dullest and most cowardly of rangers can actually stand his ground and protect others if he gives it his all. Your success notwithstanding, I recommend that you leave your trading alone, buy yourself some cool guns with the <Money> cr you have made and start whacking our enemies because this is what rangers are for to begin with.
Start: <Player>, aren't you ashamed of yourself? While the Coalition is straining in battle, your are hauling junk in your cargo bay, peddling it around for profit. I wouldn't be surprised if your guns are all rusted out, and the shield generator is covered with cobwebs -- that is, if you even have it. You are not worthy of being called a ranger! Give me your badge, I'm gonna eat it. No, you want to keep it? All right, then here is your chance to correct the error of your ways, here and now.

Our system has been under attack by pirates for some time now. These rascals rob and destroy peaceful ships under our very noses, and we cannot repulse them because our own glorious warriors are now waging war in other parts of the Galaxy. I called their leader and offered him a wager: if I can find a ranger who could protect our stellar system from the pirate onslaught for <Day> days, they will knock it all off and leave us alone. He took me up on it, but only on condition that the ranger must not be a renown warrior, but rather some clueless merchant. I agreed because I firmly believe that deep down inside every ranger is a dedicated fighter for the Coalition.

Now, <Player>, here's your chance to prove you are worthy of your name. Get up and go! Go fight for galactic peace! If it's not you, ranger, then who else? If no ships get destroyed in our system up until <Date>, I will be the first to admit that you are in fact worth something. And since all of you rangers are miserly penny pinchers at heart, we will pay you <Money> cr to cover repairs to your ship and as a sign of our appreciation. But if you can't protect our civilians, I'd better not see your ugly mug ever again, or I'll bite your face off and tear the rest of you into pieces.

44.End: Congratulations, <Player>! Peace and quiet have come to our system! My special thanks to you for making all those lyakushas, bambays and corsairs remember their manners. Your replacement is coming on duty tomorrow. Sign off and go receive your fee. Good luck to you!
Start: This is truly amazing, <Player>, that you were so eager to see me that two of the guards will now need to be sent to the hospital with bruising all over their... well, thing, you know... Anyway, that's not important. Coming back to the business at hand, I am all ears.

Pfft! What do you mean "the system is a mess"? Don't you have any scruples at all? Where would we even get a regular patrol for the system if everyone coherent had gone to the front and all the incoherent ones are now on disability -- no small thanks to you, by the way. Would you like order? I could arrange for it.

All right, <Player>, since you are a ranger and it is your duty to help systems that find themselves in dire straights, I would like you to take it upon yourself to protect this system for <Day> days. It should give me sufficient time to find a proper sheriff for our system.  So, how about it?
What's the reward? What happened to your high moral principles? How about an Idiota Bronzata medal? No?
All right, <Player>, if no civilian ships are destroyed in our system until <Date>, you can expect to be paid <Money> cr with my compliments. Any other questions?

45.End: Excellent work, <Player>! FUFU came around, promised us a pound. I mean, a loan. I've already been contemplating my options for spending my share of the loot -- I mean agent's commission. Speaking of money, here is your <Money> cr, and go ahead, make yourself scarce. The sooner the better. Don't interfere with my dreams!
Start: What is it, <Player>, you came to gloat over my misfortune? What do you mean "what misfortune"? Didn't you hear our planet is, basically, bankr--

HOLD ON A MINUTE. Your saving at our interstellar bank are perfectly safe! At least for the time being. I am sure you understand that only a miracle, such as a huge loan, may help save our world. We've been promised one by FUFU - the Foundation for Unwinding Frivolous Ultimatums.

To be sure, these "saviors" set a number of conditions, such as cutting the salaries of line workers, reducing education and healthcare costs, doing away with annual bonuses for the upper management and ensuring safe passage of trade vessels throughout the system.

We've met the first two already and figured out what to do with the third -- we'll pay the annual bonuses in quarterly installments. But what are we going to do with security? Our system has always been popular with rookie pirates, making the deed easy and fun. There's no time to waste. The FUFU committee is expected to arrive in a few days. Eureka!

<Player>, would you like to make <Money> cr? Yes? Then do your best to make sure that not a single peaceful ship is shot down in our system for <Day> days. To accomplish this mission successfully, please use any means necessary, up to and including total annihilation of your opposition.

And don't you handle these pirates with kids gloves. We have warned them of the upcoming operation. Smart ones will take heed and get out of here of their own accord, and if a few stupid ones are whacked, the Galaxy is not going to stop spinning. What do you say?

End: TEN-- HUT!

Excellent work, <Player>! Our rookies have plenty to learn from you. If that's how you handle dominators as well, then our Great Victory isn't long in coming. Here's your <Money> cr. THANK YOU FOR YOUR SERVICE!
You are free to go.
Start: TEN-- HUT! LISTEN TO ME EVERYONE!! SHUT UP!

Listen up, recruit! You've got yourself a special mission: to protect peaceful ships in this system from all kinds of punks that would try to blow them to smithereens or shake them down for some cold hard cash.

For the next <Day> days, it will be you, <Player>, who will be protecting the civilians. And watch out, we can't have even a single civilian ship destroyed in our system. Got it? If you handle it right, we'll pay you <Money> cr. If you fail, we'll court-martial you.

And by the way, judge Morrow Wind is notorious for not having brought a single not guilty verdict throughout his entire career. Your options are crystal clear here, aren't they? Then put your signature or some kind of check mark where it says "I have read the above contract, understand the terms and conditions set forth herein and agree to abide thereby."

End: Ranger, you did an absolutely top notch job! The number of discoveries made exceeded all our expectations, and when we mentioned your name at the closing ceremony a host of scientists offered to name different celestial objects after you. Furthermore, one of them actually followed through on this. Congratulations, an entire asteroid was named after you -- <Player><clr>-489<clrEnd>. Sounds good, doesn't it? So this asteroid of yours is now ... um ... no more, actually -- it was shot down by pirates yesterday and taken apart for its minerals.
Please accept my condolences. I hope the fee of <Money> cr will help alleviate your loss somewhat.
Start: Yes, we have a mission for you, <Player>! And don't you start hyperventilating at the mere sound of this word, mission. Don't you know that we have a law in effect until <Date> that makes it illegal for humanoids to inhale in excess of 1 cubic inch of air per second? It is exactly how long our All-Galactic Astronomy Symposium will last, and all those folks complain that your frequent breathing makes the lenses of the telescopes mist up.

Back to the mission, the symposium is expected to produce over a hundred great discoveries, and we simply cannot afford to put any of them at risk only because some of the objects to be observed could be obscured by mundane space trash. It will be your mission, ranger, to prevent any ships in the system from being shot down and thus help avoid any resulting complications for the astronomers until the symposium is over. Upon successful completion of the mission, you will receive a reward of <Money> cr.

48.End: Wonderful, just wonderful, <Player>! Vaccination has already begun, and now nothing is threatening the health of our system. Besides, this medication is so effective that you you can easily afford having your ship destroyed in our system. Even if the virus breaks free, it will do no harm to vaccinated pilots. It is such a pity you are not on our list of those eligible for vaccination! However, I could still offer you a shot on the side. Oops! Congratulations on getting well, <Player>! Your reward after unexpected medical costs comes down to <Money> cr. Good luck to you and take good care of yourself!
Start: Well, well, well, <Player>! Let me shake your honest hand. We have a little mission for you. All the peaceful ships in our system -- and now that includes you as well -- have been infected with the horrible Rad virus. Don't worry, it isn't all black. The virus is fairly passive and only acts up and mutates unexpectedly when subjected to strong stellar radiation. For that reason, it is not recommended that you spacewalk without a suit, he-he. This is also the reason why we cannot allow the virus to break free. All hell will break loose then. Faeyan scientists we have invited for the purpose almost finished developing an appropriate medication and even set a date for mass vaccination -- <Date>. But until then, my poor sick ranger, it will be your duty to protect peaceful ships in our system -- including your own, of course.
Upon successful completion of this mission, I will pay you 1,000,000,000 credits myself.

End: Welcome, but you're a little late. The conference has already... Ah, you're the ranger who... Remind me, would you, which mission were you given? Ah, yes. Protecting our system for the purpose of... What year is it?

As you can see, you can go crazy from all this knowledge! You can't imagine what happened, but that's probably for the best. The load on the brain is simply unbelievable! Have you ever wondered how the trajectory of large flying insects impacts currency devaluation and interplanetary tariffs? Or that bread falling "buttered-side down" depends on the height of the bread's original position in space? And I won't even go into the mind-bending research into cross-gender misunderstandings.
Anyway, here's your <Money> cr. This sum specifically expresses the value of the knowledge you were able to obtain during this time, <Player>. Have a good day.
Start: Welcome, ranger <Player>. It's great to see a face so delicately framed by intellect. What do you think is the original source of everything: thought or matter? What's the matter, <Player>? Are you not feeling well? Have a seat. Relax.

You would probably do well to attend the first annual "Great Thinker" conference, which will be held for <Day> days. During this time, thousands of representatives from all over the Galaxy will gather on our glorious planet to share their observations and conclusions in all sorts of fields. Just have a look at the program: the eighteenth report on "Which Came First? The Chicken or the Egg?", a full collection of answers to "What's the Difference between a Duck?", and the main feature of the program, "The Dissolution and Quantitative Deviation of Pairs of Socks."

<Player>, what's the matter? Not feeling well again? ? It's obvious you aren't very interested in participating in the conference. O! A thought! You could participate, say, indirectly. We happen to need a ranger to protect our guests from undesirable contacts with hostile ships. If you, <Player>, can provide reliable security for the intellectual legacy of the universe for <Day> days, then you'll receive <Money> cr at the end of the conference and I'll give you a summary of everything that happened. Deal? Excellent. Good luck!

5.End: Splendid! You did a fine job and have earned your share: <Money> cr. I could give you more, but greed is every peleng's middle name. Thanks for assisting the administration of the <FromStar> system, the only legitimate authority in this sector of the Galaxy.
5.Start: Erm, <Player>, we've got a proposition for you. A friend of mine works in the government in another system. Every so often we have ourselves an administrative competition. A couple of days ago we waged a bet on which of our two systems is safer. Would you care to help settle the bet in my favor? For a fee, to be sure. If no civilian ship is shot down in this system until <Date>, I will share a part of my winnings with you, specifically <Money> cr. Do we have a deal?

End: What? What <Player>? What mission? You're the ranger that guarded our system from the pirates? So what? You didn't let a single attack happen? Hmm... You know, the auditor already arrived... The day after you took the mission. He accepted all the gifts, signed all the reports without looking at them, and didn't verify a thing except our tavern... I guess it was a miracle, not an auditor. It's just too bad he drank and ate half our budget away in the tavern and didn't pay a single cred, but I guess that's the way it goes. I've got to think positive.

So what did you want? A reward? After this audit our entire planetary economy may go off the rails, but you still expect a reward for doing what essentially ended up being a useless job! Fine, fine, don't give me that look, you're scaring me... Here's your <Money> cr. Be off now -- I've got enough to deal with even without you.
50.Start: Missions? There aren't any missions! <Player>, are you blind? We're in crunch time here! Imagine, literally an hour ago we received the worst possible news: an auditor is coming. And what's happening here? The air routes are clogged with garbage; the vacuum-magnetic railroad connecting our city to the Penchecrakia settlement is only halfway built; the historical center restoration is dragging on for a decade -- heck, it hasn't even begun! -- and I won't even go into all the government officials greasing their palms every chance they get! Well... except for me, of course... Stop looking at me like that! Basically, if the auditor reports all of this as he should, we will all be removed from our posts, and I'll be the first! What's more, the pirates in the system are on a rampage. Not a day goes by without an incident. Speaking of pirates... You were looking for work, right? What do you think of me writing this in the report on piracy: "<Day> days without incident." Is that substantive enough? What do you say? Implausible? Well, your job is to make the report plausible. If not one civilian ship in our system perishes for <Day> days, then we may even pay you something. Do you understand the mission?

End: This is simply marvelous! I didn't know you could make so much money doing something like this! Never mind that we seized the majority of the budget allocated for humanitarian activities, we now have in our hands the fund for the assistance of deprived children, which contains more than one million donated credits! It's just beyond belief!
But hush up, ranger! No one must find out about this! ! And remember, we have a contract with your signature on it, so if you turn us in, you'll end up in court as an accomplice.

As for your wages, they have been safely transferred to your account. Honestly, we didn't want to pay you anything, but since we're literally swimming in credits, it would be stupid to quarrel over such an insignificant sum. Thanks again for your help, <Player>!
Start: Ah, Ranger <Player>. You're just in time.

Unfortu... I  mean, to the great joy and overwhelming happiness of the entire people of planet <FromPlanet>, our planet has been selected as the headquarters for the conference to promote humanitarian sentiments. After all, everyone knows about peleng pacifism, humanity, and general tolerance. The conference begins tomorrow and will last <Day> days.

But there's a problem. A lot of ships have been shot down in our system of late, and we can't let anything like that happen during the conference. Moreover, the money to prevent such incidents has already been received by us and successfully embezzled, so we don't have any other out than to hire you to guarantee the safety of all ships in the <FromStar> system.
You will receive a fee of <Money> cr for this work, but only after the conference is over. No advance payments!

52.End: Good job, <Player>. You really gave those newbies something to remember you by, Klissans take them! Now they'll be as meek as lambs... for two or three weeks. Then they'll start acting up again. They're like children who don't understand and don't want to understand. All they do is compare guns to see whose is more powerful. So if you happen to find yourself having nothing to do in about a month, fly over here to restore order again. Now sign this paper to receive your <Money> cr. and drink a small glass of our ceremonial tokilla. To our success!
Start: Lots of things are happening in our system. Pirates from clans like the Mad Beaks, Savory Guys, and Bold Peepers have arranged a competition to test which clan can steal the most money from the ships in this star system. Of course, they never asked me if I liked their idea or whether it would negatively affect my cash inflow from interplanetary trade. I do like it, but I can't sacrifice my guys. If they all end up dead, this place will descend into total chaos. So I'm turning to you, an independent and respected mate, asking you to restore order in our orbit.
If no civilian vessel is brought down in my <FromStar> star system over the next <Day> days, I'll happily give you <Money> cr. as a reward, <Player>.

53.End: Good job, <Player>. While you were driving away those useless beggars, I had time to rebuild the fountain, and once again the square has its old wonderful appearance. Look how beautifully the light beams are refracted in the jets of the water rising into the sky... Hey, quit that snorting! You have no sense of the beautiful, so get lost. Don't worry about the money; it's already in your account.
Start: <Player>, please be so kind as to come to the window. Now look out of it. Can you see that luxurious fountain, decorated with statues of pirate leaders and illuminated with underwater searchlights and hololasers, right in the center of the square? No, you can't? Well, what CAN you see? Yes, what you see right in the center is a huge hole with a piece of skin stuck there, a piece from some ugly transport ship that failed to reach its hangar because it was showered with fire from above by a brainless corsair, one of the dozens hanging about in our star system...

This is the final nail in the coffin of my patience, <Player>. I liked that fountain very much. I had partially funded its construction, but now it's gone. That's why I'm willing to pay you <Money> cr. to disperse that band of half-wits in the sky. The more of them you smash into atoms, the better, since it'll teach them a good lesson! Just try not to bring them down in our orbit. Do it in open space, otherwise my righteous anger will fall on you too! If you agree to do this for at least <Day> days, then we will consider it a deal.

54.End: Thank you, <Player>. Your selfless labor has enabled us to make a big step towards the knowledge of Ga's principles. Your money has already been transferred to your account. May enlightenment abide with you! And remember, for future reference: if you fail to realize the importance of these principles yourself, one day you may take your place among those whom you have just destroyed.
54.Start: I got a task for you, <Player>. Although we are pirates, we honor the precepts of our ancestors and respect their philosophy. Unfortunately, many Gaals grew up far away from our world, from the essence of the three rights and Ga's principles. They don't respect those who adhere to the classical ideas, and they consider us too conservative. Let it be so. We outnumber them, so we can dictate our terms to them. And these terms are as follows: a period of peace, dedicated to perceiving the value of life, is now effective in our star system for <Day> days. Not a single peaceful soul, one without the hunger for blood, can see the end of its life during this time period, or it will nullify all of our studious efforts and make us look bad in the eyes of our wavering and doubting adolescents. If you, <Player>, can ensure peace in our orbit, we will be bound to pay you <Money> cr. once this time period is over. We permit you only to destroy  the pirates, since their souls are black and they don't care for knowledge of the world through kindness.

55.End: Good job, <Player>. The sectarians have been pacified for some time, there are fewer thugs in the galaxy, and money from trade business continues to flow into our open, welcoming pockets. Rejoice: <Money> cr. have already been added to your account. And if one day you need any positive recommendations, you know who to turn to.
Start: Look, <Player>, if we are pirates, that doesn't mean that we shoot and rob everyone without a break. If we shoot down all the hucksters, what will we do then? Will we transport food and minerals from one system to another ourselves? Of course not. So the conclusion is obvious: the merchants are a necessary part of our pirate society.

What am I trying to say? That merchant ships flying through our star system must continue doing that, and the more the better! But the other day I learned from some reliable sources that a notorious sect of the GameDevs of Dawn is preparing a series of attacks against civilian ships in our sector by hiring some pigheaded thugs who won't even be able to explain who hired them and what for. These sectarians want us to give them a notorious artifact called the Devvie's Finger. I have no idea what that is. I only know that I don't like their plans at all.

That's why I'm asking you, <Player>, as a respected and sensible pirate and fellow clansman, to guard civilian ships in our star system before they are all slaughtered and people start telling bloodcurdling stories about us. This punitive action will last for <Day> days, and I would like to ask you to agree to guard our star system during that time, for a worthy reward of <Money> cr.

6.End: Hey, <Player>, here's the <Money> cr that you've earned with your valor. If it were my call, I'd double the reward, but my boss wants none of that. He says it's already too much for a pirate fighter. Our entire budget goes to support piracy. So, terribly sorry, but we couldn't scrap any more. Just the same, everyone was very impressed by your courage!
Start: Dearest <Player>, we desperately need you to do a service for us in the next <Day> days. And you, I presume, desperately need the <Money> cr we're willing to pay for this service. Intrigued? Then listen up!

Our <FromStar> system has suffered terribly from a recent dominator attack. Our security systems are weakened. Our forecasts suggest that we need not fear a dominator attack in the nearest future. Pirates, however, are an even bigger threat than before; I say this as an expert in pirates and their devious ways. Ah, the good ole' days of my youth... Mmm... Anyway, your mission it to protect this system from pirates and other suspicious elements through <Date>, making sure there are no unnecessary casualties. Necessary casualties, on the other hand, are acceptable -- specifically amongst the pirates.

End: <Player>, you are a model of courage and valor! We thank you for your excellent job! The observation station is fully functional, the population of kwamras on the planet has been reduced to acceptable levels, and the <FromStar> system is safe once again.

What's that you say? I don't feel any stench... Oh, you must meant this exquisite aroma of grilled kwamra! You can stay a while and try some, if you want to. Peleng doctors agree that nausea is a sure sign that a food is of the highest quality. I can assure you that you won't find anything like it anywhere else... Hey, where are you going? Don't forget your <Money> cr!
Then again... Shucks, you came back! Truly, my mouth is my own worst enemy!
Start: It's good that you've decided to stay here, <Player>! We have a job for you that's worth <Money> cr. Just recently a pack of wild kwamras devastated an orbital observation station with all its equipment. That means we no longer have even the slightest idea what's going on in our system. And yet common sense and our flawless peleng intuition suggest that it wouldn't hurt to beef up security.

We will pay you <Money> cr for your assistance to our orbital defense forces. If you can keep the gangsters from destroying civilian vessels in this system for at least <Day> days, that should give us enough time to repair the observation station.

End: Thanks, <Player>! You've made me a proud father, 'cause my son got the highest possible grade thanks to you! And I hope you will consider this fee of <Money> cr sufficiently generous. No? Really? Dang, I spend less money on my brat's cheat sheets!

By the way, his next exams are on the following subjects: plunder, espionage, and sabotage. If he gets straight A's down the stretch, he will be granted a license to kill civilians. Who knows, he might even become <FromPlanet>'s Supreme Lyakusha one day! The mere thought of it fills my heart with pride for my offspring!! Yeaaaaah!
Start: <Player>, dearest! I have a personal favor to ask you. You see, my son is a senior in a peleng military academy. He used to be a good student, but this year everything has changed. He's flunking terribly and has zero knowledge of space combat tactics.

Now, how can I put this delicately... Could you possibly take a super-easy exam for him? All you need to do is ensure safe passage for all civilian ships in the <FromStar> system through <Date>. Most naturally, your reward will be quite generous -- have no doubt!

9.End: Awesome, <Player>, here's your <Money> cr! Representatives of the Galactic Council found no cause for concern and peacefully departed from the system. Which means we pirates can now crawl out of the woodwork. In case you didn't pick up on it, I also represent a local pirate clan. Just don't tell anyone about our little deal; I've got enough problems with the Galactic Council as it is.
Start: How does <Money> cr sound? In our system, all pirates command everyone's respect, and that includes you. But who could have known that it would come back to bite us in the ass, <Player>! See, there's a long-standing pirate clan that has assumed the name of the <FromStar> star system. That's right -- that's the name they go by. And now the Galactic Council has put a bounty on their heads. We've been trying to convince those boys to lay low for a while, but it's no use.

So we've decided to force the issue and fight fire with fire, so to speak. If the local pirates refuse to play nice, they must be forced to play nice, and that's where you come in. Make sure no civilian ship dies in this system until <Date>. And as soon as the Galactic Council's audit of our system is over, everything will go back to normal. Full speed ahead!

GenericCongratCoal: Sorry for telling you that, <Player>, but while you were busy doing the quest, some coup d'etat had happened and now our planet is under Coalition control, again. However, we respect an agreement, even it was signed by some pirates behind our back, so you will get <Money> cr. you earned.
GenericCongratPirate: Wow-wow, the <Player> buddy! Didn't expect to see pirates here, don't you? Yeah, it's an anxious time now, so we have to rule this place instead of Coalition. But don't be a chicken, our boys always keep their word, so we'll pay you <Money> cr., even if we doesn't give a Klissan about your quest.

Info.CountDay: There are <Day> days left to complete the mission

CurQuests.Accepted: Mission completed, time to collect the fee

0.End: Yes, excellent! The <Ship> pirate is destroyed! It is warriors like you who are the pillars of our noble maloq race. And let this be a lesson to all of this swamp scum! On behalf of the maloq army, I hereby reward you with <Money> cr. It's yours!
0.Start: Fearless <Player>! I order you to destroy the brazen peleng pirate ship <Ship>. That jerk stole a large batch of kitchen stools for export and slipped away without so much as paying for parking! My government will not tolerate such shenanigans from the pelengs, is that clear? You will find him in the <InStar> system. The maloqs demand that the order be completed by <Date>, otherwise he may escape and you will not get your <Money> cr. I did mention that you are entitled to this fee if the operation is successful, did I not?

1.End: Well, <Player>, I trust <FullShip> is destroyed? Not bad for a merchant! In fact, it was pretty good for a warrior! So, what do you think? Note your compensation -- a nifty sum of <Money> cr! See, the result is the same, but the work is much more exciting than pushing all sorts of trash.
Start: Say, <Player>, are you a merchant or something? Then get the hell out of my sight!

Then again, the order is important, and we have no one else to assign it to, so listen up. There was a peleng here recently who duped us into buying a whole box of ragobam bullfrog saliva for a whole lot of money. Why? He claimed that the poison from these bullfrogs can inspire maloq hearts with courage. Soon after a group of human linguists arrived and explained what exactly he meant by "inspiring courage." Turns out he was indirectly calling us cowards! Argh!!!
Here are your orders: destroy -- yes-yes, destroy! -- this insolent pup along with his ship <Ship>. The order must be completed by <Date>. We're even willing to pay you <Money> cr for your work.
Wha? Where to look for him? Drop by the information center and use the search window -- duh!

End: And here are the winners of the bloodiest peleng show: <clr>Kill or Lose<clrEnd>! In first place is the ranger who has garnered renown in all the galactic systems -- <Player>! He is awarded the main prize of <Money> cr for annihilating <FullShip> with extreme prejudice! Bravo!
Stay tuned for further developments -- only on Peleng Broadcasting Network!
Start: Do you know where you are, <Player>? What, you really don't?! You're on the most thrilling peleng show of the century -- <clr>Kill or Lose!<clrEnd> -- with millions watching us as we speak! The rules are as follows: several ships across the Galaxy are issued an order to destroy a particular ship. Naturally, the quarry fights back to the bitter end; rules are rules, however, and nothing can be done about that. So if you haven't got the guts to partake in such a... specialized game, you can turn right around and hit the road.

Still here? Then I'll take that to mean you're interested. Let's continue. Your target will be a ship called <FullShip>, currently adrift in the <InStar> system. Find and destroy it before <Date>, and the main prize of <Money> cr will be yours! The show is simple, but extremely popular on all peleng planets. So, can we count on you as a contestant?

End: You accomplished the mission just fine, <Player>, there's just one little problem... Crimson Skull wasn't aboard <Ship>. In fact, there was never an escape in the first place: the poor sod simply collapsed from exhaustion while working out in the gym. They found him this morning under the dumbbell rack -- a bit drowsy but very much alive!

Anyway, we've decided to reduce your reward to <Money> cr. And if you have a problem with that, we will leak the fact that you've destroyed a civilian vessel. Now we'll go our separate ways and never speak of this again! Until the next time we require your services, naturally. Which should happen sooner rather than later.
Start: Say, <Player>, would you be interested in a delicate assignment worthy of a middling lyakusha? A criminal named <clr>Crimson Skull<clrEnd>, grandnephew of Red Skull, the legendary bandit in the times of the Antiklissan War, has recently escaped from one of our prisons. We have a simple method of dealing with runaway criminals -- liquidation. Besides, Skull is too dangerous to mess around with.

According to our data, he has captured passenger spaceliner <Ship> and is currently headed to the <InStar> system. The matter is sensitive and we wouldn't like it if it became public; but then, the reward will exceed your wildest expectations. Try to complete the mission in the next <Day> days; upon missing the deadline, the mission will be canceled and we will deny everything even if you manage to destroy the target.

End: Indeed, <Player>, you've outdone yourself this time; the <Ship> transport is no more. So, how about getting your <Money> cr? We'll have you know, this time the earnings are totally legit. If you want it, here you go.

By the way, any interest in buying some counterfeit cash? The rate is ten fakes against one real cred. What, conscience won't let you? Then buy yourself a moral ambiguity permit and call it a day! Show your business sense, ranger!
Start: Sure, you can always count on getting work from us! A report came in to the authorities that a certain transport named <Ship> is carrying a large amount of counterfeit money, printed without the required permit. The ship must be eliminated. What, you're not a fan of such radical measures? Too bad, 'cause the peleng government doesn't negotiate with counterfeiters.

We turn to you, <Player>, as a pilot who truly knows business! Rid us of this arrogant fool. Teach the counterfeiters that working without a license and not using the image of Supreme Lyakusha <clr>Bukhus<clrEnd> on their fakes will not be tolerated! You can do it justice or for a reward of <Money> cr, that's up to you.

Check the current location of the ship in the search window of the information center. I could have looked it up myself, but the service costs money, albeit not too much. And you know that we pelengs are the thriftiest race in the Galaxy! Far be it from me to soil the good name of my people... Right, <Player>?

End: Excellent work, <Player>! However, we kind of screwed up the target. The ship you destroyed was no experimental drone, but a regular liner with a pilot and passengers on board. Still, you've accomplished your mission with such grace that we cannot help but reward such a beautiful display of skill. You have been paid a total of <Money> cr!

Quite often an accidental mistake that leads to irreversible consequences is worth three planned mistakes! You're on the right track and have a very bright future. Believe my word as a seasoned peleng.
Start: Dearest <Player>, have you heard anything about the new contraband tax introduced on human planets? It is outrageous! Those humans are trying to drive honest peleng entrepreneurs out of business.

Traders from planet <FromPlanet> have decided to stage a large-scale demonstration against this unfounded tax. We will start by blowing up the diplomatic ship <Ship>, property of some human fat cat. It is currently in the <InStar> system. This is a top-of-the-line experimental ship piloted by a robot, so there won't be blood on your hands. Yes, your hands, because you have been chosen to execute the people's will, <Player>! You will be our instrument of revenge in the struggle for honest business!!! Accomplish the mission by <Date> and we will pay you a fee of <Money> cr on your return.

End: Wonderful, simply wonderful, <Player>! You have eliminated a hatchball club that were cup favorites this season, as they were aboard a charter flight on liner <Ship>.
With the competition out of the way, the championship will finally be ours! And <Money> cr -- yours. Oh, how sweet you are, the intoxicating aroma of imminent victory!
Start: Hey, <Player>! Have you respect for justice? If so, then we have a job for you! Also, it pays <Money> cr. There is a ship -- <FullShip> -- which looks like your regular liner... But in reality, it is a space casino called the Golden Peleng. The ship is docked in the spaceport of our planet <FromPlanet>, but the owner was never granted a gambling license! Nor does he intend to apply for one, as far as our sources are concerned.

Can you even imagine the losses our treasury department is suffering? Have you seem the stakes at a roulette table?? Folks die for a lot less money every day. Yes, you heard right, this offense calls for much more than a slap on the wrist. We demand the liner's total destruction! It is currently on course through the <InStar> system. Now go, do your duty as a peleng! And don't tarry -- the mission must be completed by <Date>.

End: The Gaalian oveon <Ship> is eliminated! Jolly good, <Player>! What goes around, comes around! We have already transferred the <Money> cr to your account.

By the way, I was thinking the other day that the gaal really did manage to make money from air. Does this mean he was right all along? Did he teach the young pelengs a clever trick? I must say, the gaal sure has an interesting teaching method... Or rather, "had." Darn, maybe we should have taken him alive???
Start: So, <Player>, what is your opinion on gaals? Me, I just can't stomach them -- there's something about our two races that don't mix...

I'm sure you know what I mean. On the whole, gaals are queer and shadowy figures, and occasionally even barefaced liars. Several days ago we had a visitor -- a gaal who introduced himself as a famous hypnotist <clr>Gaan Chewack<clrEnd>. He held a mass hypnosis show for our youth, promising to instill the young minds with knowledge in spheres of trade and making money from thin air. But instead the hypnotized pelengs voluntarily submitted their wallets and jewelry to the swindler. He even had to hire an entire transport vessel named <Ship> to carry away the loot!

What's the world coming to, <Player>, when gaals make fools of pelengs in the light of day? This makes us feel very, very angry! Destroy! Destroy this fraud! We will spare no expense to put this grave insult behind us by <Date>. <Day> days of work, and the <Money> cr is yours. What do you say? Say yes and don't give it another thought!
Oh yes, you can look up the ship's location in the information center's search window. You would never have figured that out, eh?

16.End: Damn right, <Player>, good job! May space rest lightly on this drug counterfeiter and the entire crew of <FullShip>. If everybody were as effective as you, the peleng race would have ruled the universe long ago. And here's your <Money> cr.
Start: Service, <Player>! Or rather, service and money! There's an underground lab manufacturing synthetic narcotics aboard <Ship>. Not only is the owner synthesizing narcotic substances without a license, he's distributing them outside the state's official network of pharmacies! And that means he's dodging taxes and doesn't contribute to the common fund. And if all that weren't enough, he sells his drugs at a price far below the government's, further compromising demand for our production. Isn't that just terrible?

But here's where your talents come in. You can eliminate this self-proclaimed entrepreneur now that we've been able track down his location, which is the <InStar> system. We're prepared to pay you <Money> cr, but only under the condition that his ship <Ship> is liquidated within <Day> days. If you fail to complete the mission by this date, we will be forced to contract another, more capable pilot. Well, <Player>, what are you waiting for?

End: There you go, <Player>, excellent! Great job! That pathetic excuse for a ranger flying <Ship> is no longer a threat to the purity of our race!
I hope that no other peleng will ever attempt to follow in the footsteps of this impostor, this chameleon who has besmirched the good name of our people. Take your <Money> cr for a job well done!
Start: It's good to see that Ranger <Player> is always willing to help advance the peleng cause. Would you like to know how you can further the great cause this time? Of course you would! And we won't keep you waiting!

A certain peleng named <clr>Jokh Puk<clrEnd> has gotten so obsessed with gaalian fairy tales that he ended up joining their stupid astral religion and started touring the peleng planets, proselytizing and calling for purity and harmony. It's outrageous! He went as far as changing his ship, his name and his race in order to look more gaalian... Hell, he even joined the rangers in order to fight for peace and harmony in space! We judge his behavior to be a betrayal of peleng values -- indeed, the infidel must be punished with extreme prejudice!

<Player>, would you be so kind as to find this peleng pretender and turn him into... Well, use your imagination! He is currently a ranger on ship <Ship>, posing as a gaal, though deep inside he is the foulest kind of peleng. As for his current location, you can look that up in the information center's search window. You have <Day> days to finish the job. After that, we don't want to see or hear from him ever again. For your efforts you will earn a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Bravo, bravo! We have taught those militarist maloqs a good lesson, namely that it pays to learn the difference between a space billboard and a practice target! This ain't no firing range! But this will cool their jets, no doubt about it. Seeing <Ship> eliminated will show them to play by the rules.

Oh yes, I almost forgot. Please take your fee of <Money> cr, courtesy of <clr>Streemers<clrEnd>. What is more, you will grace the cover of our <clr>Streemness Weekly<clrEnd> magazine as the official new face of our practice tar... I mean space billboard.
Start: <Player>, listen to this illuminative story. Our advertising agency called <clr>Streemers<clrEnd> has come up with a wonderful marketing tool -- giant billboard hanging in the upper strata of the atmosphere, showing off the finest goods of peleng economy. These billboards have already brought planet <FromPlanet> millions of credits in revenue.

The problem is, recently some maloq ships have started flying into our <FromStar> system and shooting down the billboards. Apparently, they remind those brutes of practice targets! The maloqs have even begun staging special shooting contests. How absolutely insufferable! We took down the name of one of the ships -- it is called <FullShip>. Head out there and take him down to teach the rest a lesson. If you can manage that within the next <Day> days, you'll earn <Money> cr. Not a bad payday for interesting and simple work, right?

Only first you will have to drop by the information center and verify the scalawag's current location in the search window. I'm sure you understand that I can't be bothered with such trivialities. Time is money, ranger, time is money!

19.End: And that's that, <Player>! <Ship> is no more, and the same goes for the hoodlums it was carrying. You know, we have nothing against against the occasional tomfoolery, but there are limits! Unfortunately, maloqs and limits just don't mix. I do hope others will learn from this, however. As for you, you have earned yourself a reward of <Money> cr. Hurray!
Start: <Player>, are you familiar with maloq tourists? No? Well, let me tell you exactly what they are. They are maloq tourists! They come to our planet, pitch training camps near our cities and start causing so much havoc that it makes the Third Peleng War look like child's play! And if ruining our forests and swamps and making racket day and night weren't enough, they're also terrorizing the surrounding populace by recruiting them into their gladiator battles.

Last year we ended up deporting an especially rowdy group of maloq tourists, but we've just heard that they're planning on coming back to our planet soon. Nuh-uh, not on my watch! It's time to put an end to this madness once and for all! The maloq tourists are aboard a liner called <Ship>, which is currently refueling in the <InStar> system. You must make sure that we never see them again on our planet. I trust my meaning is clear? Let's hope so. <Day> days ought to be enough to take care of it. If you succeed, we will pay you <Money> cr.

End: Ah, <Player>, you're back to collect on the contract for that sorry excuse for a diplomat <Ship>!

And I've just had a chat with our scientists. It turns out maloqs descend from ferocious guanto-bartabanas, and humans from monkeys. And that puny human had the gall to call me a stupid monkey! Anywho, you've completed my orders and are due <Money> cr. Here you go.

I plan on visiting one of the human planets shortly. I'll make sure to pay a visit to the local government and call them all monkeys! And if they start arguing, I'll just show them the excerpt from the "History of the Galactic Races."
Start: Say, <Player>, what is your view of diplomacy? Yeah, I don't much like it either. Allow me to illustrate my point. Yesterday a certain human ambassador named <clr>Billy Portnoy<clrEnd> called me a scumbag and a hairy monkey and vowed to wash his boots in my bathtub! Argh!!!

If it weren't for his diplomatic immunity and fifteen bodyguards, I would have ended him right then and there! Now, we can handle the bodyguards' corpses, but you must go to the <InStar> system and track down <FullShip> -- that's where that... creature is hiding out. I want him dead. Eliminate Portnoy by <Date>, but the sooner the better! What are you waiting for? Execute! The bounty on his head is <Money> cr!

End: Yesss! Yesss! That was excellent, <Player>! Unfortunately, our sources were mistaken -- that wasn't a garbage ship you destroyed, but some other vessel. Oh well, it's still one gaalian ship less, so let's call it a victory.
And this <Money> cr is yours for a job well done! Are you as happy as we are, <Player>?
20.Start: Listen here, <Player>. We assume you know that gaals worship cleanliness and abhor garbage. Well, as it happens, a gaalian garbage ship called <Ship> is currently in the <InStar> system, carrying trash to a recycling plant. What does it all mean? Only that we've got an excellent opportunity to play a little prank. Blow that vessel to hell, and the garbage will be scattered all over the system! Can you even imagine a better prank? Us neither! And we'll even throw you some money! But please try to complete the job within <Day> days or we'll have to hire another pilot.

End: Attaboy, <Player>! <FullShip> is terminated, along with its pilot, and our boss' honor has been restored.
We knew we could rely on you for a clean kill. And here's your <Money> cd, which you've rightfully earned.
Start: Dearest <Player>, what do you know about the mafia? Nothing? What about the maloq mafia? What do you mean, it doesn't exist? It certainly does exist -- yesterday's events have confirmed this. Picture to yourself our mafiosos... err, I mean our party leaders, headed by Prime Minister Don Pelengon, sitting around a table in the government building of planet <FromPlanet>... Just sitting, eating, not bothering anyone. When some music comes on, the bosses go out into the hall to dance, stretch their bones a bit. And then all of a sudden a maloq appears out of nowhere, removes all the eDough credit cards from the bosses' costumes, steals all the ceremonial silverware, drinks all the muddy liquor, and disappears!

Have you ever seen such impudence? I'll tell you one thing -- we refuse to tolerate such behavior here on planet <FromPlanet>. That maloq trickster will be brought to justice! Besides, it's pretty clear he was an agent of the maloq mafia, sent here to humiliate our... err... political officials. This is a challenge, and our response must be swift! Track down this deceiver (I suggest using the search window of the information center) and get rid of him by <Date>, and a fee of <Money> cr will be yours. Oh, his ship is called <FullShip>... Pah, these maloqs, no imagination at all!

22.End: Diplomatic ship <Ship> is no more, and we are happy to award you this fee of <Money> cr. Glory to planet <FromPlanet> and its unbending and omnipresent justice system!
Start: Esteemed <Player>, would you be available to assist in upholding the law? A faeyan computer tech specialist named <clr>Bale Gun<clrEnd> has been sentenced to death by our planet's court for aiding and abetting a group of maloq smugglers, among them agents for the tech giant Maloqosoft, notorious for manipulating the computer market. The subject has been charged and convinced on several counts under the Criminal Code. He has been stripped of his diplomatic status and declared persona non grata on all faeyan planets, and still he continues his illicit dealings.

Ranger <Player>, being the hardened warrior that you are, we propose that you execute the bench warrant and bring the subject to justice. He is presently aboard the diplomatic ship <Ship>. Apparently, he thinks that it will keep him safe. The warrant expires on <Date>, but we don't anticipate you'll have any problems completing this mission before the deadline passes. A fee of <Money> cr shall be transferred to your account immediately after.

Hmm, I had the system the subject had been spotted in last written down somewhere around here... Can't find it. No matter, you can look it up yourself at the information center; I trust you know how to use the search window?

End: Excellent, <Player>, simply excellent! Once again you were on top of your game in liquidating <Ship>!
Planet <FromPlanet>'s Department of Justice is happy to compensate you with <Money> cr. In the name of Justice!
Start: Planet <FromPlanet> is in need of a combat pilot with the nerves of steel. Not long ago on our planet we took part in joint military exercises together with the maloq armed forces. The maloq side was represented by two ships. It wasn't until well into the exercise that it became clear that one of the maloq vessels wasn't firing blanks, but actual rounds. As a result, two of our military ships were destroyed. As the investigation went on to show, the ship was piloted by a maloq named <clr>Jazzy Hoodlum<clrEnd>, the infamous maloq pirate. Somehow he had managed to secure a permit to take part in the exercise, and, by all appearances, this was his idea of a prank. It took our court here on planet <FromPlanet> only two sessions to reach a unanimous verdict: guilty without the right to appeal.

Ranger <Player>, we hereby offer you a fee of <Money> cr to execute the judgment of the court by tracking down and terminating Hoodlum, wherever he may be. At this time he's using the ship <Ship> to carry out terrorist operations in the <InStar> system. You are given a term of <Day> days to complete this special operation.

End: On behalf of planet <FromPlanet>'s investigative and judicial bodies, please accept our sincerest gratitude for carrying out the judgment for us, <Player>.
A sum of <Money> cr has been transferred to your account. May you stay pure in thoughts and well within the bounds of the law!
24.Start: Dear <Player>, at the present time all we have is a contract to execute a court order, specifically a death sentence. If you've been following the news, you should know that <clr>Caney Meatnock<clrEnd>, the famous hacker who has managed to break into Galanet and steal data from the Galactic Council's main server, has been found guilty and sentenced to capital punishment by the Supreme Court of planet <FromPlanet>. The sentence was issued in absentia, seeing as the defendant had skipped court and was last seen in the <InStar> system aboard a pirate ship named <Ship>, poorly disguised as a passenger liner. The recompense for this job is <Money> cr, provided it is completed within <Day> days.

End: On behalf of planet <FromPlanet>'s special services, we thank you, <Player>. You may be a pirate, but today you've done us a great service.
We cannot give you a medal for obvious reasons, but the promised sum of <Money> cr is being transferred to your account as we speak.
Start: Criminal subject <Player>, we have something of a delicate matter to discuss with you, and we count on your discretion henceforth. It should be noted, however, that we have quite the dossier on you, and any unnecessary actions on your part may well end up with you serving the rest of your life in prison. If we still have your interest, then listen up.

The gaalian scientists have synthesized a new narcotic, one that's extremely potent and cheap to produce, calling it <clr>Astroin<clrEnd>. The research was conducted aboard a scientific designation vessel <Ship>. So high is our interest in this research, particularly its medical and military applications, that after lengthy negotiations we've managed to secure limited shipments of Astroin for study.

But there is a problem: somehow the pelengs have learned about a defenseless vessel carrying a batch of drugs, and have already dispatched a crew to intercept it. The risk of pelengs getting their hands on a super-potent and cheap narcotic is so great that we have no choice but to take extreme, though fully justified measures -- liquidating the entire ship. You can imagine how serious we consider this threat to be... This is our last resort.

You should further understand that the executing agent can in no way be traced back to us, lest we become mired in an epic scandal. That is why we come to you -- a pilot with the reputation of a pirate. If you do it, it won't arouse any suspicions. What is more, you will become <Money> cr richer! Think fast, for time is a factor and we expect this business to be over with before <Date>; we just cannot wait any longer.
You can find out the exact location of the target ship in the search window of the information center.

26.End: You have been a great help to the environment, <Player>! I hope you didn't forget to pick up the valuable goods that fell out of the poacher's ship? What do you mean, there wasn't anything there? Ah, I see now, you've kept it for yourself. I suppose your courage has merited a couple of hides as a bonus to this official reward of <Money> cr. Still, you mustn't let greed get the better of you. Living nature is invaluable for all the races of the Galaxy, and the sooner we all understand it, the better!
Start: Allow me to brief you on the materials of a certain criminal case. Several days ago our environmental services picked up the trail of a faeyan poacher who has been killing off rare species of animals in planet <FromPlanet>'s National Park. By the time we discovered his handiwork the bandit had managed to procure and unload over one hundred hides of rare horned antelopes and about 100 kilos of redbellied elephant tusks. As per new environmental legislation of our planet, this kind of extreme poaching is punishable by death. The identity and guilt of the criminal have been confirmed in absentia over two court sessions. Unfortunately, the poacher escaped aboard <Ship> and is currently headed for the <InStar> system, where, according to our reports, he's continuing to sell his illicit goods.

<Player>, if you agree to become our instrument of justice and accomplish this mission within <Day> days, starting from today, we shall pay you a total of <Money> cr from planet <FromPlanet>'s environmental protection fund. Naturally, the Green Party will also be eternally grateful.

27.End: We are happy to observe the fervor with which pirates strive to uphold the letter of the law. As for you, <Player>, you've completed the mission most excellently! We commend your efforts and encourage them with a payment of <Money> cr. And here a note validating your reduced future prison sentence. Simply present it to a judge the next time you're facing trial.
Start: Pirate <Player>! We invite you to take part in a special event called Pirates Supporting the Law, organized by our law enforcement for correctional purposes. Each pirate completed mission upholding law and order will translate to their prison sentence being reduced by one year. Besides, this is a paid job, so it must be of interest to just about any ranger.

The story is simple and even a bit comical. After losing all of their money at one of our casinos, a group of pelengs (space pirates, as it turned out) subsequently robbed it. Many innocent bystanders, as well as some law enforcement agents, were harmed. The robbers have escaped the planet and are currently hiding from the law aboard a pirate ship named <Ship>. According to unverified reports, they are currently in the <InStar> system, terrorizing all vessels flying through it. We propose that you be our instrument of justice and dole out retribution, i.e. the death sentence for their crimes. This must be done by <Date>; after this date, tracking them will become very difficult. We will compensate you for your time with a fee of <Money> cr.

28.End: Ranger, I hereby declare your mission to liquidate Ranger <Ship> -- the culprit behind potential political turmoil -- completed as per the provisions of our contract. The agreed upon fee of <Money> cr has been transferred to your account.
Start: Ranger, please try to focus on the following set of facts and make the necessary analytical connections to make sense of them. Two days ago our planet was visited by a maloq ambassador to negotiate a contract under which two hundred maloq persons would be delivered here to perform various tasks of unskilled labor. Upon completing the negotiations, the ambassador met his death before he could even leave the stratosphere of planet <FromPlanet>, terminated by Ranger <Ship> -- a well-known opponent of exploitation of persons and animals.

Though we planned to simply to ignore the incident, the maloq side demanded that the ranger be punished by death or they would declare war on the entire fae civilization. We have no interest in exasperating the current political situation, so we've agreed to this measure in an effort to preserve the stability between our two nations, unequal as they may be in their intellectual development.

You, <Player>, are charged with this difficult, yet fully justified mission. Track down the current location of Ranger <Ship> (use the search window in the information center), and eliminate him by <Date>. Upon successful completion of this task, your account will be credited with a sum of <Money> cr as recompense from the faeyan government.

29.End: Ranger <Player>, <clr>T-101<clrEnd> has been successfully eliminated, and your contribution duly acknowledged. As per the terms of the contract, you will be paid <Money> cr for your assistance in the war against the dominators.
Start: At a recent session of the Guild Quorum, it has been concluded that the dominators' technological advances have surpassed our initial projections by 27.6%. According to the latest reports, the robots have completed the development of a new <clr>T-101<clrEnd> android model, which is visually indistinguishable from a human being. The android model killed a human ranger piloting <Ship> and seized his ship, then began to engage in sabotage activities under the guise of a ranger. You must be aware of the fact that this pretend-ranger is actually a new generation dominator android. If you eliminate the android and its ship within <Day> days, the government of planet <FromPlanet> will reward you with <Money> cr.
The current whereabouts of the ship can be retrieved via the information center's search window.

End: Mission accomplished Your fee is <Money> cr. Now let's close the file: <FullShip> has been terminated by a pirate named <Player>, working for the <clr>"Friends For-less-than-ever"<clrEnd> agency.
That reminds us -- we also need to hire a decent accountant to keep the books for us. 'Cause right now it all looks like gibberish.
Start: Following the peleng lead, we maloqs have opened up an assassination agency, calling it <clr>"Friends For-less-than-ever"<clrEnd>. Rich folk are always ordering hits, so why not give us the work? Still, we don't want to botch our first order, so we'd rather outsource it to a real pro. And learn from his actions. You're an infamous pirate, so you can teach us how to make money in this business.

Anyway, the job pays <Money> cr, and the target is a trader flying aboard <Ship>. Naturally, we cannot disclose any information pertaining to the client or their reasons for ordering the hit. All you need to know is that you've got until <Date>. Should you accept the job, look for the ship in the <InStar> system. Ride on, <Player>!

End: We've received information that the smuggling ship <Ship> has been successfully terminated. A total of <Money> cr has been transferred to your account.

Should you ever encounter the pirated copies of our nanorobots, rest assured that their functions are minimal and their service period will conclude after a month's time. No amount of hacks or code generators will ever make them fully functional.
Start: <Player>, we wish to inform you that progressive faeyan technologies have encountered aggressive competition from primitive maloq pseudo-technologies and reactionary economic model. Our scholars from <FromPlanet> have devised a molecular microprogram, enabling the construction of new types of nanorobots. However, the ship transporting the first shipment of robots to the planet where testing was scheduled to be conducted was captured by a maloq pirate ship named <Ship>, known for its smuggling activity. Our sources say that the maloqs are planning on utilizing their outdated technology of solid-state nanocopying to begin production of counterfeit copies of our nanorobots.

The consortium of advanced technologies of planet <FromPlanet> hereby assigns the mission to terminate the ship <Ship> to you, <Player>. By the way, the vessel's current location is in the <InStar> system. Upon completing the operation by <Date> you will be paid a reward of <Money> cr.

31.End: We were extremely saddened to watch the demise of the innocent crew and passengers aboard <Ship>, but this decision was necessitated by the bigger picture -- preserving sentient life in the entire universe. In fact, we intend to be just as decisive and uncompromising going forward. Please take this payment of <Money> cr for helping us to carry out these sanitary measures.
Start: Ranger, I want you to familiarize yourself with a series of facts that I intend to present to you! As an erudite individual, you're probably aware of hyperleprosy -- an illness of unknown origin that attacks organic life forms in hyperspace. The infection stays latent in the host body for a number of years, whereupon it commences a phase of active mutation, resulting in the death of the host and all surrounding organics. Until recently, this highly contagious and as-of-yet incurable disease has led to the eradication of whole planets. I say recently because literally a few days ago the brilliant faeyan minds have come up with a solution. We have developed a scanner that allows for remote detection of infected passengers aboard any given spaceship.

In order to protect the Galaxy's healthy population from outbreaks of hyperleprosy, we intend to act swiftly and decisively. We have discovered that passengers aboard the liner <FullShip>, which exited hyperspace in the <InStar> system, have become infected. You, <Player>, are tasked with destroying this ship at any cost. You are given <Day> days to complete this sanitary operation, whereupon you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr. We hope you understand the tremendous significance of this mission.

End: Our psychoanalytical mediums have confirmed the successful liquidation of the aforementioned dangerous weapon. Levels of psy-energy in the surrounding systems are back to normal.
Based on this information, we are fully justified in paying you, <Player>, a monetary reward of <Money> cr.
Start: We have a mission of critical importance for Ranger <Player>. Our psychoanalytical mediums have registered a splash of psy-energy in the vicinity of the <InStar> system. A more detailed investigation has revealed that a ship named <FullShip>, currently flying through the system, is transporting an unknown type of ultra-long-range psychotropic weapon. Unfortunately, we were unable to ascertain the vessel's trajectory, nor the purpose for which the weapon is being transported. We are, however, privy to certain data that indirectly proves the aggressive intentions of its owners; this theory is further solidified by the fact that this ship has not been officially registered at any port, and that the ship's captain has refused to state its point of designation.
