Ranger, if your intellectual potential allows you to assess this situation in the context of potential and probably outcomes, you will easily characterize it as critical. The only right decision in this situation is the physical liquidation of the vessel, together with its hazardous load. We hope you understand this, and thus we entrust the mission to you. Use whatever means you have at your disposal to exterminate the threat to the safety of <InStar> and surrounding systems. Provided that this mission is accomplished by <Date>, you will be rewarded with a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Unfortunately, <Player>, in this particular case the positive factor ended up on top. According to an updated report, the passengers aboard <FullShip> weren't terrorists, but regular persons who had recently consumed typical maloq food...

Alas, our control systems are presently incapable of differentiating between traditional maloq food and chemical agents. We hope that you will keep mum about this incident, and we're happy to credit your account <Money> cr to solidify this understanding. Please accept our apologies.
Start: Here is the situation. A certain passenger ship marked <FullShip> has begun visiting our system at a frequency which greatly exceeds normal; naturally, this drew suspicion at our statistics agency. Upon scanning the vessel with biological control scanners we've detected an unknown and potentially poisonous substance inside the passengers' digestive tracts. Our calculations place the probability of the substance being a new biological weapon, "muled" in special containers inside the terrorists, at 68.3%.

Such a significant preponderance in favor of a negative factor leave us with no room for hesitation. You, <Player>, shall be tasked with eliminating the aforementioned <Ship>, along with all its passengers. We hope that you understand the full gravity and criticality of the situation. <Date> is the latest date we expect the successful conclusion of your mission by all the means at your disposal. Your compensation shall total <Money> cr, payable by the faeyan government.
The location of the liner can be verified via the search window in the information center. I trust your intellectual capacity is sufficient to carry out simple operations such as this?

End: Thank you for your assistance concerning <Ship>, Ranger <Player>.
Please try to understand our point of view. Any spiritual literature must be sanctified, lest it can carry only negative energy.
And here's <Money> cr for your services to further spiritual purity in the universe.
Start: Seeing your ardor in the fight for justice is an inspiring sight, <Player>! Wondering how you can serve these higher ideals at this given moment? Well, we dare not keep you waiting. We have just become aware of a pirate ship called <Ship> disseminating fake spiritual gaalian literature in the <InStar> system. What is more, our works have been woefully mistranslated into Common Galactic. We deem such conduct absolutely reprehensible.
As such, as want to pay you a sum of <Money> cr for destroying this deplorable literature by <Date>. If the terms are clear, then Godspeed, and may your intentions be pure.

35.End: A brilliant conclusion to a difficult and regretful mission! We were certain that you would succeed, for the purity of our mutual cosmic home is key to everybody's safety and prosperity. Sad as it is, this lofty ideal often necessitates such cruel measures. Dear <Player>, know that we share your grief over the peleng pilot's untimely departure, though it was his own imprudence that brought about his demise. We hope that this fee of <Money> cr will be of some solace.
Start: We've received reports that a certain peleng pirate is piloting <Ship> -- a ship with such an outdated engine that it bears an ancient inscription, "Made in China." To our great sorrow, this engine retches ungodly amounts of pollution into our virgin-clean space. We have sent several notices to this individual and even offered a new ship at a discounted price, but he refuses to compromise.

Alas, we have no other recourse but to rid the universe of his physical presence. <Player>, you must consider the very real possibility of polluted space -- an ominous specter hanging over all the developed worlds! What is to become of our Galaxy if others choose to follow the lead of one ignorant lyakusha? I can see indignation springing up inside you! May this righteous feeling drive you to carry out this difficult mission. The ship must be taken care of by <Date>, and we are prepared to pay you a sum of <Money> cr to do it.
To find out which part of space the pirate is currently polluting, please use the search window in our information center.

End: The Great Convent and the entire gaalian race grieve the death of the peleng ambassador, whose own imprudence and stubbornness have led to his downfall. Thank you for sharing in our troubles, now it is time for us to share in yours.

This <Money> cr will help you solve any material problems you may have. Whilst you may quench your spiritual thirst by reading our literature, <Player>. May the omnipresent purity of space be your savior!
Start: You, <Player>, are a guest on our planet, and the laws of hospitality dictate that you must share in our troubles, as we share in yours. As you know, the gaalian race exemplifies a world of peace and harmony -- such is the duty of every citizen unbereft of inner wisdom. However, sometimes certain regretful incidents require that we act more forcefully for the common good.

It is common knowledge that our shortsighted peleng friends are using all manner of espionage devices, most of them primitive in nature, to try and steal our technological advancements. And no, we have no intention of keeping these technologies secret, especially since an awful lot of them are already common throughout the Galaxy. There are exceptions, however; some of the technologies, especially of the military variety, are too powerful to be trusted to less developed races. Sadly, one such technology has recently been stolen by a peleng ambassador, whose ship <Ship> is currently drifting in the <InStar> system. When we proposed that he either return the stolen information or destroy it, he refused us.

Sad as it is, we have no other choice but to terminate this ship for the sake of saving the Galaxy. This sacred mission is entrusted upon you -- our friend and colleague. <Date> is the deadline for justice to prevail. We also intend to pay you a fee of <Money> cr as soon as the operation is completed.

End: Hello, uncle? Brace yourself, I have bad news for you. Your son's ship was shot down by some ranger by the name of <Player>. Uncle? Are you all right?!
Oh, yes, Ranger <Player>! I knew I could rely on you. What a marvelous job you did! The stuff of legends!
Believe it or not, I am a millionaire now. How about a glass of Civilian Backwater? That's my favorite cocktail.

You don't want them? Then here is your fee of <Money> cr. I'd be happy to pay you more, but a contract is a contract. I hope you understand. By the way, if I were you, I'd tread very carefully now since the uncle's bodyguards must have heard your name real well.
Start: ...what a character! That formidable look alone speaks volumes! A great specimen all around...
So, what was I talking about? Oh, the mission, yes. We have an easy little mission for you.

You see, I am very fond of my uncle. He used to have quite a name among the pirates -- the real scourge of all merchants and diplomats. But he has already left the business. He is deservedly retired now, so to speak, he-he, which isn't much of a surprise, not with the three extra holes in his head.

And as it often happens with senile millionaires, all of a sudden we have had us some sleazy character springing out of nowhere and claiming he is his direct heir. However, you and I, we both know it well that yours truly is the man's only legitimate heir. Unfortunately, after yet another unsubstantiated accusation, uncle's heart got the better of him. He now remains connected to a respirator at the Galaxy's best hospital. He just can't be bothered when he is like that. So we'll need to take care of this business in a very discrete manner.
You have <Day> days to terminate that presumptuous bastard. If <Ship> is destroyed in time, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr.

38.End: Congratulations, <Player>! You have accomplished your mission, and, what is even more important, kept quiet about it. Truth be told though, we shouldn't have taken offense at the great Maarodi. The company he has founded is still in business and throws off quite a bit of cash for its shareholders. But anyway, it's no use crying over spilled milk now. On the other hand, the government will now be able to take over the firm since its owner is dead. But that's no concern of yours. Here is your <Money> cr, and make an about face.
38.Start: <Player>, have you ever been cheated? Neither have we, since everyone knows maloqs cannot be cheated. We are just too smart for that. However, some time ago this gaal surfaced on our planet promising untold riches to anyone who would buy the shares of MMM -- Maloq Micromodules. Many maloqs trusted this Maarodi enough to give him all their hard-earned savings. But instead of living up to his promises, he took the money, boarded the ship <Ship> and ran. Besides, he has recently bought his way into the legislative assembly and now enjoys immunity from prosecution. Not that something like that would stop a ranger, would it? So you will have to terminate that liar no later than <Date> because we will not be able to keep information about that incident from the press any longer. And God only knows what can happen when the entire planet learns about it. If you do the job and keep mum about it, we will pay you <Money>. Now off you go, <Player>!

End: Great! The liner has been destroyed right on time. Take these <Money> cr for your services. They come from the lyakusha's own campaign funds. You are free to go.

Err... Why campaign funds? Oh, all right, we can bring you in on it now. We have misinformed you a little since there were no contagious patients on board that liner. It was bringing two of the Supreme Lyakusha's main political opponents back from a resort, and I was ordered to take care of them. It all worked out fine, didn't it?
Start: Come on in, dear <Player>, come on in! Care for a mud bath? They are good for you and also help restore peace of mind, which is so important in our difficult times. But a bath could wait, it will come in handy later.

The Supreme Lyakusha of our planet selected you for a very sad mission. The thing is that one of the distant peleng colonies has been struck by a horrible mental disease, rectitudinous trutholovee, that makes pelengs stutter and tell nothing but the truth. Can you even imagine what a bad affliction it is for us pelengs? Originally, a hospital ship named <Ship> was sent for those afflicted, but all the doctors' efforts were for naught. In the end, the rescue team decided to quickly relocate all the colonists to planet <FromPlanet>. But, swampy scum be my judge, further research indicated that the disease was highly contagious and virtually incurable. And now the ship whose comms on top of it all are down is rapidly approaching our own planet. The Supreme Lyakusha decided that in view of the imminent danger and as a measure of last resort we have to completely destroy the <Ship>. Hurry up, <Player>, you have to destroy the ship within <Day> days or the entire population of our planet may be affected. You see, we are very much concerned about our electora... I mean the public, of course. Once you successfully complete the mission, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Yes! Watching you destroy <Ship>, packed with innocent civilians, and not even flinch was super impressive! If you think just anyone could do it, think again! Still, we maloqs need to keep fighting the good fight for the purity of our race. The cowardice gene must be rooted out with fire and steel.
And your account has increased by <Money> cr! That's your reward, in case you didn't figure it out.
Start: We maloqs don't take kindly to refugees! Just today I read a special services' dispatch, learning that thousands of our refugees have fled this planet on a liner called <Ship>. And all because another war broke out on <FromPlanet>! Pff!
We need to teach those cowards not to desert their home planet in times of danger! The ship with the refugees is currently in the <InStar> system. We order you to destroy it by <Date>. Get to it!

40.End: Greetings, <Player>! Our entire planet is in your debt! Here's your well-deserved <Money> cr. How about it, a friendly system has been attacked in the neighboring sector! We need to warn them that those are not dominators but rather pelengs in disguise, or they will follow our example and run, and surrender their planet to these rascals. We managed to learn that there's an entire gang of pirates operating, and their ships are equipped with holographic disguises. So be careful and don't fall for this ruse.
40.Start: Ranger <Player>, we have an emergency here that requires urgent expert intervention. The thing is that about a month ago a Terron equantor landed on our planet. Under the impression that the system was under attack by dominators, the population followed the Catapult plan and evacuated the planet. In the ensuing confusion, all valuables were left behind, and not even the state bank managed to evacuate the planet's treasury. The planet emptied out. It was only later that they discovered that the presumed dominator was but a peleng pirate ship, the Labean, using an electronic disguise. A gang of pelengs disembarked and stuffed their cargo bay to the brim with all kinds of loot, including, among other things, the cash from the treasury. Naturally, the ship scurried away right after that. It was only two days ago when the population began to return that we realized what a grave mistake we had made. Ranger <Player>, if you manage to destroy <Ship> and its peleng crooks with their disguises, we will pay you whatever is left in our official accounts. I am sure you could use <Money> cr. And yet another request: please do not tell anyone about this incident. Otherwise we'll be the laughing stock of the entire Galactic Council.

End: Ranger <Player>! On behalf of the entire peleng race we thank you for your service. Please accept these <Money> cr as a sign of our appreciation.

By the way, we are glad to inform you that we have found a new way to bump up our ever declining reputation. We have acquired a license to film yet another Star Wars installment in open space. We will produce our own movie showcasing pelengs at their best and poking fun at the stupid humans.

With your help, we have already filmed the first scene -- the destruction of <FullShip>. By the way, your fee has been paid out of the special effects budget that saw substantial savings. Overall, we discovered that it is so much cheaper to use documentary footage even though it doesn't look as good as those ridiculously expensive computer graphics.
Start: Oh, all right, ranger <Player>, it's good that you asked about the mission. Actually, we have this file for all kinds of dirty business that must be handled with the utmost discretion.
Let's see now... This one isn't for you, nor this other one... Oh, all right, I got it.

So here's the deal, <Player>. Have you seen the Star Wars movies? Now, what is it with me, of course you have seen them. Anyway, in the last forty episodes all those dumb imitators piggybacking on the glory of the great original director go out of their way to portray us pelengs as some kind of villains and hustlers. It may be true, but it is quite detrimental to our image and trade that have declined substantially over the past hundred years or so. Naturally, we are upset about it.

For that reason, this very moment a new installment of the Star Wars is being edited aboard <FullShip>. It's called Episode 158: The Secret of the Devious Lyuakusha. At the moment, the ship is positioned in the <InStar> system.

Ranger! We are begging you! Destroy this ship and all the material filmed prior to <Date>, and we will pay you <Money> cr. Otherwise, they will finish editing the film and release it, and our trade volume will go further down, which would be a true catastrophe.

End: Wonderful, <Player>! My only serious opponent from the opposition who could run against me to become the ruler of our planet is now dead, and the public remains none the wiser that this is my doing. Oh, you didn't understand anything, ranger? It's all right, it's even better this way. Here's your hard earned <Money> cr. Break a leg, <Ranger>!
Hey, mind your manners! I ain't no Charlie to you! Security, there's this ranger here bugging me for no good reason. Get him out of here!
Start: <Player>, don't you recognize me? We went to the Flight Academy together on planet Earth. That's me, your old buddy Charlie the Cunning, aka <Ship>. Well, I know I don't look the part, but please, I need your help.

It all started so well -- the old ruler asked me over for a visit. On my first night here, I had one too many and passed out before I knew it. In the morning, I woke up in this body. No matter how hard I tried to convince the officials that I am not what I seem to be, they did not believe me and kept saying that the real <FullShip> had left the planet late in the night. At first I was very upset about all this, but in a few weeks I grew into my new role as the ruler of <FromPlanet> quite nicely. Besides, the luxurious halls of this palace are way more comfortable than the cramped quarters of a spaceship. The job is money for nothing, and you live like a cow in clover.

But what do you know, it now appears it was the old ruler's enemies who had arranged for that mess of a body swap, and now he had come to his senses and wants to swap back. But I got used to this life, and the last thing I want is to go back to where I came from. I am prepared to pay you <Money> cr to get rid of him. At the moment, <FullShip> must be traversing the <InStar> system. Please take care of it before <Date>. Many thanks, my friend.

End: Oh, Ranger <Player>! What a glorious sight! What am I talking about? About the Criminal Galaxy program. I particularly liked the part where the ship's debris begin flying all around. That was a real sight to see.

By the way, don't be surprised if you learn that the gaals have some serious beef with you and have put a reward on your head. I simply forgot to tell you that Hex Tortionist had long since redeemed himself with his fellow countrymen and now enjoys a good enough name. Yeah, my memory ain't what it used to be.

But he had never made it right with us. We have invested so much in recruiting him, yet he never reciprocated. But now this will serve as a warning for others that we do not waste our cash or make empty threats.
By the way, here's your well-deserved <Money> cr. We pelengs can also be honest -- when it suits us. Or when there's a ranger standing over our head with a blaster gun.
Start: <Player>, what a pleasure it is to have a great warrior such as yourself visit our planet! Your victories over dominators have long become a newscast staple.
Waging battle for the freedom of our Galaxy must have cost you a pretty penny, huh? Some extra cash never hurt anyone.

In this case then, we have a proposal for you, something that needs to be handled with utmost discretion. You see, we have learned -- and we are not going to tell you how, so don't even bother asking -- that one of gaal diplomatic ships has a famous pirate for its captain -- a certain Hex Tortionist who has caused a lot of grief to our race. We suspect that not even the gaals themselves know about it since he is very cunning and resourceful.

The mission itself would be to destroy <Ship> within <Day> days. I think that when the truth finally becomes known even the galls will appreciate what you will have done. And we will pay you a fee of <Money> cr upon your return. Any objections? Alrighty then! Why are you still here?

End: Hello, <Player>. Congratulations on successfully accomplishing your mission! Don't worry, we are well aware that the container with the elements was not on board. The thing is that before you had your way with <Ship> it was attacked by pirates and had to give up its entire cargo. For that reason, even without you and I getting involved the fae would have paid us a penalty for the breach of contract, specifically, under paragraph 49(4) that provided for a timely delivery. So it now appears you got your hands -- and your good name too -- dirty for no good reason. It's all right though. What happened, happened, and there's no turning it around. But don't let this upset you. At the very least, we have one smartypants less to worry about. As a sign of our appreciation, we will transfer <Money> cr to your account.

I've been thinking that if it keeps going like this the factory may once again accumulate a decent chunk of capital, and piracy will become a legitimate cause in support of maloq battery production. So do drop in anytime, ranger!
Start: We have a mission that would fit you perfectly, <Player>! We have been watching you blatantly flaunt the law and would like to warn you that we are not particularly fond of pirates. Folks like you belong on the electric chair. Wait, where are you going? I haven't finished yet. I hope you realize that if that was what we wanted to do with you I probably wouldn't be talking to you now. The thing is that we need your help in a certain delicate matter.

I am sure you know that our race closely cooperates with the fae. What did you say? No, you guessed wrong. No, we do not want to return any broken red buttons to them and claim contractual damages. No, this is about something else. Our planet is home to the largest manufacturer of Mal-O-Chryser batteries, a market leader among similar products. However, it is not commonly known that the factory is using faeyan calponic elements that are regularly delivered via commercial carriers. Unfortunately, at the moment we do not have sufficient funds to pay for our next delivery of such elements. At the same time, we would hate to stop production. For that reason, we are forced to resort to extreme measures that are so unlike us maloqs. Here's the plan: you, ranger, will have to find the faeyan transport <Ship> that delivers this new technology and destroy it any way you see fit, preferably without establishing any communications with it. After that, you'll need to pick up the container with calponic elements and deliver it to our planet <FromPlanet>. All of this needs to be done before the cargo gets delivered, i. e. prior to <Date>. Naturally, once you accomplish your mission successfully, we will pay you an attractive fee -- <Money> cr.

End: Ah, <Player>! We have an intelligence report about <FullShip> having been successfully destroyed. You have met the deadline set, so here's you well-deserved <Money> cr. Now the pelengs will know what all their thievery can get them.

Oh, ranger, look, what's that thing flying out the window? A piece of metal flying or something. It looks like... No, it can't be! This is our damn satellite! What is it doing here? What's this writing on it? Repairs required?

So, <Player>... Our new smart system sent our satellite back to our planet for repairs. It looks like a serious error has occurred. The invention outsmarted its developers. It seems time our satellite deserves a medal for quick thinking. But it's all right, it's not your fault. It's not like we are trying to grab your honest earnings back. Goodbye, <Player>.
Start: We have an extremely important job for you, <Player>.

Three weeks ago, our system's latest invention, the smart satellite IS-106, was launched into orbit of a certain uninhabited planet. We used it for a week to conduct research and then left it in the care of a state of the art decision matrix loaded into the central processor. The satellite had to conduct a survey of the planet's canyons and gorges. And what do you think happened? A few days ago, it disappeared! It just fell off our radar screens! A survey of the planet's surface produced no results, and no traces were found of the probe ever being there. We got suspicious right away. And we had every reason to be since our other satellites reported peleng diplomatic ship <Ship> loitering near that planet on the day the satellite disappeared. It is more likely than not that they have stolen our satellite! We contacted the ship immediately, but its pilot wouldn't even talk to us. He said they didn't know anything about any satellites missing. And he cursed us out too. As only a peleng can! We are not going to put up with this. A state of the art satellite guided by a new smart system couldn't just disappear! The government of our system hereby authorizes you to destroy <Ship>. You have <Day> days to accomplish the mission. Let us show them they cannot get away with stealing someone else's technology.
Once the mission is successfully completed, we will pay you <Money> cr. Good luck, <Player>!

End: Excellent, <Player>! We never forget those who do right by us.

Yes, what now? Oh, the money... You see, ranger, one could argue you are very lucky. We have already spent our entire campaign budget, and had our splendidly generous candidate Wantello not donated his own funds... Long story short, <Player>, here's your <Money> cr.

I hope you understand it's not like we are trying to buy your vote for the only truly deserving candidate, Ulan Wantello? If this were the case, we would resort to good old blackmail instead of paying you since it was you after all who had shot the ship down. Good luck!
Start: <Player>, please make sure the door is closed all the way. What did you say? Oh, yes, we have plenty of things to hide. Don't deny it, rangers don't care much about politics. Otherwise you would have known that a number of human candidates are now running for their race's seat on the Galactic Council.

Our planet <FromPlanet> had no intention of sitting on the wayside and thus proposed its own candidate. This candidate, Mr. Ulan Wantello, is one of the most venerable citizens of the Coalition -- a centenarian veteran of the Klissan War and a renown scholar with ten college degrees. We just couldn't wish for a better candidate, <Player>. Our analysts are certain he is very likely to be elected. However, Mr. Wantello does have one viable opponent -- Cossack Able from planet Earth. The fact that he has some serious following makes us nervous -- and please, <Player>, don't look at me this way. Let me tell you, in case you are not aware of it, that Able is one exceptional liar and hypocrite. A devious son of a gun all around. We just can't afford to let him win, you see. Humanity's very survival may depend on it. Are you grasping the gravity of this situation now?

But not everything is lost yet, ranger. A week ago the enemy... I mean the opponent, sorry, sent <FullShip> on a humanitarian mission to deliver some badly needed relief supplies to the population of a certain planet that had recently been liberated from dominators. Never mind the name of the place. That's all very noble, of course, until one considers the inconvenient little fact that a quarter of the transport's cargo bay is stuffed with propaganda fliers of the "While Some Simply Want, We are Able" variety. It makes no sense at all!

<Player>, shooting <Ship> down will destroy Cossack Able's reputation once and for all. If you do it, they will write it off to rampant piracy. What is required of you here is flawless execution and utmost secrecy. You have until <Date> to do it. If the mission is a success, we will pay you <Money> cr. Do we have a deal?

End: ...no, Mr. Andersen, I don't know anything about it. I am sorry about your friend, but... You'll have to excuse me, I have an important visitor. Could you call back later?

It's good to see you, <Player>. You did an excellent job all around. The criminal is dead and will never disturb public peace and order again. By the way, did you get to read those ridiculous memoirs of his where he is saying we are all living in a computer game, and the world around us is but a virtual reality? Apparently, some do believe him.

By the way, that was a top secret mission, and we will have to take certain precautions. What if you had a chance to read the documents, huh? No, no, you have nothing to worry about. All you have to do is look at this pen -- here comes the flash!

It's good to see you, <Player>. You have done a great job taking care of that criminal. Here, this is your hard-earned <Money> cr. We may still need your services, so please don't go too far, all right?
47.Start: Well, I think you could help me all right. Let me introduce myself. My name is Smith, I represent the Galactic Censorship Committee. We are having a problem with one former diplomat, Mort Fermius. Not only did he manage to get access to top secret files, steal an official ship and disappear, but he is now also spreading totally ludicrous ideas that put the human race and the government of the Coalition in a negative light. We have tried to settle this matter peacefully, but now it looks like we will have to put the screws to him. If you manage to destroy <FullShip> before <Date>, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr. It's a great chance for you to make a buck.

48.End: That's great, <Player>! The criminal got what he deserved, and you earned yourself a well-deserved reward of <Money> cr. By the way, could I interest you in buying some batteries? Now that the power plant is back online, energy prices tanked, so these little power sources have actually become quite attractive. Some other time? Well, as you wish.
48.Start: Did you notice that it is kind of dark in my office? And do you know why? It's because our planet has been hit by an energy crisis. Our local power plant didn't receive the fuel it needed on time because our transport Energize had been attacked by pirates and destroyed along with its cargo. We are certain that the main culprit here is a certain Lenneth Kay, a notorious pirate and scoundrel who had committed plenty of crimes before. But this time he bit more than he could chew, so the government decided to terminate this rascal as soon as possible. If you, <Player>, help us and destroy the pirate ship <Ship> that is now located in the <InStar> system by <Date>, upon your return you will be paid a reward of <Money> cr. You have to admit, this is a good price for the head of such a rascal.

49.End: Ha-ha, <Player>! On behalf of the Radical Degradation Fighters, it is my pleasure to thank you and pay you your well-deserved <Money> cr. It is only with the help of such selfless warriors as yourself that we can hope to weed out all the weak links in the maloq gene pool and save this race from degeneracy.
Start: Oh ruthless warrior, we are glad to welcome you to our planet! We happen to have a job for you. It's not like you are afraid to get your hands dirty committing yet another murder, right? Or, rather, you will play a punishing sword here.

<Player>, you may have heard of the RDF -- Radical Degradation Fighters. This society is trying to prevent primitive races from degenerating even further by destroying their least intellectual specimen so that their genetic imperfection wouldn't be passed along. Just imagine, they are murdering intelligent creatures just because they are a little more slow-witted than their brethren. We staunchly oppose such a policy and use RDF's own methods against them.

If you destroy <Ship> that has one of the RDF's worst henchmen on board by <Date>, upon your return you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr. Are you ready to save hundreds of innocent idio... I mean uneducated intelligent beings, of course.

End: Damn, <Player>, you are one ruthless killa! We are delighted with your swift handling of that diplomat <Ship>! Argh!!!
Take your <Money> cr. Don't be a stranger now. We may have more orders for you. We're not even past the A's in the Galactic phone book...
Start: Hey, pirate! We have an order for a tough customer such as yourself, one who doesn't know the meaning of the word "mercy." Sometimes certain individual fall out of favor with the maloq government.

The reasons... the reasons aren't important. For example, currently on our blacklist are <clr>Allen Killallmaloqs<clrEnd> and <clr>Albert Maloqsuck<clrEnd>. They're hiding out aboard <FullShip>. We wish to never see those individuals -- or hear their names -- again. You don't need us to explain the particulars, now do you? Then get to work! We will pay you as much as <Money> cr if you manage to do it by <Date>.

You'll need to clarify the ship's location at the information center; there's a search window there, which I'm sure you'll figure out how to use. And when you figure it out, don't forget to tell me... But then, a true maloq has no need for such things!

End: Excellent, <Player>! Here's your <Money> cr. You know, I had some tests done at our hospital. All my organs are in good shape. The gaal did a fantastic job. And as to my strange behavior... Apparently, while visiting one of the uninhabited planets, I have contracted a very rare disease -- the pacifist syndrome. Luckily, it is easily curable. They got me up and running in no time, and the first thing I did was enjoy an entire raw piglet. Then I personally executed 20 war criminals.
Don't you feel sorry for that gaal. One more, one less -- who is even going to notice? Take care, ranger!
Start: <Player>! I'll be damned if you are not a real godsend! I hope you have enough gun tubes aboard your ship to blow up one lousy gaal barge.

Let me tell you what this is all about, and I am sure you are going to hate this wicked <Ship> as much as I do. A couple of years ago, I turned to him as the planet's best surgeon so that he could cut out that damn piece of shrapnel out of my gut and sow me back up with durable red thread. He put me to sleep and kept picking at my body for three days! He told me he had fixed or replaced a number of internal organs.

And then I started noticing certain changes in myself. I became disgusted at the taste of raw meat, and then, before I knew it I became an all around vegan. Then my voice softened, and my roar lost its former might, and now I cannot even... Bear arms! I used to be a maloq, and this damn gaal quack turned me into some kind of sissy! Only his miserable alien blood can wash off my shame and rectify the injury he had caused me.
Find that <FullShip> and blow it to smithereens! If you can do it by <Date>, I'll pay you <Money> cr.

End: Excellent, <Player>! Your <Money> cr is being transferred to your account as we speak. Thank God you managed to destroy that mutant before it was too late. We are still trying to figure out how that mutant ape managed to escape the lab and steal a ship. To be sure, our targeted breeding program helped us increase this monkey's IQ threefold, but that's nowhere near enough. It could have been a math error somewhere.
Once again, many thanks for helping us destroy this runaway beast. Naturally, we couldn't tell you the truth up front -- you wouldn't have believed that a monkey could steal a spaceship.
Start: Always glad to see you, <Player>! We need help urgently! The problem is a certain crazy scientist has recently left our planet. He is on board <FullShip> at the moment, and he could cause a lot of damage.

The poor sob is totally nuts about the Gobsaurus Man superhero. You know, the brave superhero, savior of the Galaxy, protector of the downtrodden -- that kind of stuff. So our guy decided he wanted to be a noble daredevil himself and just like Gobsaurus Man jumped into a vat of toxic waste to become a mutant hero. I have no idea how he could possibly survive such a feat. But believe it or not, he is not only alive but also fancying himself a mutant superhero. In reality, he never mutated even though he did manage to catch a deadly infection.

We need you to destroy <FullShip> prior to <Date> when the latent period of the disease is expected to end. The ship will then become a deadly carrier of incurable space plague! We will pay you <Money> cr for doing this unquestionably noble deed.

End: Excellent, <Player>! Dance us a jig, your account has been credited <Money> cr. Tell us the truth, your onboard computer is probably using the Nondows operating system, huh? I am positive you've cursed its developer on occasion and wished you could break the damn nerd's neck one day.

Now, that's exactly what you did! Congratulations, ranger! From the bottom of my heart! Oh how I wish I were in your shoes! Millions... Heck, no, billions of hapless Nondows users are green with envy now. The thing is that one of the creators of that infernal system was traveling aboard <FullShip>. Unfortunately, it wasn't the big guy himself, but rather one of his top testers. Still, it makes you feel good, doesn't it? Best of luck, ranger!
Start: <Player>! Your timing is perfect. We happen to have a wee bit of business for an experienced space warrior like yourself.

We are currently running a campaign against software piracy. Anyone surrendering ten pirated halodiscs will receive one licensed copy of the software. And those unwilling to do it voluntarily are getting three -- years in prison that is, not disks. All the disks so recovered have been loaded onto <FullShip> whose automatic pilot has been set to guide the vessel straight into the insatiable flames of our star. However, it appears that the ship itself was using pirated software since rather than guide the vessel towards the star the automatic pilot took it to the <InStar> system.
If you destroy this ship loaded with pirated software disks prior to <Date>, you will be paid <Money> cr. And don't you worry, there are no living creatures aboard, it's all automatic.
By the way, does your onboard computer use licensed software? When you come back, we'll have our experts check it out.

53.End: Good. Great! Wonderful! <Player>, you have saved the lives of hundred of agents, and then some. Had those lists fallen into wrong hands, or worse yet become public knowledge, heads would have rolled -- yours and mine included. Here's your <Money> cr. Let me also remind you again that I have never seen you before, nor you me, nor has there ever been a maloq. You are getting my drift, aren't you?
Start: <Player>, please close the door behind you and keep your voice down as much as you can. Even the walls here have eyes, ears and agile hands. After all this is the main representative office of Dzuhallag in the <FromStar> system By the way, at the moment you are being closely watched by five snipers, two psychologists and one student of medicine. Oh, all right, veterinary science.

We have a contract for you, <Player>. A murder contract, that is. There is this one maloq... He is one exceptional son of a gun -- the only maloq in the Galaxy with a phenomenal visual memory. It so happened that our people tried to recruit him and had him remember 50 pages of a random text as a test. Naturally, no one bothered to check what the text was. It happened to be a comprehensive list of all our moles, complete with their personal files and secret passwords. All those responsible have been already punished, but the maloq himself managed to disappear aboard <FullShip>. He is already in the <InStar> system, and if you don't terminate him before <Date> our secret information will not be so secret anymore. This is going to be a total disaster!
If you terminate the mark successfully, you will receive a fee of <Money> cr. And ranger, I hope you understand you have never visited here, and you and I never met.

54.End: This is unbelievable, <Player>! The game is already in stores! Apparently, this has been a heck of a motivator! Here are your <Money> cr -- you totally deserve them. Lines at the stores are so long that I will only be able to enjoy this Mystic Pagers 3 some time next year. But that's all right. According to early reviews, the game is fantastic! Thank you again.
Start: Argh! I can't wait any longer!

Please forgive me for this sudden outburst of aggression, <Player>, but I have my reasons. Our entire planet is nuts about computer games. Everyone is particularly fond of the good old Mystic Pagers 2. You play being a space warrior there, saving the Galaxy and destroying aggressors. The game is completely fictional, but it's great fun nonetheless. Why do we play all this old stuff you ask? Because the scoundrels that are making the game have been dragging their feet for years developing the third installment. They never seem to be short of excuses, lame as they may be.  But now we've had it! Enough promises! We Want MP3 now!

Sorry for being so verbose, but I am now talking for the entire planet. We decided that the time for polite requests and delicate prodding is long past! Time has come to take resolute action, or we will never see our favorite game in stores. We have learned that one of the developers working on the Mystic Pagers 3, a certain <clr>Gus de Boob<clrEnd> is now traveling in the <InStar> system aboard <Ship>. Shoot that sucker down! We are certain that <clr>Gus de Boob's<clrEnd> untimely demise will give the other developers a good kick, and very soon we will be able to enjoy a new installment of the greatest game ever in the entire universe! I think <Money> cr will make for a sufficient incentive for you, even if you are not a fan of computer games. But remember, it is crucial that you accomplish the mission within <Day> days. Otherwise the developers will come up with another excuse, which may cause many among the public to kill themselves in desperation.

End: Very well, <Player>, you have completed your part of the mission. To be honest with you, I have never before had a chance to do business with such a shamelessly cold-blooded killer capable of whacking, for a pittance of <Money> cr, an influential mafioso who, if memory serves me right, had just given us a loan at a usurious rate. Now we both know where he is, he and that loan of his.

By the way, your fee that we have openly transferred to your account is but what's left of that loan's proceeds. For that reason, in the interest of your own continued good health and well being, I suggest you learn how to keep quiet. It helps enhance one's natural longevity. You are free to go.
Start: <Player>, you may be aware that foncer races have become widely popular lately. Naturally, this spectacular albeit risky sport has drawn the attention of not only billions of fans but also of black market bookmakers. Some of the bets they take may well exceed our planet's entire budget. In turn, this kind of mad money drew in the the mafia and the governments. But that's just some background.

On the eve of the most recent championship's finals that ended yesterday, tension flew higher than ever before. In his very first season, a young driver named Burnheardt from planet Earth left plenty of famous racers in the dust and became a contender for the number one spot. The incumbent champion is faeyan <clr>Feitel<clrEnd>, an experienced race driver. They've been going neck to neck up to that moment, so whoever won that round would become the new champion.

The mafia bet big on <clr>Feitel<clrEnd>. Like, real big, ranger. A day before the finals, they put the screws to <clr>Burnheardt<clrEnd>, threatening to kill his sister if he won. Naturally, the young racer lost all interest in his coveted trophy right away and agreed to finish second after <clr>Feitel<clrEnd>. From the start, he took the lead but just barely. Apparently, he still wanted to stroke his ego before giving up. He stayed in the lead for a couple of rounds but then slowed down a few miles before the finish line and yielded to the incumbent and a couple of others. It was all going fine, but then all of a sudden, a hundred yards or so before the finish line, Feitel crossed paths with another opponent who was going faster. He made a mistake, the two foncers had a collision and both got thrown off the track. Burnheardt did not have enough time to react and crossed the finish line, thus winning the race and the title he wasn't supposed to get.

That's some situation all right, isn't it? On the one hand, <clr>Feitel<clrEnd> made the mistake that cost him his title himself, on the other this isn't going to give the mafiosos their money back, and now they have to deliver on their threat as well. For that reason, they decided not to get mixed in it themselves, instead telling someone who owes them money to sort it all out. And that means us. Don't even ask how we have come to owe money to the mafia. It is much easier than you might think. Naturally, I am not going to kill that <clr>Burnheardt's<clrEnd> poor sister myself, so I would like to hire someone unscrupulous enough.

And please don't look at me like you want to strangle me, <Player>. We all have families too, and I don't want anyone of my kin to die in lieu of a girl I do not even know. It's nothing personal, it's just this dirty, cruel business that we happen to be involved in. Your target is now hiding aboard liner <Ship> located in the <InStar> system. If you would like to make a few bucks here, then shooting the ship down will earn you <Money> cr, but if you think you are too conscientious for something like this all of a sudden, then forget all about it and don't say a word to anyone if you don't want someone coming for you one day as well.

56.End: Excellent work, <Player>! That ship with a peleng brain has been written off for scrap. My brother was spared plastic surgery. He is undergoing neurorehabilitation now. And you can enjoy your well-deserved fee that I am about to transfer to your account.
Start: <Player>, your timing is perfect.

Have a look at this stereo shot. Doesn't this maloq look familiar? No, that's not myself on the morning of the New Year's Day. What you see here is my brother the way he looks now. He is a well-known tester of new equipment. It is through his selfless travails that modern society will soon be able to appreciate the convenience of new maloq stools with an anti-gravity system in lieu of legs! But that's not what this is all about.

Today, while testing a ship with an imported artificial intelligence module, we had an emergency situation. The peleng electronic brain wouldn't take commands from my brother the tester, and following a number of his attempts to call that rebellious tin can to order by way of direct application of fists, it went berserk altogether.

At the moment, the ship with my brother on board is making its strange maneuvers God only knows where. And since he never bothered to buckle up, that's what we have at the moment -- what's on that picture, that is. Judging by the progressing deformation of his mug, <Player>, you have <Day> days to destroy this runaway tin can known in the catalogs as <Ship>. By the way, it was last seen in the <InStar> system.

Don't worry about my brother's safety. The escape system on that ship is maloq-made and very reliable. So please try to meet that deadline, <Player>. If you linger, our entire clan will face a shameful catastrophe, with one of its own having to undergo plastic surgery. But if you deliver, I'll be very grateful -- to the tune of <Money> cr.

End: Well, <Player>... What is it they say, better late than never? Oh, no, you did meet the deadline, and <Ship> has been destroyed. But a few days before that they managed to rob a yacht that belonged to one of my maloq colleagues and, to add insult to injury, posted a stereo record of the heist for everyone to see. As a result, he had to resign since he was not alone in his cabin.
What? And you saw that part with the peleng? I wish you had been a little more diligent about complying with the terms of your contract! Here is your <Money> cr, and consider yourself dismissed.
Start: <Player>, don't you look at me like that! This is not my outfit at all! You see, a bunch of yahoos broke into this place some time ago. Those insolent bastards took all my clothes and gadgets and stole my personal ship <Ship> too. And that's only a few days after I put a new engine in! Man, I didn't even have a chance to break it in properly. This is total fu--

<Player>! I should have realized it right there and then what a great danger those bandits may pose to society. They need to be arrested and put on trial ASAP -- or better yet, terminated. You think I am being cruel? Imagine my colleague of another race in a women's robe! Not that I give a hoot personally. We fae are hermaphrodites, but a maloq would sooner shoot himself to avoid the shame. To avoid any such exigencies, the criminals must be punished as soon as possible. Naturally, it's a pity about the ship. Its shower alone, the one with the microparticulate spray... But back to the business at hand!

<Player>, your mission here is to destroy <Ship>. If you do a good job and take no more than <Day> days, there will be <Money> cr in it for you. So, how about it? If you agree, get started ASAP. Use the search system to locate the bandits.

End: There's wailing in all the streets, ranger, and cries of anguish in every square. The messiah's coming has been postponed indefinitely. Weren't you ashamed of spilling the blood of innocent Foodick? Well, yeah, it was us who put out a contract on him, but we made a mistake, and it was your job as a ranger to verify everything. Thank God the rescue team arrived on time and managed to resuscitate the poor sob. Or you and I would be talking now in a nice, clean prison cell with bars on the window. And to think that the end of the war was so close! And then you...

But be it as it may, you have discharged your obligation to us in full, so we simply have to pay you the agreed upon <Money> cr. But as I am sure you have already realized, there won't be any promised favor from the Lord coming your way.
Start: Ranger, do you believe that our victory over dominators is near? And no, it won't be won on the battlefield, it will be by a touch of grace. Our oracles predict that on <Date> a messiah will be born who will turn the dominators' own rage against themselves and thus put an end to this never ending war. And that messiah is to be born on our very own <FromPlanet>! However, there is a gloomy side to this blessed news. To be reborn as the messiah, he will need to complete his life in his current incarnation. Which at the moment is as Foodick Flamesky, the pilot of <Ship>. He is still very young, and if we wait until he dies of natural causes we are not going to have us any messiah coming any time soon.

Ranger, the fate of the Galaxy is now in your hands! Release the messiah's eternal soul from its worldly body of Foodick Flamesky, and you will obtain favor from the Lord. Besides, since I hear you rangers are great fans of gold, you will come back from this mission to a reward of 13 authentic gaaldoc coins that translate into <Money> cr, give or take, at the current exchange rate.

59.End: Excellent work, <Player>! I have read your report and now believe that the Pension Fund will grant our appeal in full, and instead of the miserly 1,000,000,000 credits a month Maglus will be getting five times as much. No, don't gasp at me so, these are in our local currency, and the exchange rate to galactic credits isn't much in our favor. As for you, you are getting a reward of <Money> cr for successfully completing your mission and writing a creative report.
Start: Ranger, what are you going to do in retirement? What do you mean, you never gave it much thought? Sooner or later, your services won't be needed anymore, and believe me, give it another few years and space ailments will get the better of you, so you will want a cozy little cabin facing a lake in the woods somewhere, and maybe a pachvaraus farm... Just you look at this predecessor of mine, Maglus, whose retirement we celebrated yesterday. Now, that was a warrior in his time! No one in the system ever heard of pirates back then. And it's not like there were no pirates at the time, there were, but with brave Maglus around they never lasted long. So here is our Maglus, preparing to retire and open himself a small candle factory, and then it turns out they are going to shortchange him on his veteran's pension. You see, his record, as it happens, is one downed pirate short. Ay-ay-ay!

This is where you could help us, <Player>. All you need to do is shoot down a pirate, come back and report that the kill shot was fired by Maglus who just happened to be riding along as a guest, aching to relive the good ol' days. In all fairness, the old man himself has been suffering from a vortex contusion for years and isn't up to much of anything, not even something as simple as that. We even found you a victim. There was this half-baked pirate wannabe here some ten years ago. Ron is his name, and these days he is tooling around in an old barge, <Ship>, that fits the bill easily. All it'll take is a couple of salvos, and the guy's history. Just remember that the Pension Fund is due to review the appeal by <Date>, so you only have <Day> days to complete the mission. I hope the fee of <Money> cr will prove to be a sufficient motivator for you.

6.End: That's right, <Player>. Thanks to you Ranger <Ship> did not escape maloq justice! Yee-haw! Would you like a medal for this job? Maloqs are always eager to hand out medals. Don't worry, you can have your <Money> cr as well. We've got plenty to spare.
Start: Say, <Player>, do you remember being recruited into the rangers? The selection was very tough! You were lucky to have matched all the requirements. But a maloq ranger piloting <Ship> was taken on for no good reason! Specifically, he bought his license for money, then stole a ship from my own nephew. My nephew goes to a gaalian university, so he'd decided to forgive and forget. Pff! I enjoyed beating that gaalian gobbledygook about forgiveness to all out of him.

Now the nephew has finally filed a request to have the hijacker punishd. Punishment will be swift and unavoidable. Now go to the <InStar> system and terminate the criminal. These are your orders, and your deadline is <Date>. Now go, duty is waiting!
Grr, why are you still here? Didn't I already tell you that you'll be paid <Money> cr for that bastard's head?!

60.End: Radical situations call for radical measures. This crook has to be taught a lesson. We thank you for your assistance in the struggle for the cultural face of the Galaxy, and will transfer <Money> cr to your account.
Start: It's simply scandalous! Forgive me, honorable <Player>, for being emotional. My blood is just boiling with indignation. A certain person aboard the pirate ship <Ship> has acquired a V Burner 2.0 hyperlaser and couldn't find a better use for it than to leave filthy language on the surface of uninhabited planets. What's more is that the size of his writing is so big that these linguistic embellishments can be read from a great distance; this will certainly lead to the embarrassment of representatives of the developed races. In response to an urgent request to immediately erase the raunchy words, accompanied by an extremely delicate warning regarding steps being taken with respect to <Ship>, the hooligan advised us in a most indecent manner to go to hell, which we later determined to be the residence of dark forces in ancient human belief systems. We have no other choice but to neutralize it, or this may lead to an intergalactic confrontation.

Right now <Ship> is in the <InStar> system, preparing to leave another mark on one of the system's uninhabited planets. If you don't foil his plans before <Date>, he will succeed in leaving his mark on the planet and disappear in some unknown direction.

End: That was a decidedly glorious battle. We've already reviewed the material captured by your cameras and will soon receive records from the droid operators and the black box from your opponent's ship. I think when we finish putting it together we'll end up with a wonderful, realistic and ruthless film, full of violence and strong ranger language. In other words, just the thing for preschool kiddies.

Well, <Player>, we won't keep you any longer. The promised <Money> cr have already been transferred to your account. You can peacefully depart to perform your ranger duties, unless of course you want to become our full-time gladiator. No? Well, all right. In that case, goodbye. May your enemies be strong!
Start: <Player>, we heard that you're a decent soldier -- is that true? Then you may be able to help us. You've probably heard about an ancient form of entertainment: gladiator fights. This is our great pride. Maloq gladiator fights have taken place through the centuries and millenia -- and they have changed very little during this time. Nothing compares with the feeling of real battle, when your life is at stake, when each blow may be your last, when bloody sweat pours into your eyes and your mouth is filled with the copper taste of shattered teeth. It is a real sport for real men! We maloqs are deeply convinced that only under threat of death can you find out what you're capable of and what you're worth... But I digress.

So, as I said, our gladiator fights have taken place through the centuries, virtually unchanged, but not too long ago a new type of fight has gained popularity: Space Gladiator Fights". As you might have guessed, these are duels on spaceships. They engage in combat while all of their actions are recorded. Both inside the ship, using standard cameras, and outside, using special droid operators.

I think you already know what your mission will be. We'll hire you as a professional gladiator and your opponent will be another hired gladiator flying <Ship>, which is currently in the <InStar> system. And to stoke your interest even more, in addition to a great battle we are also offering compensation. If you're still alive on <Date> and your opponent is not, you will receive a cash prize. The prize fund is currently <Money> cr. Go on, say yes -- there may not be a second chance!

End: You won't believe this, <Player>, but it turns out that the Bambay <clr>Wallop<clrEnd> you zapped was real, too! Here's what happened. Our Bambay landed on some desert planet. I won't tell you its name, 'cause I want to search it to find out if I can make some profit there. Anyway, his companions spotted an abandoned Faeyan lab on the surface. He found his way inside and came across some machine. We don't know what he tried to do with that machine and what that machine ultimately did to him, but a moment later another Bambay <clr>Wallop<clrEnd>, completely identical to the original one, appeared on the planet next to ours. He suffered from a terrible headache and couldn't recall what had happened to him on that desert planet. And the first <clr>Wallop<clrEnd> must have never noticed anything: he picked up whatever things there he found useful and flew away. Of course it's sad that you and I bumped off such a competent pirate, but that's ok since we still got another one! Plus, we don't know what would have happened to the universe if two <clr>Wallops<clrEnd> had met each other in the same point of time and space. So whatever happens, happens for the best.

Your money has already been transferred. You may go, but don't tell this story to anyone. And don't you dare search for that lab. We don't need a host of clones suffering from amnesia wandering around!
Start: It's good that you asked, <Player>. I got one delicate job for an outstanding rogue such as yourself. The Bambay <clr>Wallop<clrEnd> is now in the <InStar> star system aboard his <Ship>. Blow it to the Klissan sky so its fragments scatter all over the system! If you do, I'll pay you <Money> cr.

Want to know the details? Well, the real Bambay <clr>Wallop<clrEnd> -- who, by the way, is a good friend of mine -- is currently two rooms away from here, suffering from a terrible hangover, and he can't recall who hijacked his ship and when. We tried to make the hijacker give the vehicle back to its owner in a peaceful manner, but he refuses to do so, claiming that he's the real Bambay and that we're try to mess with his mind. So there's only way out: kill the impudent jerk.

63.End: I knew that you would make it, <Player>, I knew it! Let me hit you in the jaw once or twice! It's just that I can't restrain my emotions! Now our race is relatively safe, and we can continue to enjoy our wars. It's a pity you weren't born a Maloq. You've missed a lot! By the way, your money has already been transferred to your account.
Start: Yes, we Maloqs need help, quick and competent help. You really are suitable for us, <Player>. Our race is on the edge of extinction, but not because we all are going to die in battle any time soon. Oh, that would have been a glorious death, but no!

Some eggheaded Faeyan scientist whose name I couldn't even memorize is obsessed with the idea that we are bloodthirsty, warmongering psychos who will conquer the whole galaxy soon, plunging it into an abyss of endless battles, darkness, and pain. I won't deny how tempting that sounds, but to tell the truth, it's not at all what we're striving for. Anyway, he invented some remedy, "genofect" or "xenophage" -- I can't quite recall its name. He expects to use it to regulate the Maloqs' birth rate on each of our planets. That's not in our race's plans, though: the enemies are strong and numerous, and when we are gone, they will whack you all out, one by one, without a moment's thought.

You, <Player>, as a distinguished pirate and a tough fighter, can render an invaluable service to our race! The scientist is now in the <InStar> star system, aboard the ship called <Ship>, together with all of his villainous designs. He's searching for a planet where he can test his invention to find out what it's good for. Your task is to destroy him and all his work so that there's nothing left, not even dust. If you manage to do this within <Day> days, you'll get <Money> cr. If you fail, we'll hire someone else, since the stakes are too high and we can't take any chances.

64.End: Excellent job, <Player>! The Lyakusha Jubba is pleased how you solved the situation and promptly had the remuneration transferred to your personal account. Consider yourself to have another fan, and remember: if Jubba ever needs to do more dirty work, he will turn to you first!
Start: Please don't take this wrongly, but I don't have any special tasks for you. Don't hang your head yet, <Player>! My good friend, the Lyakusha Jubba, needs help he personally asked me for, but I think that you could do even better, even though you only have two upper extremities.

Anyway, Jubba told me that his personal treasury had been robbed by someone who knew their trade, since they didn't steal any treasures or rare weapons but just a debtor's statue. Let me explain. Debtor's statues are, in fact, frozen debtors who have failed to settle with Jubba in time and have been put as decorations on the walls of his treasury. The robbery was most likely performed by the buddies of the debtor whose statue was stolen. All right, enough of this sentimental talk. The harsh reality is that they are making it away from their punishment on a ship called <Ship> which, according to our intel, is now in <InStar> star system. If you want to receive <Money> cr from the Lyakusha Jubba, then you better say "I'm game" right now and run to the hangar. The employer clearly insisted that the job must be done before <Date>.

End: The job is done, the coward is no more! And his name has been recorded in the maloq Book of Shame. May his fate be a lesson for the younger generation of warriors. Cowards and deserters have no right to besmirch the valiant maloq race with their existence.
Don't forget your <Money> cr. You're an independent contractor, after all.
Start: Outrageous news, <Player>! A maloq from the elite Red Hatchets detachment -- may his name go down forever in infamy and oblivion -- has displayed the kind of lily liver and cowardice unbefitting our race! He deserted! Having captured diplomatic ship <Ship>, he piloted it off the planet! Our agents report spotting the deserter in the <InStar> system. There are no ways about this situation, <Player>. The traitor's ship must be destroyed before <Date>, and that's that. Now excuse! Sorry, I meant to say, execute!

Are you still here? Argh, almost forgot, we will pay you <Money> cr for the successful completion of this mission! I guess it's true what they say -- you rangers refuse to lift a finger until the magic topic of money is mentioned. Who knew...

8.End: Excellently done, <Player>! You know, we wouldn't have minded getting our hands on that device of his, but the fae and the maloqs have been eyeing it already. So the decision to destroy the device was correct from our peleng point of view, which is the only right point of view... Did you want anything else? Oh, yes, the <Money> cr is also yours.
Start: Murder! How do you like the music of this word, <Player>? And what would you say to a sum of <Money> cr? Do you not see the connection between them? Well, then I'm going to show you. One <clr>Orlon Brong<clrEnd>, operating aboard the ship <Ship>, is using an unknown device for his own dirty purposes. Specifically, he lures dominator squads to populated systems and takes advantage of the ensuing panic and impunity to rob and pillage transport vessels. Pretty cold of him, isn't it? He's clever lad, I'll give him that, and if it weren't for these foul tricks with the dominators he could have made himself a name among the pirate community. But nobody likes dominators, which is why Brong and his secret device must disappear for good. Do this before <Date>, and the promised dough will relocate into your pockets in a jiffy.

Oh, one more thing. I was so busy dealing with all this stuff that it slipped my mind to check the ship's current location in the information center's search window. I mean, I've only got four hands, not a dozen! But you'll figure it out on your own, yeah?

9.End: You know what, <Player>? <clr>Polluxius<clrEnd> the shaman is dead, and you're a man of your word. There's one caveat: we found out that there actually wasn't a curse; the bullfrogs were dying out because of the low-grade feed we started giving them to save money. Oh well, these things happen. You've earned your <Money> cr just the same, and one less shaman to worry about is always good news.
Start: Feel like making a little money, specifically <Money> cr? Of course you do, I can see it in your eyes!

We were recently visited by a very powerful shaman named <clr>Polluxius<clrEnd>. And do you know what he did? You'll never guess! He posed an ultimatum to our government -- either we start buying ragobam bullfrog poison exclusively from his relatives' farm, or he would exterminate all of our planet's bullfrogs with a powerful spell. We obviously refused -- really, we ain't no fools! But he delivered on his threat and put a hex on our planet's farms, and now the bullfrog population is dwindling.

Now the government is thinking that if the shaman were to die, his spell should be lifted as well. He was spotted in the <InStar> system not long ago, aboard the pirate ship <Ship>. My dear <Player>, would you do us a service and liquidate the pesky sorcerer by <Date>? This may be the only way to salvage the bullfrog trade, which is planet <FromPlanet>'s main and only source of revenue!

End: It's very nice to see this <clr>detonation-gripper<clrEnd> in one piece, <Player>! This is an extremely valuable device. You could say it marked the golden age of our race. But don't worry, I won't bore you with a lecture on our history. Few enough of us know it anyway; no, we prefer to learn from our own mistakes, not those of our forefathers.
Please accept <Money> cr. from us for your efficient handling of the matter.
0.Start: For quite a long time on our proud planet, executions were performed using a special miniature <clr>detonation-gripper<clrEnd>. In reality, this is a separate bomb for mineral works, to make it clear specially for you. These days, however, the maloqs use a more appropriate method of taking care of criminals! Thus, the old device is no longer needed, and we want to deliver it to <ToPlanet> (<ToStar> system). There is a historical exhibition of maloq military machines there. A very cognitive one, may I add, I recommend a visit! Though it's closed for reconstruction for the moment -- one of the exhibits went off again, those jokers had forgotten to unload it! It should reopen around <Date>. You must deliver the <clr>a detonation-gripper<clrEnd> by then! They will pay you a reward at the museum: <Money> cr.

1.End: Wonderful, the gaalian hand is safe and sound! You're a brave warrior for taking this job! If the gaals had noticed you, their ceaseless torrent of pacifist speeches would have meant certain, slow and excruciating death. Here's your <Money> cr. Our doctors will now investigate the resistance of gaalian tissues to external sources of radiation.
1.Start: There are doctors on <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system who specialize at treating specimen of any race. Your orders are to deliver there a cryogenic flask with a <clr>gaalian hand<clrEnd>. It is a trophy, received by one of our finest warriors in a fight against a gaal! That is why only a brave warrior can deliver it! The scientists on planet <ToPlanet> will study the hand so as to learn more about the mysterious gaalian biology. This will aid us in our expansion. And you... You can expect to be paid <Money> cr. But you must complete the job by <Date>, while the arm is still fresh!

10.End: Long has the <clr>ckhasha<clrEnd> traveled the world until it finally returned to its master! It was like a lost soul, sowing misery all around until it found peace. I am glad to give you this sum of <Money> cr, charged with the energy of life. May fortune forever be with you!
Start: Believe it or not, our planet has been suffering from terrible cataclysms and natural disasters for over three hundred years, and all because of a hex cast with a <clr>ckhasha<clrEnd> by a powerful shaman from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system.

A <clr>ckhasha<clrEnd> is an ancient magical object, dating back to the Tzin Dynasty. According to an old legend, the hex will be lifted around <Date>, but only if the shaman and his ckhasha are reunited in his tomb. Take this ckhasha and deliver it to the shaman's home planet of <ToPlanet> before the specified date. There it will be placed in the shaman's tomb and forgotten. And though you're not at all hurting for money, you'll also be paid a sum of <Money> cr.

End: We were expecting a package from <FromPlanet>. The pelengs have promised us a surprise, and here it is. "Khavas" is inscribed on the box -- a sort of peleng kvass. Excellent, the holidays are coming and we'll have a chance to try it. Though I can't help but wonder why the pelengs are giving away out their rather expensive kvass and fermentation cultures?
At any rate, <Player>, thanks very much and here's your fee of <Money> cr.
Start: Dearest <Player>, we've got a job that's worth <Money> cr for a brave space ranger. We know that your ingenious forbear used to assist our special service troops in their operations against the humans, so consider this your chance to follow in his footsteps!

You are to deliver this biological weapon of mass destruction to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system, giving our human chums a few pleasant surprises to deal with. And the best part is that no one will suspect a thing until whole planets begin dying out. You must try to complete the mission before <Date>, otherwise our precious bacteria won't survive to do their job.

End: I don't get it, <Player>, how can a warrior do courier's work? Shame on you! Moreover, you did it for those peleng swamp freaks!

Their scoops are just as useless at stirring mud as they are in combat. One of our soldiers equals a hundred of their kind! Take your <Money> cr and begone! A great holiday awaits -- the day of our victory over the klissan!
12.Start: Dearest <Player>, there's a job that pays <Money> cr -- fair compensation for a great warrior such as yourself! All you need to do is deliver a set of <clr>ceremonial combat scoops<clrEnd> to our brave swamp troops on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. They are going to participate in the Victory Day Parade, celebrating our triumph over the klissan. It is imperative that you complete the mission by <Date>.

End: Halt, alien, don this robe of torment... Wait, you're <Player>! And you're carrying the ceremonial <clr>mud cake<clrEnd>, decorated with woshak and pakryak feathers, intended for young pachvarausi who have completed the trials. This is wonderful!

According to our tradition, whoever brings the cake shall be paid a fee in the amount of <Money> cr. Furthermore, <Player>, it is my pleasure to congratulate you on completing our rite of passage. You are now a man! Now, if you would, please return the robe.
Start: Dearest <Player>, a brave soul such as you cannot refuse a job that pays <Money> cr. You are to deliver a ceremonial <clr>mud cake<clrEnd> of swamp slush and pakryak blood. The cake is an essential component in a rite of passage that's due to take place on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. The delivery must be made by <Date>. And don't you even think of refusing!
Sure, the cake may stink pretty badly, which is why everyone else we've asked passed on the job... But a professional like yourself surely wouldn't be act so unwisely!

14.End: Hmm, <Player>, this is fine liqueur you've brought us. You're clearly a connoisseur. Would you like to stay for the feast? I'll save you the least moldy seat at the table. No? Very well, modesty looks good on you. Please sign this receipt for <Money> cr.
Start: How does a job paying <Money> cr sound? Sounds mighty fine -- I know! A traditional alcoholic festival dubbed "Universal Abyss" will soon begin on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system, and every peleng planet will present a sample of their signature beverage. These samples are then poured into a single barrel and offered to attendees. It makes for an excellent party!

Your mission is to deliver an amphora of our <clr>signature swamp liquor<clrEnd> with pulp. After that, you can stay and enjoy yourself. But make sure you finish the job by <Date> if you want your fee!

15.End: Why, it is none other than Ranger <Player>, whose efforts toward interplanetary cooperation are worthy of the highest praise! Madame Gaalsaud values your contribution to the development of robocopying technology; in fact, she values it at exactly <Money> cr.
15.Start: Umm, <Player>, do you know that earning <Money> cr can be as easy as one, two, three? A certain Madame Gaalsaud from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system wishes to open a museum with robocopies of celebrities from across the Galaxy. Among others, she has ordered a <clr>robocopy<clrEnd> of our lyakusha-president <clr>Klush Hamsius<clrEnd>, which we have successfully reproduced and are now entrusting to your custody. As a veteran soldier, we know that you'll be able to protect this, the most precious of cargoes, against those who may wish it harm. Please be so kind as to deliver it safe and sound by <Date>, lest all your efforts will be in vain.

16.End: Hello, <Player>! That is how humans speak, isn't it? With this chameleon cloaks you delivered, you can barely tell me apart from a real human, don't you agree? Now take your <Money> cr and let's forget that we've ever met.
Start: <Player>, we have a job for a real pirate from the spy agency Dzuhallag! You are to deliver special <clr>chameleon cloaks<clrEnd>, crafted from Haritian swamp chameleon skins, to the human planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system.
Deliver the cloaks and you will be compensated as much as <Money> cr, which you will agree is an overpayment for such a simple gig. But hurry -- our agents will be waiting for your arrival by <Date>.

End: Mmm, <Player>, you've done a great service to peleng science by delivering this CD here. As it happens, we're already well on the way to devising a new Rachehan! Ever heard of him? He was a legendary pirate -- truly savage and ruthless. We've been singing songs of his exploits for three hundred years now.

What we're doing now is importing the cognitive activity of the new peleng society's most distinguished representatives, hoping that it will help build a new Rachehan, maybe even more devious than the original. In the meantime, this well-earned <Money> cr is yours to enjoy.
17.Start: <Money> cr is already waiting for you, <Player>! Taking into account your reputation as someone who takes good care of his cargo, we want you to deliver to our specialists over on planet <ToPlanet> (<ToStar> system) this <clr>CD with brain imagings<clrEnd>. These were taken from some of the most notorious criminals. Our scientists will try to scrutinize their propensity toward banditism, to figure out the nature of cruelty, deviousness and other positive peleng qualities, so as to amplify and utilize them better. So please hurry and make sure you deliver the cargo by <Date>.

End: Have you brought the <clr>SL<clrEnd> Medallion and the cups? That's great, <Player>! The amount of <Money> cr will be transferred to your account right away.

Now that the prizes are here, we will start soon. All we need to do is wait for the rainy season to start, so that there would be more mud and the action could get more graphic. Take my word on this -- you are dealing with an expert here. We pelengs have perfected the art of electoral campaigns. Not that many societies can boast the 100% turnout at the polls.
Start: Here is your chance to make <Money> cr right here and now, but the offer won't be available tomorrow! Planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system will soon be electing its Supreme Lyakusha. A centuries-old peleng tradition calls for these elections to be in the form of a competition where the candidates would throw mud at each other. The winner will get this <clr>Supreme Lyakusha Medallion<clrEnd> and become the top dog, with the next six runners up getting trophy cups.

Your mission is to deliver these awards to their destination by <Date> at the latest. Time is of the essence here! They may even let you throw some mud out of competition. I don't think I need to explain it to you what a pleasure it is to throw some fresh mud at your political opponent and evade the return shot.

End: Mmm, <Player>, is this fresh tobacco from planet <FromPlanet>? How wonderful! It is a true godsend for our cabinet ministers that have currently backed themselves into another creative corner.

And by the way, the gaals say that smoking kills, but if you ask us, dominators are much better at killing than smoking. So what's the point focusing on tobacco? So here's your <Money> cr then, and our generosity in this case indicates the extent of our gratitude.
19.Start: There is this contract with Trocter & Campbell, the leading tobacco company in this region. Business in our system isn't too good because of the ever more stringent healthcare requirements. Our marketing experts recommend that we start looking for new markets, especially with the pelengs. We signed a contract with a big dealer network on <ToPlanet> (<ToStar> system), and now their tasters need to get a <clr>test batch of the product <clrEnd>.
