We are giving you this mission, seeing that you are an experienced merchant pilot, on condition that you deliver by <Date> at the latest. Your contract is worth <Money> cr, excluding insurance and hazard allowances.

End: Great, the maloq flag has arrived. While waiting for it, dimwitted maloq storm troopers spent time terrorizing the locals and destroying a number of buildings. Now we fear that if they fail to win the exercise, there will be further large-scale destruction. They could also go at each other's throats and then blame us for the carnage. To prevent them from losing, we have taken a number of tactical measures. Some walls were replaced with props that fall at a mere push; locks have been marked with "Beware of Open Door" signs, and red arrows have been painted on corridor walls to point to the flag pole. On top of it all, our military have been ordered to use only immobilizing weapons and only on our own troops. This way, our chances of winning stand at .03%, taking into account possible disorientation of the opponent.
Ranger, we are about to transfer the amount of <Money> cr to your account for helping us free planet <ToPlanet> from maloq occupation.
Start: Ranger <Player>, here are urgent orders from the maloq government! A military exercise will soon be held on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. With faeyans and maloqs participating. A group of our troopers is to raise a maloq flag in the middle of the newest faeyan base. And this is no joke! As is well known, a single maloq space trooper can break a steel door with his bare hands! Besides, our brave warriors will be well equipped.

Naturally, the fae find it hard to believe that our guys could win. On the other hand, we think that our opponents will try to win by deceit. Puny creatures cannot play fair, can they? For that reason, just to be on the safe side, we we are giving you this <clr>maloq flag<clrEnd> that has a powerful charge hidden inside the pole. If our guys lose, they will break the pole over a knee as a sign of their sorrow, as required by an ancient maloq tradition! This way the fae will pay for their treachery and learn that we are damn serious, even in play. You must deliver this flag to them before <Date>. Is that clear? Now get on with it! Once you arrive at your destination, they will even pay you <Money> cr for it.

End: Oh, <Player>, you have not just brought some world class cultural treasures to our planet! These practical guidebooks will be invaluable to us in such an important matter as educating our young. From now on, these advanced educational techniques will help our children become better prepared for emotional stress and the harsh reality of life.

I would like to specifically mention this one work with an apparent philosophical bend -- Little Red Riding Hood. It's as if it was written about the gaals. The wolf here is the temptation by chaos, which the girl could not resist. She was then rescued by the hunters -- the fighters for the purity of the world. However, I am not going to bother the brave ranger with my blabbering and will simply transfer <Money> cr to your account.
Start: <Player>, do you happen to know they are facing a crisis of education on the gaalian planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system? Their kids became so emotionally sensitive because of the overhumane methods of upbringing that they turned out to be unable to comprehend the reality adequately.

In order to help solve the problem, the gaals have studied our human educational methods and found them to be very effective. All our children get emotionally hardened from a very tender age because they are being constantly intimidated by all those imaginary monsters, such as boogiemen, vampires, poltergeists, mummies, trolls and whatnot. Heck, even infants are taught that their cradle can fall off a tree top and the fall would split their head right open!

The gaals ordered an entire <clr>shipment of the Alles Kaput series educational books for children<clrEnd> from the libraries of planet <FromPlanet>. We request that you deliver them before <Date> in exchange for a fee of <Money> cr. But be careful -- the books are fairly old hard copies, all pre-electronic, and need to be handled with the utmost care.

End: Now you are talking, <Player>! What a great bunch of bulky ancient <clr>Windows<clrEnd> systems that our best minds just love working with. Well, if you can call them that.
I hope you haven't held any copies back, have you? We are afraid of pirated copies. Just kidding -- we maloqs fear neither pirates nor their copies! Here are your <Money> cr for a job well done.
Start: Dear <Player>, our computer historians discovered one of the very first computer viruses that used to plague information systems on planet <clr>Earth<clrEnd> in the ancient times. The epidemic of this <clr>Windows<clrEnd> virus was so widespread that even the best antivirus software of the times -- such as <clr>Lynux<clrEnd> and <clr>Eunux<clrEnd> -- could do precious little to beat it down.

We were about to destroy that find, but all of a sudden a certain corporation, Maloqsoft from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system, offered us quite an attractive amount for it. It's hard to say what they need it for, but since we need it even less we'd be more than happy to get rid of this dangerous relic. We suggest you deliver this <clr>consignment of CD-ROMs <clrEnd> before <Date>, and Maloqsoft corporation will pay you <Money> cr upon arrival.

End: Oh, <Player>, what you have delivered is invaluable. The truth is somewhere nearby. Studying different peoples' memories is both the source of Wisdom and the surest way to Reverence and Enlightenment.
Let the sense of utmost satisfaction of being connected to the truth be a better reward for you than this <Money> cr that really isn't worth much in this world.
22.Start: As of late, the gaals have started to show a keen interest in human religions, ecclesiastical literature, different types of mystic practices and other esoteric things. They ordered a whole bunch of different <clr>religious items<clrEnd> from us, which we ask you to deliver to them in exchange for a fee of <Money> cr. Deliver this freight to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system before <Date>, and you'll see how grateful those spiritualists can be.

End: Excellent work, <Player>. Nicely done. Now, give me the clock. I see the humans made a wonderful mechanism for us, the charge is all right, excellent. This infernal contraption simply has to work on time, doesn't it. By the way, here's your <Money> cr.

I dare hope that our Supreme Lyakusha won't survive today. She is to pass down her authority and die beautifully. Otherwise, she will be shamed, mocked and slung mud at. The great ceremony of <clr>Bhaga-pasyaga<clrEnd> is the newest and most emotional peleng rite. It's only two hundred years old but it has already captured our citizens' hearts.
Start: We have some urgent business for you, <Player>! The oldest and best known delivery service, MHS -- which, by the way, stands for Make Haste Slowly -- from planet <FromPlanet> is to deliver a clockwork to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system for the famous amorphous clock that belongs to the queen of that planet. You're a business-oriented ranger and should know how honorable this mission is.

You need to deliver it before the great <clr>Bhaga-pasyaga<clrEnd> scheduled to be held on <Date> starts. You are to hand it over to our representative and he will ceremonially present the clockwork to Her Majesty. There are going to be a lot of people there and they will all see this... bright gift. You follow, don't you? You're a pirate, after all! And by the way, you will be paid <Money> cr for making this delivery.

End: Thanks for delivering this Rubik's cube. This thing is ideal for exercising our brains and we even want to start mass producing such cubes.

What are you mumbling there about some luxurious palace? Oh, <Player>, quit pulling my anti-gravitational leg! Luxurious, you say? Nonsense! The maloqs don't understand this concept! Of course, some people think that we maloqs are not smart enough. But in this case, you're the fool if you believed in all those fairy tales about palaces and such.
We will transfer <Money> cr to your account so that you could prop your intellectual abilities up a bit.
Start: ...I don't want to hear anything else. It's going to be twenty centimeters, period!

Ah, <Player>, I'm sorry, that was for our partners from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. Those precious maloqs contracted us to build them an unusually luxurious <clr>presidential palace<clrEnd> with tons of room and amenities they are usually not in the market for. There's going to be thirty dining rooms alone at that place! What is unique about the technology used there is that our engineers managed to pack the entire facility into a cube with an edge of twenty centimeters. They achieved such a phenomenal result due to the newest technologies of the pseudospatial furl. In all fairness, this palace is the first prototype of its kind, which needs to be delivered to its destination and unpacked to its original size. We would like to hire you to deliver this cargo and will pay you <Money> cr if it safely gets to its destination before <Date>.

End: Dear <Player>! We thank you for this delivery of disodane. This is a very valuable mineral, and it will help us push our psychozombification studies to new heights.
No problem at all.
You came all this way to deliver the mineral to us! Tell us, did you feel like your mental state was being affected or anything?
No problem at all.
You sound like a broken record. Take the money, at least. We have transferred <Money> cr to your account.
No problem at all.
All right, I see... My poor pilot, you have been undoubtedly, and irreversibly, affected by this mineral. Your sacrifice is worth much more than this miserable handful of credits.
Start: <Player>, we will always have a job for someone with a fast cargo ship. A very unusual asteroid has just exploded in the vicinity of our planet <FromPlanet> and it has most likely come from outside our Galaxy because the debris contained some previously unknown minerals.

One of them, <clr>disodane<clrEnd>, appears to have some very interesting properties indeed. Since it is rapidly approaching the state of complete decay, you will only have <Day> days to deliver it to our faeyan colleagues on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system for a series of experiments.

By the way, our scientists suspect that disodane may have a profound influence upon one's mental state -- up to and including complete zombification. For that reason, we are offering you <Money> cr for this delivery. This is a very good price.

End: Ah, here are the new processors! Wonderful, <Player>, just wonderful. Although, we do not exactly need these for the billboards right now, so we're just going to use the processors for the personal computers of our government officials.

You may wonder, of course, why an official may need such a powerful system? The thing is that in order to be able to make tough and destructive decisions officials need plenty of practice and intensive training. Have you ever heard the term "political games"? It's not a metaphor at all! Our leaders are training day and night with little rest, trying to discover new, more effective ways to ensure survival. Our games have everything: day, night, sound, and smell. Only endless practice on political simulators allows one to achieve -- and most importantly, preserve -- power. Then again, ranger, you need not know all of the nuances. Here's your <Money> cr, which is only a small part of our gratitude.
Start: We are lucky to have met a business-savvy ranger! Have you ever encountered a situation where a client is waiting for a shipment, but the carrier cannot deliver it due to force majeure circumstances? Our partners from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system are waiting for us to deliver a <clr>shipment of processors<clrEnd> for new billboards that we have developed. However, our means of transportation came to a standstill at the most inopportune moment.

If you can deliver the cargo to its destination before <Date>, we'll pay you a bonus of <Money> cr. Don't worry though, the processors are very small and won't take up a lot of space aboard your ship.

End: Did you bring the database of peleng criminals? This is unbelievable, <Player>, you have honestly earned your <Money> cr!

I must admit that the humans have managed to put an excellent album together. We are happy to see such a magnificent cohort of outstanding pirates in a single book. I suppose this must be made available to schools and colleges. Young lyakushas should be able to learn from real life role models.
Start: Despite the difficulties we are facing fighting dominators, more and more regular citizens are taking the slippery path of piracy, a tendency best observed among the pelengs. In order to help the pelengs fight crime, our law enforcement have developed a special multi-volume issue of the <clr>"Wanted by GalaPol"<clrEnd> magazine dedicated exclusively to peleng criminals.

The magazine looks like an old-fashioned police filing system in an armored case. We are planning to give it to our colleagues on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. And you, <Player>, will be our police courier. If you deliver the package before <Date>, law enforcement agencies will pay you <Money> cr from their own funds.

End: Have you brought us a package from planet <FromPlanet>? Let's see. There's even a postcard there!

All right, let's have us a read: "Hello, old friend! How's it going, how is your wife? As promised, I'm sending you a couple of bottles of cognac from the boss' cellar. Unfortunately I couldn't get them through customs, but I managed to send the package via some of our clandestine channels with one very naive ranger."
Oops, sorry, the rest of it is private. Oh yeah, I almost forgot. Here's your payment of <Money> cr and thanks for making it so fast!
Start: Ranger <Player>, the government of planet <FromPlanet> has authorized me to offer you this urgent top-secret mission. You must deliver this <clr>parcel<clrEnd> containing important intelligence data to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system and hand it directly to our agent. It contains a key to a code, which in turn is a key to another code, which our representative on <ToPlanet> has in his possession.

Please try to deliver the package before <Date> and be extremely careful -- you of all people should know who counts on the success of this mission! If you succeed in delivering the package, you'll receive a payment of <Money> cr and be placed on the list of honorable agents of planet <FromPlanet>'s government. Good luck, <Player>, you'll need it!

End: Dear <Player>, I see that you've delivered a <clr>new anthem<clrEnd> from the planet of our faeyan friends! Yeah, we've also been thinking about changing our own anthem. Between you and me -- in the old version of the anthem, our ancestors had made some good old-fashioned fun of the fae. It's because of some old bad blood between our two nations harking back to the old times. Fortunately, all of this is now done and over with. We were about to apologize to the faeyan side and write a new anthem, but they beat us to it. It'll make it all the better now.

By the way, what's this incomprehensible line in the second verse? Then again, who could make anything out of this faeyan dialect anyway. Let it be. Oh, here's your <Money> cr for helping us strengthen friendship between peoples of this Galaxy!
Start: You were lucky enough to receive an important mission of diplomacy and ethics from the faeyan governmental hierarchy. <FromPlanet> and <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system are sister planets. About three hundred years ago, our human partners wrote the majestic <clr>anthem "Let the Galaxy of Peace Prosper Forever"<clrEnd>, which became the symbol of our friendship. Back then, due to a bad quality recording, we could not make out one line of the anthem. But today, thanks to our latest technologies, we managed to decode it and sadly, this is how it reads: The fae are witty and clever, but their faces are as ugly as ever. This line caused an outrage amongst many of our citizens!

We wanted to pay the humans back for this in the very same currency and wrote a <clr>new anthem<clrEnd>, which we would like you to deliver to the intended addressees before <Date>. You'll be payed <Money> cr if you do.

3.End: What is it you brought us, <Player>? The brain of the president of planet <FromPlanet>, you say? As an amateur zoologist I can assure you that this is a brain of a maloq burkusha monkey -- and a great specimen at that. Well, our geneticists will transplant it into the cranium of a female cave baboon and examine her reactions, which will constitute the next great step in our effort to study the zoology of lower vertebrates. The amount of <Money> cr you will be paid for your services will come from planet <ToPlanet>'s scientific research budget.
Start: We have an important mission for you. Our president is negotiating hard with the humans about the colonization of uninhabited planets. Humans cannot live there because their weak constitution makes procreation next to impossible under such harsh conditions. But the excessive greed this race is notorious for prevents them from yielding to our demands.

Our president challenged their president to a duel, throwing his armored glove into his face as the applicable human tradition requires. Now our president is on the way to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system to kill their president who has just recovered from plastic surgery to have the dent in his skull repaired. This is the only true solution to this problem. Our council has already issued him a license to kill, and the president is on his way to do his duty.

To ensure our president's security during the flight, his <clr>brain<clrEnd> in the state of deep hypersleep will be transported separately -- as a regular package aboard your spaceship. Then the body and the brain will be put together again. But you have to deliver it before <Date>, or this mighty maloq brain will die. Hurry up, and you will be rewarded handsomely!

End: Well, <Player>, thanks for successfully delivering the "toothbrush," which in fact was a bug left at the diplomatic hotel of planet <FromPlanet> entirely on purpose. This isn't the first case where the fae found our spying devices and gave them back to us without realizing what was going on. No wonder the pelengs manage to fool them all the time.

Tell me, why would they want to replace the memory stick that was concealed within the handle of the brush? Of course, I do understand that the memory was insufficient, and they replaced it with something more powerful. But they could have copied the information back to it! Who would want a reformatted brush, all squeaky clean, complete with a telescoping gamma-ray emitter? It's as if these fae are trying to make fools of us!
But I may be taking it a little too close to heart. You've done us a great service by bringing back this item and absolutely deserve your reward of <Money> cr.
Start: Would it inconvenience my dear <Player> too much to deliver an urgent parcel to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system? This is a device that the human ambassador left behind in the bathroom when he was coming for a short visit. The item provoked an interest amongst our wisest dalani, and we found out that it's called a "toothbrush" and serves as an instrument for hygienic care of the internal cavity of the head. However the humans are mistaken about its functionality -- the device is extremely inefficient, with an efficiency ratio of only 2.05%. This have been confirmed by thorough experiments.

As a token of our good will, we have upgraded the device and would like to return the improved version to its rightful owner. Now it not only cleans the human cranial cavity, but also improves mental fabrications, stimulating blood circulation in the brain cells and restoring the aura, as well as enhances the nutritious environment for valuable symbiotic bacteria, which the humans refer to as "caries monsters." None of the humans have such a unique device. You'll be payed <Money> cr if you deliver this magnificent gift by <Date>.

End: Dear <Player>, thank you for delivering the video of us testing our new weapon of mass persuasion <clr>"Maxpa-1"<clrEnd>. We will transfer the amount of <Money> cr to your account immediately. Now, that's what we call a great delivery service all around! You must have been shocked when watching the footage, isn't that so? Ha, thought so! Planet <FromPlanet> became a truly invaluable testing ground for us.

Now we know it for sure that a one megaton head can destroy at least one hundred thousand people. And while the "criminals" are being publicly tried, we will build us a bulkier version of the weapon, the <clr>"Maxpa-2"<clrEnd>. Hopefully, next time the results will exceed our expectations tenfold. New tests will be conducted on a peleng planet. As a quid pro quo, the pelengs will text some new ragobam virus on us, but that's not something we would be afraid of. We maloqs are young and strong and will simply shrug off any of those wicked peleng plagues. Well, except maybe some of the seniors, but so what?
Start: We have a very important government mission for you. We need a representative from planet <FromPlanet> to attend a trial on maloq planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system.

Let me fill you in. The crux of the matter is that some maloqs were using our planet to make a historical movie about the klissan. Our red brothers envisioned the enemy ravaging captured planets as huge heads with plentiful sharp teeth. So the maloqs built what they deemed to be a huge klissan head that, according to their script, would pop its humongous jaws hovering over a city. But once the shooting started, something went terribly wrong and the head plunged right down, onto the innocent civilians. Hundreds of thousands died! And the maloqs, they quickly packed up and went back home, to planet <ToPlanet>, leaving the completed footage behind.

We contacted the maloq government, and they apologized and said that the perpetrators would be put on trial starting on <Date>, and that they need the disks with the video record of the disaster as evidence to make sure the villains are successfully prosecuted. Now, would you take it upon yourself to help justice prevail?

And while you are thinking about it, let me also add that whoever agrees to deliver the disks will also be given a special record player to be able to play them and see the carnage in all its gory splendor. And let me tell you, <Player>, this isn't your usual horror flick! Besides, timely delivery will earn you a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Thank you for delivering this great faeyan painting to us. Believe it or not, <Player>, even on our planet there are some that can truly appreciate faeyan art. Here is your <Money> cr for speedy delivery.
Faeyan art is kind of strange, wouldn't you say? That "enter password" sign against the white background is truly impressive.
Start: Here's a cultural mission ordered by faeyan administration. Some time ago Faeyanardo, the best of our transhumanitarianists, made a famous <clr>painting<clrEnd> and auctioned it off through GaidNet. You've heard of this pan-Galactic computer network, haven't you? The highest bidder remained anonymous, the only thing known about him being that he lives in the <ToStar> system, on planet <ToPlanet>.

Your mission is to deliver the canvas to its new owner. Please note that the painting incorporates the latest faeyan copyright protection technology, which means that you can only see the actual image once every hundred years, or after entering the password. If the password is entered incorrectly or after a certain expiration date, the image will disappear for the next one hundred years. We will set the activation date for <Date> at the latest. We hope that you will deliver the painting by then. Once you accomplish this mission, you will be paid <Money> cr.

End: Thank you, <Player>! We have almost lost the use of our robot assistants. Had you not delivered this faeyan <clr>heniroil<clrEnd> on time, we'd have to do everything by ourselves. The management of our spaceport would like you to accept this modest reward of <Money> cr as a sign of our gratitude.
Hey, you, <clr>B-243<clrEnd>, get me a beer and get yourself ready for some maintenance. I have some <clr>heniroil<clrEnd> for you.
Sorry, <Player>, I digress. Work, work, and more work, that's how it always is. It's hard to imagine how we would ever manage it without the fae. These techies sure know their lubricants.
Start: We have an exclusive mission from the space terminal network administration. Our planet now has a surplus of <clr>heniroil<clrEnd>, while planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system has a shortage.

For more efficient management of fuel and lubricant stock, we need to send some of this oil right here, to this little dot on the map. If you can accomplish the mission within <Day> days, a fee of <Money> cr will be transferred to your account.

End: Oh, you brought us the red buttons, <Player>! Great! Here is your <Money> cr for speedy delivery.

These faeyan buttons are fairly good, of course, at least they work every time, unlike that crap we produce locally. Unfortunately, they are not very durable. Heck, almost disposable even! You know how it is, don't you? You jam that button, the missile goes whoosh, and the button is kaput! The last consignment we got had long been broken, so now we are forced to wage war without some of our most efficient weapons. Then again, a maloq soldier could work miracles with his bare hands. Say, I could do a miracle job on your face right here and now. Ha-ha, just kidding! Good man, excellent work!
Start: Ranger, you are now a preferred candidate for a mission for an electronic accessories factory. As you may know, national leadership of all the races have those special red buttons at their disposal. You may also be aware that all the red buttons in the Galaxy are being made right here, on our planet <FromPlanet>. This is why they are so famously durable.

Your new mission is to deliver a shipment of <clr>red buttons<clrEnd> to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. Here are the exact coordinates. You will be paid <Money> cr, but only if you make the delivery on or before <Date>.

End: This is fantastic! <clr>Psy-weapons<clrEnd> is just what we need at the moment. Apparently, those faeyans are really short for cash if they suddenly lost all their scruples about who they are selling weapons to.

And you, <Player>, can now claim your <Money> cr for a job well done. First off, we will make these weapons available to our schools. Teachers will now be able to unleash psychic attacks against their students to warn them off cheating, or rather teach them to be more discreet. Cruel, perhaps... But oh sooo effective! I mean, look at the Dzuhallag that is now prospering due to such technologies. Now our entire planet will prosper as well. All of it thanks to you!
Start: Ranger, you have been selected for a very prestigious mission that would be of great help to the military industries of planet <FromPlanet>. On this planet, our main export is clr>psy-weapons<clrEnd>, of which we are a renowned manufacturer. One of our most profitable clients has just placed an order for a large quantity of these hi-tech weapons. The deal is not a hundred percent kosher, so in order to avoid any unwanted attention we decided to ship them aboard a vessel that could not be easily identified as a transport -- such as your little sloop, <Player>.

The weapons will be stowed away in your cargo bay, and once you take off head for planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. If you make the delivery before <Date>, you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Thank you, <Player>! The fae have done a great job, which is not in the least surprising since that's the only way they know how to do them. Amazingly, this player does not only play back the music itself but also augments it with bubbling and croaking arrangements from the swamp sound library!
It's been a while since I last heard something so beautiful. It is my pleasure to pay you your fee of <Money> cr out of the marathon fund.
Start: It is very inspiring that a criminal such as yourself would even want to make an honest buck! A dance marathon is about to start on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system in the next <Day> days. The event itself is fairly dull, everybody twists and turns awkwardly to some kind of beat. Still, for a true faeyan this is a great opportunity to showcase our new technological developments. The peleng organizers somehow procured -- by having robbed a human transport, most likely -- a large quantity of old records that they want to use for the marathon. However, they are missing a record player.

They placed an order with us to make them a <clr>record player<clrEnd>. We have successfully accomplished that task, and now all that remains is to deliver the player before the event starts. The pelengs promised to pay the courier a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Thank you very much, <Player>! Throngs of gamers of all kinds are already besieging their local game shops all over the planet, anxious to try out the new faeyan games.

They are said to have some totally unheard of features. There is even a rumor that these games zombify humans, and that the fae are trying to enslave us this way. We don't know yet what to make of this information, we have to try them out first. In the meantime, here's your fee of <Money> cr. You've done a great job.
Start: We are offering a delivery contract for independent transport owners. You are probably unaware of the sad little fact that the humans have been trying for a thousand-odd years to create a computer game one would really want to play. Instead, they keep producing cheesy doomsday shooters with boring gameplay. Out of pure scientific curiosity, our researchers interested in mental activities of lesser developed races made an attempt to come up with a quality computer game for human consumption.

This is a special biogame, or rather a whole set of them where the human brain would interact with the software for enhanced effect. Once inserted into the cerebellum, the chip would take over all of the human player's emotions and feelings. The player would then get all those fantastic sensations that may also be fairly addictive.

Some of the human planets have already shown a great deal of interest in this new development of ours. One of them is planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. We would like you to deliver a <clr>test batch of these games<clrEnd> to them. If you can make it by <Date>, a total of <Money> cr will be transferred to your account.

End: Good health to you, <Player>! Have you brought that new fabric for military uniforms that the maloqs were so eager to get from the fae? Great! We couldn't lay our hands on it, so we hired those cunning pelengs to do it for us. What do you know, they did deliver! They have talked the fae into giving away all those high technologies for free under the pretext that they are now obsolete.
Ha-ha-ha! You know great saboteurs when you see them! Here's your <Money> cr, and good luck in battle!
Start: Our planet is currently hosting a giveaway event called Goodbye, Old Technology that involves a free transfer of materiel to the maloq army, such as a large quantity of <clr>self-sealing armored fabric <clrEnd> for military uniforms. You may find it surprising that we are helping maloq military industries of our own accord. However, this isn't quite what it looks like. This fabric is a fairly old technology that, though not very likely to add much to the maloqs' combat readiness, may help improve the political relations between our two races.

Seeing that you are an independent combat pilot, we would like you to deliver this cargo to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system before <Date>. Once you are done, we will pay you a bonus of <Money> cr.

End: Oh, <Player>, you have no idea how valuable the device you have brought is to us! Indeed, the maloqs made an attempt to colonize new worlds but our robots went too far out of range and now we cannot find them. This is where this new server you brought will come in handy since we'll be able to use it to send signals directly into hyperspace. Here's your <Money> cr and stand at ease!

We are going to test the new device right away. That's great timing too. A faeyan liner seems to be in distress in hyperspace not too far from here. So we are going to test the server, locate the ship and save those lost faeyan souls. Since the fae helped maloqs out so, maloqs are going to save some faeyan bacon as well.
Start: Ranger, please use your brain to get to the very bottom of this problem. As it turns out, the maloqs from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system are working on a comprehensive project to colonize some remote sectors of our Galaxy. In the course of the project, they have dispatched navigational robots to different arms of the Galaxy. However, the dumb gizmos flew so far out that they are now out of range of their tracking station. To resolve this problem, they ordered a special <clr>navigation server<clrEnd> from us that can send and receive signals to and from hyperspace.

However, you should understand that we have little interest in seeing the maloqs expand even further. As it is, they have already gone beyond what's reasonable. For that reason we are going to send them a sabotaged device that will fail to find their targets in 97.99% of all cases. You will be paid a fee of <Money> cr to make this delivery provided you do it before <Date>.

End: Great, you have delivered a new replica of the maloq red bug! The management of the Galactic Macropromexpo will now pay you <Money> cr for timely delivery.

We have never seen any mechanical statues of such enormous proportions. Such a small insect and such a large replica! And the color is so beautiful! Now we should give the bugger a couple of guns to hold! And maybe a red helmet too, to make it look more fierce. Don't you agree, <Player>? Anyhow, your admiring face alone makes it clear that this idea of ours is pure genius.
Start: Yes, we do have a mission for a merchant. Our manufacturers of large forms managed to recreate an exact replica of our smallest insect -- making it thousands of times larger. The replica will be exhibited at the Macropromexpo -- an exhibition of large items that is currently taking place on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. This project is extremely important for our maloq industries since displaying such a unique item will surely promote greater respect for the maloqs throughout the Galaxy.

Our last large form was in fact so large and heavy that the transport it was on simply could not launch and crashed back to the ground causing a lot of damage. However, we did come up with a new, better design. The new model weighs only half as much, so the maloqs trust you could transport it, all the more so since you have a large and spacious merchant ship. Head for the <ToStar> system and deliver this cargo no later than <Date>. The exhibition promoters will pay you a fee of <Money> cr once you are there.

End: Did you bring the case with electronic bugs? Excellent!

Gaalian intelligence will think they have tricked us. But we know they have been broadcasting cooked data all along. Otherwise how would you explain their behavior? After all, everyone has secrets to keep, right? Not too long ago, we got to observe their government meeting -- if you can call it a meeting, that is. A whole bunch of folks got together, young and old, and went round and round singing some boring songs. Then the oldest of them said he was tried and the meeting was going to be rescheduled. Is this how you do government business? No, they are obviously trying to fool us!
However, we have no beef with you, <Player>. The bugs are all intact. You are going to be paid <Money> cr, and you have our gratitude.
Start: Ranger <Player>, would you feel amenable enough to help our intelligence services? Our suspicious human friends from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system keep planting their <clr>listening devices<clrEnd> with us and don't much bother trying to conceal the effort. We are quite happy that the humans are so interested in our way of life and hopeful to learn from our experience. Unfortunately, it so happens that these bugs of theirs are hardly ever planted in all the right places and thus cannot provide them with a complete picture.

We have been thinking awhile now about how to streamline this information transfer. We even considered ordering more advanced models form the fae. But then the right decision came unexpectedly and all by itself. It's as simple as life itself too. We installed our own video and audio surveillance devices. Now any human can connect to GaidNet, which I am sure you know is our pan-Galactic computer network, and see for himself or herself what the life of each particular gaal looks like at any given moment of time!

As to the old bugs, we decided to pluck them all out and give them back to the humans. Everything is in good shape and in perfect working condition. However, the microchips in that special case we are using to ship them will only work for <Day> days. This is your window for delivering this fragile cargo. Upon arrival, you will be paid <Money> cr.

End: Thank you, <Player>! You did bring us some fresh <clr>gekkers<clrEnd>, didn't you? Here is your fee of <Money> cr.

Hang on a sec, but they are all dead! They're not moving! You couriers are all the same! By the time you finally drag your feet into port here the gekkers are all cold and stiff! Oh well, forget it, diners at the restaurant are going to be none the wiser.
Start: Dear <Player>, we are breeding these small semi-intelligent creatures called <clr>gekkers<clrEnd> that work very fast and are widely used in construction. The government of planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system ordered a small shipment of <clr>gekkers<clrEnd> from us.

We cannot ship them via regular carriers since it takes way too long. <clr>Gekkers<clrEnd> do not take to zero gravity well and lose their qualities. But we heard a lot of good about your fast pirate ship and would like you to take up this mission. To make the job easier, we have put the entire bunch to cryo-sleep, so they will be able to survive in space for exactly <Day> days. The maloqs will pay you <Money> cr once you deliver the cargo to their planet.

42.End: Greetings, <Player>! Winters on our planet may at times be so harsh that red paint peels off our combat ships. Now the gaals have sent us these great special covers, so an entire squadron of brand new combat ships will be well-protected. Here is <Money> cr for your troubles.
Start: In the name of Spiritual Unification we are happy to greet you, <Player>! We have a special garment factory on planet <FromPlanet> that makes <clr>warm clothes<clrEnd> for people in all walks of life that work hard and in hard conditions.

For humanitarian reasons, we are going to send a large shipment of such clothes to maloq ice scrubbers that work in totally inhumane conditions, with no hygiene at the ice mines of planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. If you deliver this cargo to those hapless maloq grunts before <Date>, the great satisfaction of having helped your neighbor will be all yours. Naturally, we will also pay you <Money> cr.

End: Hello, <Player>! Gaals do know their business! The secret truth serum that you tried to smuggle in under the guise of a pizza is working perfectly!

As has been proven experimentally, after eating that pizza our volunteer only needed five minutes to reveal his true feelings about the law enforcement authorities of planet <ToPlanet>, his wife and his mother-in-law. We could never even dream of ever getting such a fantastic interrogation tool as this pizza! We will immediately make the recipe available to all our detention centers. Here is your delivery fee of <Money> cr.
43.Start: You know, <Player>, we have recently learned that the humans too have this taste for a certain dish of culinary extravagance that makes one's guts cringe. I am talking about pizza here. Our food scientists developed a new type of pizza that does not have any harmful ingredients. As a token of our friendship and unity with the humans, we would like to send the recipe for this pizza to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. We would like to hire you for this mission, <Player>. Time is of the essence here, so please do all you can to make this delivery before <Date>. We will make sure to pay you a fee of <Money> cr.

End: For your information, <Player>, what you have delivered is a scientific exhibit of great importance that has the potential to flip our classic ideas about space and time upside down. If our calculations are correct, then the second axis of the continuum is not as convergent as we used to think earlier, which is convincingly illustrated by this sample.

We may have made yet another large step towards being able to control time. Why don't you try to reflect upon possible implications of such a discovery in the next 5 days? Besides, that would be a great way for you to make <Money> cr while helping promote scientific research.
Start: Some students in our lowest academic quartile conducted a laboratory exercise to freeze a <clr>ray of light in a piece of ice<clrEnd>. Some of the best minds of planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system declared the experiment a great scientific discovery and requested that it be presented at the next symposium on the issues of time to be held there.

They believe this experiment to bear on time, which is actually incorrect since the second axis of the continuum is absolutely convergent -- something that had already been proven by our distant ancestors. However, we cannot refuse their request because this would run contrary to the great principle of the Integrity of Knowledge. Please deliver this item to them by <Date> at the latest, and the satisfaction of being a part of this great discovery will be reward enough for you all by itself. Plus, of course, you will be paid <Money> cr upon arrival.

End: So the portal has been delivered. Thanks for your good work, the amount of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account.

All right, just to test this thing out let's try to get us some beer from planet <FromPlanet>. But what's this? Order a can of beer -- get a bowl of water. Is that the way it's support to work? It's either this technology still requires some serious debugging or the gaals simply have no beer. What do you think, <Player>?
45.Start: Together with our human friends and partners from planet <ToPlanet>, we have developed a teleporter prototype that will connect our planets outside the boundaries of time and space and allow for instant exchange of cargo. This is an experimental model that is still under development; however the first operating component has already been completed and awaits to be shipped. We call it <clr>Beta Portal 01<clrEnd>, and it will need to be installed on the receiving end -- on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. Please deliver the device within the next <Day> days. Just try to imagine this permanent bridge across time and space between our two friendly nations! What could be more exciting? And don't forget the neat amount of <Money> cr you will be paid for your troubles.

End: What is this? Why did you bring us this container with our very own junior diplomat who had had his memory purged, tongue amputated and other body parts altered as a punishment. Oh, yes, and then we exiled what was left of him to a distant gaalian planet.

And to add insult to injury we will now have to pay you the amount of <Money> cr. It says it right here, in your waybill. So what do we do with this container now? Most likely we will be sending it to some godforsaken asteroid in the middle of nowhere.
Start: It is a sad fact that rare species of exotic creatures are becoming extinct. Some time ago, a peleng delegation recklessly abandoned one of their domestic animals on our planet. Having checked our database of rare and valuable animal species, we found out that this was a <clr>Decrepitliptus Vulgaris<clrEnd>, one of the lower forms of the peleng leprace animals: it looks like a peleng but walks on four legs, is covered with green fur, cannot talk, and shakes its head all the time.

We sincerely hope that the pelengs treat lesser creatures right and suggest you deliver this lost animal to its rightful owners on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. We trust this will help preserve biological diversity we all need. We will place the animal into a special survival container where it will be safe for <Day> days. We hope this will give you enough time to make your delivery. We will even pay you a per diem of <Money> cr. Good luck, <Player>, and Godspeed!

End: Ten-shun! At ease! The gaals claim maloq military software has bugs in it. But this just can't be since there can be nothing better than properly licensed software in general and maloq software in particular. Those conniving gaals simply envy us, or maybe they are even planning an act of sabotage against us.

Still, chances are this <clr>programmator<clrEnd> could after all be put to some good use somewhere. It's pretty heavy, and all metal; maybe we could use it for scrap. You will be paid <Money> cr for this delivery -- at the scrap metal rate. Fall out!
Start: Do you know, <Player>, that we are very concerned about the maloq army not being properly and sufficiently equipped? We have recently discovered yet another software vulnerability in the onboard computers of maloq military spaceships. This appears to be an exploit that dominators frequently use to put this equipment out of order. Apparently, the maloq army is getting its software from the notorious <clr>Maloqsoft<clrEnd> corporation.

To help our maloq friends out, we have developed a special <clr>programmator<clrEnd> that will help them eliminate this pesky flaw in their fleet software. By taking no more than <Day> days to deliver it to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system, you will do a huge favor to the maloq fleet and make a substantial contribution to our common fight against dominators. And if that is not enough, you will also be paid a fee of <Money> cr.

End: Ha-ha, what kind of a <clr>Universe Scanner<clrEnd> is that? Oh, it shows how well your brain works, you say?

Apparently, it is out of order because once you point it at me it shows nothing at all. But when we point it at you it shows that you want your <Money> cr. Oh, all right, there you go. May you always hit the bull's brain! I mean bull's eye! Hit your earnings targets, that is. That's what I mean.
Start: We have a mission for an upstanding citizen such as yourself, <Player>. We are positive it will be a great honor for a merchant such as yourself to deliver this <clr>Universe Scanner<clrEnd> to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system.

I can see the bewildered look in your eyes. The <clr>Universe Scanner<clrEnd> is a unique device that will analyze astral flows and transform them into chunks of useful information. Or, in plain language, it reads minds. You will be paid <Money> cr provided you deliver the scanner to the maloqs within <Day> days.

End: Ah, and here comes <Player>! Well, well, well, what did you bring us this time?

A device to neutralize radiation? Great, we could probably rig it to increase the radioactivity of ragobam bullfrogs' saliva, which is something we have been working on lately. Here is your <Money> cr for this delivery.
Start: You, <Player>, have been walking down the road to perdition on the wrong side of the law! Would you like to do a noble thing for a change and maybe get rid of some negative energy and lift the burden off your conscience? We have some information about a natural disaster on planet <ToPlanet> located in the <ToStar> system. Apparently, there has been a catastrophic eruption with large quantities of radioactive magma spewed out. To help our peleng friends, we are going to send them a <clr>spherical shield<clrEnd> -- a unique device capable of neutralizing radioactivity across large territories.

You could improve your self-esteem and feel proud next time you look at yourself in the mirror if you deliver this device to those who need it. Besides, we can guarantee that you will be paid a fee of <Money> cr.
However, please try to do your best to make this delivery by <Date>, or it may be too late for those poor pelengs.

End: I see, <Player>, that you have brought the evidence from planet <FromPlanet>. Though really, what kind of evidence is it anyway? They are just two hairs of maloq red-belly stinkers, two old khassats and a Dzuhallag badge. Junk, basically.

By the way, for your information, our psy-trackers are already tailing some suspects in the spaceport of planet <FromPlanet>. We are going to test our remote copperscope on them to fish out the information we need. So, really, we have no use for the evidence you brought, and it will be destroyed as investigation materials that are no longer needed.
Regardless, we are grateful for your help with this murder investigation. <Money> cr have already been transferred to your account.
Start: We have this one mission, but it's not going to be much fun. <Player>, we will pay you <Money> cr for delivering some crime scene evidence to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system.

What, you haven't heard of that heinous crime that turned our entire tranquil little planet upside down? Why, three faeyan ambassadors were beheaded in one day! And it all happened on my watch, while I was in charge of the planet's security! I made all those miserable sleuths of ours comb the crime scene with a fine brush a thousand times. Heck, two thousand even! And they did find it, damn it! The evidence needs to be delivered before <Date> or the investigation will go astray.

End: I can't believe it, <Player>! You are giving it back! This <clr>Liberation Helmet<clrEnd> of ours, oh it is so precious! I am an initiate of the Helmet myself, so on behalf of the entire congregation let me pay you this reward of <Money> cr as a token of our appreciation!

By the way, would you like to join us? Come join a different world without dominators, klissan, pirates or anything else for that matter that may burden your restless ranger soul day in and day out. No? Not interested? Well, suit yourself then, remain in this worthless dimension where you are but a pawn in the hands of fate.
Start: Dear <Player>, here's the situation. A certain new religious congregation known as <clr>The Disciples of the Liberation Helmet<clrEnd>, is preaching some very worrisome stuff. They have found a certain helmet that they claim has arrived from a different Universe. They also maintain that once you put the helmet on you will move instantly to a different dimension where a better life awaits you.

Why am I telling you all this? Some time ago, this sacred helmet of theirs was being transported aboard one of our freighters that crashed not far from the orbit. The helmet itself had miraculously survived and was picked up by the escort ships. Now we must return it to those crazy yahoos. However, they do not trust our own transports anymore and demand that we bring in a competent independent contractor. Your reputation speaks for itself, so we would like to offer you <Money> cr to deliver this item to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system before <Date>.

End: <Player>! I am glad to see a brave ranger!

What did you bring us? The gaals are returning to us an ancient statue of the maloq god of harmony Bababoom? Ha! Well, it is indeed a statue of a bababoom warrior, or thunder warrior, if you translate it into your own language. We now call them kamikazes. You see that ball? It's an explosive charge of huge destructive power. A bababoom warrior would sneak into the enemy's camp, bite through the bomb's cover, and everything within a mile's radius would get blown to pieces. It was through the efforts of such thunder warriors that the battle of Ratabam was won.

Man, only the gaals could call a thunder warrior a harmony god. So what did they call the bomb -- the symbol of harmony? Ha-ha! Thank you, ranger, for making me laugh. Those gaals, those stupid idiots!

Here, ranger, take this <Money> cr. The statue itself isn't worth anything, we have tons of them, but at least now I have a great new joke to tell about stupid gaals. And believe me, that in itself is worth serious money.
Start: Yes, <Player>, we have a very special mission for you.

Faeyan scholars are very concerned about the ongoing trend towards sharply lower cultural awareness across the Galaxy. Spiritual degradation among populations of different planets is progressing rapidly. If this trend continues, in some four thousand years every race will lose their intelligence -- that very something that makes us distinctly different from animals. Special attention should be paid to maloqs who, as everyone knows, have never risen much above the animal level to begin with. But do you know, <Player>, that they have not always been like this? Many centuries ago, the maloq society appreciated art very much, and they sought to live in harmony with the surrounding world. It was so inspiring! It was indeed the true golden age of maloq culture!

To preserve and restore the maloq race's spiritual culture, our government launched a program to repatriate maloq cultural valuables to their historical surroundings. Unfortunately, during our quest to learn about the Universe, we gaals took possession of many spiritual and cultural artifacts that belonged to other races in the Galaxy. Now we must make it up to them.

One of the museums on planet <FromPlanet> has an ancient maloq masterpiece -- a statue of a maloq holding an ideal sphere, the symbol of harmony. Some believe it to be the ancient deity Bababoom. We would like you to take it back to planet <ToPlanet> by <Date> -- the day of a great historical holiday celebrated by maloqs.
You will be handsomely compensated by the maloq government.

End: Oh, all right, here's the courier. It doesn't look like you were in any particular hurry. Uh-huh. Encrypted instructions from the client were received two weeks ago. So what do you have there? Oh, it's a container with a flower! A rose! I love roses. And the attached cryptogram must contain the key to the encrypted message, right? We can read it together if you want -- I know rangers are a curious bunch. Let's see... It says it here that a sister-in-arms of the great maloq warrior princess Hannah ka'Boom requests that this human symbol of appreciation be handed in to a certain ranger whose bravery, courage and rugged good looks she admires. And the lucky guy's name is...

Ha-ha! <Player>! It is actually a gift for you, ha-ha! Oh, you the ominous conqueror of maloq princesses and galactic expanses, ha-ha... Haven't had me a laugh like this for a while! Yes... Here is your <Money> cr for this job. However, according to the shipping instructions, the cargo must remain with us. Those dimwit maloqs used a standard order form to ship it. So, alas, the container goes into storage. Even though you are welcome to smell the flower one last time. I feel infinitely magnanimous today.
52.Start: We do have an order from one of our great lady warriors. But what makes you think, <Player>, that you are worthy of delivering it? Your rank? Number of combat missions accomplished? Number of dominators destroyed? Number of skulls crushed and kidneys mangled? Um... OK. That ain't too bad for a human weakling. Listen carefully and do not interrupt! Our client needs this container to be delivered ASAP to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. It has some kind of grass inside. You have until <Date> to deliver and will be paid <Money> cr. Now get on with it!

End: Ah, <Player>, come in. Rumor has it you have some kind of a top secret package for us. Come on, give it to me.
Let's see... And the instructions? Don't tell me they gave you no instructions on how to open this damn package. Either way, maloq security systems are a joke. I am going to show you now.
All right, type in the password... "Password." Done!
Fingerprints... Ranger, give me you hand. Done!
Enter your keyword... "Keyword." Uh-huh!
All right, I am taking out the paper-- Ouch! It hurts! What is it, a mousetrap? Why is there a mousetrap inside?
You think it's funny? You knew it, didn't you? You knew, but you never told me about that mousetrap! All right, here's your <Money> cr, and now get out of my sight! Man, it hurts so much!
Start: I have an assignment for you, ranger. We did some hush-hush business with the humans and now owe a favor to their security service. So I want to reciprocate since they did help us out big time with that lyakusha.

Here you go. You must deliver this parcel to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system and hand it to the secretary of their planet's committee of state security in person. They will pay you <Money> credits right there. But be careful with it, it's a very valuable parcel.

I hope you are not going to look inside, are you? My security people put four levels of protection on it. They'll need to enter a randomly generated verbal password, then a unique key phrase and pass genetic personal identification. We maloqs protect all our secret documents this way. And there's yet another surprise developed by human secret services. It is called... hold on... I have this scrap of paper somewhere... Here we go! It's called an "inert anti-rodent deterrent system with pressure action." How about that! This isn't some load of baloney here. So be careful with it!
Oh yes, I almost forgot. It must be delivered prior to <Date> or the contents will self-destruct... derstuck... Err, it'll break, in a word. Good luck!

End: Ranger <Player>, at last the button has been delivered! Here is your <Money> cr, take it. Now everything is so much clearer than it used to be. The thing is that Francisco is in fact...
Err, never mind, just go. The two thousand one hundred and eighty-second episode of my favorite show is about to begin.
54.Start: You know <Player>, if I were you I'd get me a hanky. The thing is that Maria met Juan Carlos at a reception hosted by her husband Mario. She fell in love with Juan Carlos, and once, while taking a walk in the garden, the two of them stumbled upon another pair of lovebirds. They were Juan Carlos' sister and Mario's father. It so happened that Mario had an illegitimate brother who had left for planet <ToPlanet> where he met Auntie Maria's female cousin. Their daughter came back to planet <FromPlanet> where she married Francisco, Mario's son. So you have <Day> days to get to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system and deliver this button to Maria to prove that she is a great niece of the son of her double removed aunt. Get on with it! If you do a good job, you may be paid <Money> cr by the father-in-law of Mario's daughter-in-law's son's aunt, who is also her mother's brother.

End: Oh, <Player>, you brought our annihilator, didn't you? Unfortunately, the consul has already bought a new, better model. Oh! I've got it! Tomorrow is the day when we dispose of all the trash that accumulated during the year. It is a great holiday too. The annihilator will come in handy, and it should have plenty of power!
Thank you, ranger. Here's your <Money> cr for delivering the device.
Start: Hello, <Player>! We have a mission specifically for you.

As you may be aware, our planet was recently visited by human diplomats from planet <ToPlanet>. Let me tell you, these people can drink! At the banquet, they may have had one too many, and their consul opened fire with his personal annihilator of secret documents using cans of penchecrakus meat for target practice. We even had to rename the Swamp-Green Banquet Hall the Room of 999 Mysterious Holes.

But let's get down to business! It was only after the mission went back home that we discovered that their stupid consul had left his annihilator behind in his hotel room. Our experts played with it a little, and voila, instead of destroying the documents it now sends them right back to our planet using a sophisticated system of floating teleporters. So now we will be aware of all their plans.
Deliver this gadget to <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system prior to <Date>, and on top of the satisfaction of a job well done you will also be paid <Money> cr.

End: <Player>, I am so glad to see you on our planet! You are always a welcome guest, ranger. And what's that strange beeping? Umm...

Oh, you brought us the detector. So quickly, who would have thought... Many thanks, and here's your <Money> cr. You know, <Player>, you did it so fast that I was even thinking of giving you a bonus. There! But there it is again, that strange beeping. Can you hear it? Or maybe it's my ears playing tricks?

So where were we? The bonus? What bonus? I don't remember mentioning any bonuses! Aha! That's the device beeping, the one you brought with you. Those tadpoles must have hidden a beeping mine in it. Duck! I'm gonna get it now!

Damn it! Why is it so fragile? That was just one little whack, it should have been able to withstand that! Ah, never mind, it must have been out of order anyway. All it did was beep. And what may I ask is that? A user manual? Umm... "Set the device up, bring the test subject into the room..." Oh, OK. "...if the test subject lies, the device begins beeping..." But of course! The device must have been out of order. All it did was beep. Or do you think I was lying to you? Huh, ranger? Look me in the eye! I can tell you think I was lying, you miserable space mercenary! Now get out of here while you still can!
Start: We do have a job for you.

A few days ago, we finished testing our next generation lie detector. It was a maloq order; they are going to use it to question their prisoners more effectively. We did everything they asked for: the detector incorporates new state of the art modules for timber and voice range recognition and a revolutionary brain scanning system to determine whether the subject is lying. The system has been rated to be 99.7% accurate. That's modern science for you, <Player>!

Now, what we want you to do is very simple, but it's an important mission nonetheless. You need to deliver the device to planet <ToPlanet> located in the <ToStar> system. Keep it in mind that our contract with the maloqs calls for the device to be delivered by <Date>. If you are late, you will have yourself some serious beef with them and with us. If you do it on time, you'll be paid <Money> credits. Good luck!

57.End: What is it, <Player>? The remains of an ancient penchesplasher? That's very interesting. You know, we are not quite used to receiving such generous gifts from pelengs. How about we make a little formal inspection? Nanosensitive scanning... microstructure analysis... visuals... Ha, that's no surprise! These are the bones of a regular penchecrakus stuffed with 19 remotely controlled and active miniature devices: 12 listening bugs, 4 concealed microcameras and three microscopic recording devices. All of this stuff falls under Article 657 of planet <ToPlanet>'s Criminal Code -- Espionage. Don't be so upset, it's only 7 years in a prison camp. They will give you scientific articles to read there and make you solve simple macrophysics and quasielectronics problems. In a nutshell, you will be rehabilitated. Oh, I am just kidding. The lie detector built into your armchair indicates that you are perfectly sincere. Come to think of it, the pelengs even did us a favor sharing their secret espionage toys with us. This may even call for a bonus. Here's <Money> cr for you.
57.Start: Yes, <Player>, we have a mission for you. You see, all the pelengs from planet <FromPlanet> have suddenly become aware of the error of their ways with respect to their purple Coalition partners. We have sto... umm... borrowed so many secret technologies from our colleagues the faeyans, while offering them nothing in exchange, that now we realize it is time to rectify this unfortunate oversight. Not so long ago, while excavating a site in the Chushan Valley, our archaeologists discovered the remains of a penchesplasher -- an ancient Churassic ancestor of the modern day penchekrakus. We believe that this find may be of great interest to the faeyan Paleontology Museum on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. So we would like you to deliver this gift to the faeyans as a sign of our eternal appreciation and friendship. If you deliver this cargo prior to <Date>, you will be paid <Money> cr.

End: We are glad to welcome you to the branch offices of the cleaning concern Puri-Tee on planet <ToPlanet>. Our motto is: Clean Out Everything -- of Everything! Just don't ask us to clean up the Galaxy and get rid of the dominators. This is but an advertising sound bite. By the way, you are our ten thousandth customer of your race today, so as part of our "quick, clean and tasty" promotion we will not only clean your... erm... rug quickly and thoroughly, but also treat you to some fenezal pizza. Or, rather, pay you a money equivalent thereof -- <Money> cr -- since we are all out of pizza, <Player>. But that's not all. Here, write down your address, and we will deliver your thoroughly cleaned item absolutely free.

Excellent. All right, let's have a look at this rag of yours... Man, this is a real treasure trove of different minerals and all kinds of insects, albeit somewhat battered, ha-ha! Isn't this impalia pedoptera by any chance? I kind of thought they went extinct three hundred years ago. All right, <Player>, I think vacuum cleaning and surface treatment with an all-purpose solvent will do the job. Goodbye!
Um... we need to show this rug to our scientists. They will be totally delighted. Where should we take it first -- to the Grand Entomology University or to the Geological Academy?
Start: Hold it, ranger! No, no, don't you make another step! Take off your dirty boo-- Oh, no! You know, <Player>, you have just wiped your feet on the first ever carpet weaved on our planet. It costs a fortune! You have just desecrated one of our most precious relics, and I wouldn't be surprised if a mob of textile workers and historians demanded your body, so that they could torture it in every unspeakable way imaginable. That's because we have a holiday coming -- the All-Planet Rug Weaver Day -- where this particular rug would be used in the weaving ceremony as a sample.

I've got an idea. Planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system has one of the best dry cleaning plants. Our secret service will help you safely leave the planet before news of your sacrilege becomes public knowledge. And may I suggest you get it done before <Date> or they will not be able to deliver the rug back to us in time for the All-Planet Rug Weaver Day.

End: Oh, <Player>, your timing couldn't be better! We've finished all preparations for the test some two hours ago. Did you bring the console from planet <FromPlanet>? Great, let's have it.

Here's your <Money> cr. Please sign the form here. Don't go away just yet. I suggest you take time to watch the magnificent sight of the shield being unfurled. Press this button... Look! That's right, you shouldn't be able to see anything since the shield is all transparent. Isn't this a stroke of genius? The secret here is that a multitude of cameras located on the outside of the shield project the image onto its inner surface. This helps prevent any discomfort this great new technology may have otherwise caused the population.

Umm... And what's this button for? Pressing... Oh, look, they are showing a hatchball game on the surface of the shield! Can you imagine it? The entire planet can now watch the game... well, basically, in the sky! Oh, those engineers... Except, perhaps, it's a tad too loud. Where's the volume button? So, this is the animal channel, and Penchecrakuses Around Us is on. And this is a news program, The Eyes of the Dzuhallag. Whoa! This is the adult channel -- oh my, look at that action! Only why is there only peleng programming... But it's all right, we will figure it out somehow. Thank you, ranger. All the best to you!
Start: Do you see that gadget, ranger? I bet you are wondering what it is for, aren't you? Great, let me give you a brief rundown then. At the moment, they are developing a planetary shield on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. According to the designers, the power shield should be able to envelope the entire planet in case of a dominator attack. Thus it will isolate the planet and prevent any landings on the surface -- or so they think. The shield is equipped with additional systems for ventilation and hyperprojection of video and audio onto its surface. It even has vacuum reflectors! All of this makes for an almost perfect universal solution.

Their scientists ordered this control console for the shield from us, as we are better at applied quasielectronics than they are. The shield will be built and deployed to orbit by <Date>. It is by that time that you will need to deliver the device to its destination for field testing.

End: Oh, you brought us the detector. Great! The maloqs are renown experts in interrogation techniques, and it would be very interesting to adopt some of their methods. Now we will become better at differentiating between criminals and honest citizens, and the rule of law will prevail on our planet! Your fee in the amount of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account.
What a strange lie detector, it looks more like an armchair! I have never seen such a bulky model...

Hmm... This must be a nerve-ending scanner, though it is in fact somewhat strange. And what is this built-in biological waste incinerator for? Oh, OK, there is something here in the manual about a hole for extremities processing. That's interesting. Now, myself, I am not ready to stick my hand into it, but maybe you would agree to test this wonderful device yourself? Relax, <Player>, I am just kidding!
6.Start: Ha-ha! Can you imagine it, <Player>? These humans from planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system are saying that their lie detector is ineffective! We decided to send them one of ours as a goodwill gesture. It is one hundred percent effective, and I'll eat a thousand red-belly stinkers if it this is not true! It used to be that we had to torture some of you pirate folk, and it was very effective. Our authorities have allocated <Money> cr to pay for the delivery. You must deliver the device before... let's say, <Date>.

60.End: Ranger <Player>, did you bring the forgotten book? All right, let's see... Now, what do we have here? A physics textbook... ...for elementary schools and private academies. And the point of bringing it over is? We have recently introduced new textbooks where physics is covered in more detail. And the old ones, with a lesser physics curriculum, got discarded. So some school kid left this wad of recyclable paper behind on planet <FromPlanet>. Big deal! Anyhow, here is the <Money> cr for your service. To your credit, you brought this throwaway back to us instead of trashing the galactic environment. Such noble yearnings should be encouraged.
60.Start: <Player>, will you be passing through the <ToStar> system by any chance? We need to have this book delivered to planet <ToPlanet>. A certain gaal left it behind a few months ago. What an idiot, the book contains some top secret data! It took our secret service some six months to decipher all of that stuff. We even had to pay a small fortune to contractors from a different planet. At the moment, we are still trying to process the data received, while the original book needs to be returned to the gaals. Let them believe we don't know anything. You'll have <Day> days to make the delivery. Upon delivery, the gaals will most likely pay you handsomely for the favor.

End: Ranger <Player>, how long do you expect us to wait for you? What's that supposed to mean, "wait a while, it's not like you have the Holy Grail delivered every day"? We have them delivered every hour! All kinds of crap too -- of every shape, color, size and even smell imaginable! Right before you, a peleng dragged some ungodly animal in and claimed it was the Holy Grail. Our analysts are going nuts trying to sort all this stuff out; the Order's storage facilities are jam-packed to capacity.

Well. If I am not mistaken, your find is from planet <FromPlanet>, from the maloqs? Hmm... What's its weight again, of this Grail of yours? Well, not that you could expect any different from the maloqs. With them, bigger and heavier means more valuable. So where do you suppose we should put this hulk? All right, go ahead, unload, and then we'll decide. I'll register it.

Item: Maloq Grail. Weight... !! Number assigned to find: 78.430. Yes, ranger, yes! Size: Huge -- no, strike that. Ginormous. Color: Present. All right, done! Here's your <Money> cr for making the delivery. Keep them coming, we'll be happy to take them off your hands. Only next time, please, bring smaller ones, because we are running out of storage space here.
Start: <Player>! What a great stroke of luck! Your timing is perfect. I hope you are aware that the Eternal Search Order is offering a huge reward to anyone who would find and bring them some Horny... no, Holy Grail. You never heard of it? Never heard of the 1,000,000 credit reward? Let me repeat it for you, in plain language: one million credits! This is like... more than ten maloqs have fingers on their hands! And on their feet too!

So who do you think was the first to find this Grail of theirs? Well, maloqs of course! So go ahead, load this find of ours into your cargo bay and head to the <ToStar> system full speed ahead. You will be met there, on planet <ToPlanet>, by a man from the Eternal Search Order who will take the parcel off your hands. And you'd better not pretend it was you who had found the Grail! We have already informed them of our find, and they can't wait to receive it.

A million credits... it sounds like music! Just imagine how many tons of weapons this is going to buy! Indeed, how many? Long story short, if you do it within <Day> days, you'll get <Money> cr right there and then. Whaddya say?

End: Ah, <Player>! The Galactic Patent Bureau has finally sent me down to meet you. Maloq scientists have already contacted the Bureau, but all we could get from their incoherent ramblings is that you were going to bring some kind of a mechanism over. Could I have a look at it?
Umm... What an interesting and inspiring... Umm... Aha... So that's how it is! Very interesting...

Bear with me, I'd hate to come through as overly pushy, but... could you explain what this thing actually is? <clr>A geartrunk<clrEnd>? What a strange and beautiful name! And what does it do? Promotes science and evolution? I have to admit, this is a very original and broadly defined purpose. And did the maloqs care to elaborate on how that stated goal is actually going to be achieved? You know, <Player>, of course we are going to pay you the <Money> cr due you, and we will even go as far as process the application for this... umm... geartrunk, if you will... But I am afraid that in the absence of any theoretical justification and accompanying documentation the patent application is going to be denied. The maloqs never gave you any documentation, did they? That's what I thought, but that's all right, that isn't your problem. We'll get back to them ourselves and send them all the necessary forms. Good luck to you!
Start: Greetings, oh brave ranger! Welcome to our technologically advanced planet! You don't believe me? Well, not that anyone else believes it, but now... Ha! We are going to prove it to the entire Galaxy that maloqs can do science too. Oh, now you are interested? All right, I am going to tell you, but only out of my great respect for you.

I am sure you know there are some important scientific discoveries that move evolution forward. The wheel, antibiotics, gunpowder, nuclear weap... umm... sorry, got carried away. Soooo.... Our scientists have discovered a way to improve and build upon one such discovery that had remained unchanged for thousands of years. This will be a true next step forward in science, a new stage of evolution.

How much do you know about mechanics? You must have heard of a gearbox. That's the invention that our scientists have improved. They have invented a... <clr>geartrunk!<clrEnd>! I'll tell you more: they are now working on a gearcoffer! Here it is, the new dawn, and it was us maloqs who made it possible!

Now, before someone else reinvents it, we have to get a patent on it ASAP. Help us out, ranger. This ingenious geartrunk of ours needs to be delivered to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system prior to <Date> so that all applicable patents could be issued. This way no one will be able to claim our invention as their own, and you will make <Money> cr. So are you going to help us?

End: Ah, <Player>! Did you bring the... umm... letter? My old buddy from planet <FromPlanet> should have passed it along. All right, give it to me!
You must be curious about what's in the letter, yes? Let's read it together then.

"Greetings, my friend, I hear you have finally got what you wanted and became some kind of a VIP." Umm, <Player>, this is just a regular letter from an old buddy. Nothing between the lines, no coded messages. Are you surprised? I bet this is the first time you get to deliver such a totally ordinary parcel. Don't worry, you are definitely getting your <Money> cr. All right, good luck to you, I'll see you later...
Start: Hello, ranger!

I bet you are going to be surprised when instead of a regular mission, like all those dozens of others, I am going to offer you something a little different from your usual fare. I would like to ask you to deliver... a letter. A totally unremarkable regular letter in a paper envelope.

It contains no important data, revelations or secret information. This is not even business correspondence, but rather a personal letter to my old friend who has a government job on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system.

I realize they do not normally turn to you with such mundane requests, but I figured the amount of <Money> cr would be incentive enough for you to make an exception and undertake to deliver the letter before <Date>.

End: Ah, <Player>! Did the maloqs ask you to bring this stool for inspection? Umm... All right, let's see what the gauges say.
All right... Umm... Aha! Hmm, so that's how it is!

Well, all I can tell you, <Player>, is that no maloq has ever touched this stool. On the other hand, at least five different individuals of peleng persuasion sat, lay, stood and even ate on it. And if you look here, lick here and swipe your finger here it will become clear to you that this is not an authentic maloq stool but a cheap imitation. This stool is <clr>comfortable<clrEnd> to sit on, it is <clr>not shaky<clrEnd>, and you <clr>cannot<clrEnd> get any splinters from sitting on it! No maloq job could be so crude. We suspect that pelengs are making such counterfeits right under the nose of maloq authorities.

We will forward a detailed inspection report to the maloqs, and you will get your well-earned <Money> cr.
