With your help, <Player>, maloqs will be able to stop this disgraceful racket with counterfeit stools and restore the good name of this... what's his name... Arrakh Arbakga. Best of luck, ranger!
Start: Yes, <Player>! Come on in, have a seat. Hold it! Just not on this stool! Here, sit on this... floor. So it's a little dirty, big deal. You know that for us maloqs stools have a certain ceremonial value. They are considered to be luxury items and are prohibited from everyday use.

I have an offer for you, ranger. This very stool needs to be delivered to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system as part of an ongoing investigation. The thing is that this stool was discovered in the house of Arrakh Arbakga whose rank, despite all his achievements, is not high enough for him to have such a luxurious item in his possession. When questioned, Arrakh claimed that the stool had been planted by his enemies and maligners, and we would like to send it to planet <ToPlanet> for forensic analysis. If you manage to do it before <Date>, the date of the court martial, we will pay you <Money> cr.

End: Me little bottle! Oh, my darling, you are still in one piece, as luck would have it. I am going to display you prominently in my office and hire someone to wipe dust off of you every three hours. Heck, every hour even! Oh, I am sorry, <Player>. I got way too emotional.

It's not like I have always been a businessman. I was born in the slums, to a a very poor family with way too many children. I have always dreamed of making a lot of money and leaving my pauper life behind. I have started small -- by collecting and redeeming bottles. Then I hired others to do it for me. Then I opened my own bottle redemption center which later became a chain. Then came my first glass container plant. Now, years later, I am the food industry minister and the corporation I have founded is a monopoly exporter and importer of alcohol on our planet.

And this here bottle was my <clr>first ever<clrEnd> -- the very first bottle I have picked up. It has become the primary incentive and the financial foundation of my business empire. Unfortunately, it is only now that I have finally managed to trace its fate and take possession of it again -- all of it thanks to you, ranger. As a sign of my gratitude for returning my good luck charm to me, please accept this <Money> cr. Try to spend it on something good and remember that a bottle here, a bottle there... that is a loan here, a loan there -- and it all adds up.

And now a commercial message: When buying any of our alcoholic beverages on planet <FromPlanet>, you can redeem your bottles at a special price and even receive a gift -- an amount equivalent to the redemption value of 16 bottles!
65.Start: Good afternoon to you, dear ranger. We have an assignment for you. The crux of the matter is that our Galactic Museum of Vials and Containers received a request from a certain businessman from planet <ToPlanet>. He would like to purchase a certain container from us. This is a glass container with a narrow neck that we call the Vessel of Moral Turpitude, and it happens to have been brought from the <ToStar> system. This benefactor must be concerned about preserving his homeland's cultural heritage. We simply cannot deny this gentleman's noble request and ask you to deliver this fragile vial to planet <ToPlanet> within <Day> days. Our client will pay you <Money> cr right there and then.

End: It's good to see you, ranger. We have already been informed that you brought the flight recorder that survived the crash of the dominator ship. Let's have it.

Well. And what may I ask is that? Umm... Etching: "Property of Apentuck Circus. To Be Used for the Saw Her in Half Trick. Inventory No.: 620." Oh God, ranger! I am really afraid to open this box. What if the dominator fell on the circus during that very trick? I shudder to imagine what may be inside! Still, you have honestly earned your <Money> cr. Here they are. As for the box... I am going to plant it on the next department up. Just imagine the kind of fun they are going to have when they open it up.
Start: Greetings, ranger! And goodbye -- seeing that you will probably want to get started right away on your way to the <ToStar> system so that you could make <Money> cr. That's some serious cash! All you have to do is deliver this little black box to planet <ToPlanet> within <Day> days.

Umm... Do you want to know what's in the box? So do we, very much so. The box was found amidst the ruins of the Apentuck Traveling Circus. There was a show on when an Equantor was shot down and crashed right into the building. The only thing that survived the explosion was this very black box. We have reasons to believe that this is an indestructible dominator flight data recorder similar to those we have on our own space ships, so that we could decipher the records and determine the cause of the crash.
Can you imagine? Chances are this box may contain data from the last few days of this dominator. Would you agree to deliver it to planet <ToPlanet> for analysis and decoding of the flight records?

End: Hello, ranger. You brought this tape right on time -- we have just figured out how to use this... what's its name... VCR. Yeah, that! While they are bringing it in from the museum, how about I have a look at what you brought?

Umm... Hmm... Terminator, Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines. Indeed, it sounds similar to dominators, and judging by the description it's about some killer robots from the future. Unless those scientists from planet <FromPlanet> mixed everything up and assuming this record is indeed some documentary footage of the rise of the dominators, it is quite possible that dominators may know the secret of time travel.
Here's your <Money> cr. I hope this ancient equipment still works as advertised and we can learn the secret of these dominator-terminators.
Start: Dear <Player>, we are glad to welcome you to our planet! Might you be looking for some easy money? Well, there is this very important parcel that needs to be delivered to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. We have discovered certain video records in ancient archives, and we have reasons to believe they have something to do with dominators. So what is so important and unusual here, you ask?

What if I told you these archives we found are a thousand years old? To be more exact, the videos date back to the end of the second millennium. So chances are we may have proof that dominators existed as early as a thousand years ago, which would radically change all our assumptions about these intelligent machines.

Unfortunately, these video records are on ancient media used by people over a thousand years ago, and we do not have any equipment we could use to watch them. Folks from planet <ToPlanet> agreed to help us out and transfer the records to modern media using some ancient equipment from their museums. If you can deliver these videos to them prior to <Date>, you will be paid <Money> cr.

68.End: That's great, <Player>! I haven't had me a laugh like this for a while! Had the orcs... I mean the maloqs read the book to the last page, they would have discovered it was published on one of our planets only two years ago. You have no idea how popular classical fantasy is at the moment. I have to admit even I read some in my spare time. I think an entire planet is a bit too much to ask for, even if some of our writers have excessively vivid imaginations. Just as it would be a little excessive to pay you <clr>10,000,000<clrEnd> cr for a delivery. I hope you won't hold a grudge if we only pay you <Money> cr for your troubles. No? Wonderful!
Start: We have an assignment for you, brave Ranger <Player>. Have a seat, relax, have a mug of ersatz mead. While our grooms are taking care of your mechanical horse, listen to what I have to say. It appears our rivalry with the faeyans is a few thousand years old. We thought they were but a bunch of vile sissies, but apparently there is a history here. And now there's proof! Just a few days ago we got hold of a historical document harking back to those times. It is called A Tale of Filaneya and Gromgar and it describes our own bravery and faeyan treachery. Back then, they were called elves and we were orcs, but otherwise it's clear how things really haven't changed at all. Here, <Player>, see for yourself:

"Once upon a time, our great ruler Gromgar gathered round his troops and embarked on a mission to defeat and depose his sworn enemy Filaneya. For three days they marched towards the rising sun, leaving a black swath of plundered and stripped earth in their wake. On the fourth day, the troops reached the very end of our lands, where on the other side of the border Filaneya himself was waiting for them with his pathetic army of flimsy, pointy-eared dorks. The troops then regrouped for battle and charged. Thus a great battle started, but neither side could prevail. Our warriors crushed and smashed left and right with their axes and maces, while the wicked wussies reciprocated with clouds of arrows and evil spells. Thus three days passed. Then all of a sudden Filaneya himself rode out in front of the lines and yelled (not much of a yell it was, to be sure, nowhere near as loud as ours) that while we were waging battle his troops invaded our lands and took our toothless elders and helpless children prisoner (not without some effort though, since our children are fairly active and old men not altogether toothless). And he said we'd better lay down our weapons or he'd waste all of our kin. And that was how peace was made with them on their terms."

That's how it all went down, <Player>! And never you mind that it was in the ancient times. Their abhorrent wickedness calls out to us through the centuries to be avenged. Kindly deliver a copy of this document to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system along with our demands for compensation for that horrible wrongdoing. It needs to be delivered by <Date> at the latest because then our Great Gorging will start and we won't have any more time to deal with these wretched faelings. Don't worry about your fee. We have put it into the document that they'd better pay you handsomely, or the main course at our Great Gorging may happen to be suspiciously purple.

End: <Player>, we are so happy you made it on time! You don't look too hot though: tired, pale, losing hair... You are not sick, are you? We recommend you visit the nearest medical center, but in the meantime, how about that parcel? It's hard to believe that we are finally going to have light restored for millions of residents. Come on, hurry up, we don't have a single second to waste. Give me that ring. Ouch! Have you gone mad? Don't you dare bite me! Ouch!! So that's how it is, huh? You know, <Player>, your ailment seems to be much more serious than I first thought. Get yourself checked out right away.

But that can still wait a while, and now look, the most important part of the process is coming right up. I am going to plug the device into this hollow that's been specifically made for it, the <clr>"Volcano"<clrEnd> machine will turn on, and the entire city will light up as if in the middle of the night. Here we go... By the way, did you notice the flashes of light dancing on its sides? They are so beautiful! You just can't take your eyes off of them. It's a real treasure. Yes, a treasure... my little crate of joy... my... precious...
<Player>, here's your <Money> cr, and now leave me alone! Goodbye. I hope you won't have any problems finding your way back to the ship in the dark.
Start: Have a seat, <Player>, and listen to my story. We have this old man living on our planet, an absolute genius but an eccentric nut too. His name is <cle>Gen-Doolf<clrEnd>, and he always walks around in a grey cloak and a broad-brimmed hat. And he's got a beard thiiis long. At the same time, he holds a few dozen degrees and has a ceremonial walking stick of a Top Academician. Ludicrous is what it is, but God's honest truth just the same.

So anyway, our quest pertains to the energy crisis that struck planet <ToPlanet> some time ago. Residents are sitting in the dark, and no electric trains or streetcars are running either. However, this <clr>Gen-Doolf<clrEnd> of ours has recently invented a totally new device for generating and accumulating energy. The coolest thing about the device is that it is very small and looks just like a regular ring. At the same time, it emits golden light and is capable of generating enough energy to power the entire planet. They have already built a <clr>"Volcano"<clrEnd> generator for that particular purpose, and now all they need is that little shiny ring thingy. Here, look! Careful! Don't touch it, it may be dangerous. It would have been delivered long ago, but the mischievous old timer set a number of conditions that none of the candidates had yet been able to meet. But I think you may fit right in. Are you ready? Great!
To begin with, is your heart pure? You don't have to answer, we have already scanned you upon arrival. There are some blemishes, but who doesn't have them nowadays? You pass.
Furthermore... You have to be short enough. Umm... squat a little. Some more. OK, that'll do too.

Next requirement: hairy feet. Don't ask me why, I feel ashamed as it is. Take your boot off, let's check. Umm... no, this won't do, <Player>! You let me down here, basically. Still, if you promise not to take off your boots until the mission is accomplished no one will ever know anything.

An now, his final wish. Do you have a good friend from each of the Coalition races that would agree to accompany you on your quest and share in all the hardships involved? No? It's too bad, because there is something else I haven't told you yet. A dangerous pirate, <clr>Siriman<clrEnd>, is also anxious to get hold of this energy source, and your ship will be in danger of being attacked by his minions while the device is on board.

If you agree, then here's the ring. And remember, you have only <Day> days to accomplish your quest, because all those poor folks on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system are suffering greatly with no light! If you can make it on time, there'll be <Money> cr in it for you.

End: Great, your brought this duplicate talisman of the maloq national team right on time! These unruly maloqs have already turned the entire Olympic village upside down demanding their stone back. Can you hear those yells in the distance? Well, they are back at it, searching other athletes.

As far as we know, their stone was smuggled off the planet long ago. It must have been the pelengs' doing since some of their athletes suddenly got sick right after the stone disappeared and flew back home. I'm sure they took the stone with them to sabotage the Olympics.
But everything will get back to normal now. We are grateful to you, <Player>! Planet <ToPlanet>'s Olympic Committee will have <Money> cr transferred to your account for delivering the duplicate.
Start: <Player>! Prove is to us that you greedy merchants are capable of something else besides wheeling and dealing. Like, for example, supporting your favorite teams. I hereby order you to become a sports fan! That half-baked human planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system will soon be hosting the <clr>552nd Olympic Games<clrEnd>. And what do you know, our national team's talisman has just been stolen! Those damn human cheaters!

So here are your orders: deliver a duplicate <clr>maloq national team talisman<clrEnd>, inscribed with their "Strength and Honor" motto, to planet <ToPlanet>. Deliver it to the human representative before <Date>, and he will pass it on to our team. And he'd better pass it on! Or our national team will take their stinky little planet apart!
If you agree to take this mission on, you will be paid <Money> cr.

70.End: <Player>, this is absolutely unbelievable! I am at a loss for words. What this new chip really is is an actual dominator component -- their processor, so to speak. And when that hapless kit model hobbyist puts his purchase together, the model comes alive and begins acting just like a dominator would. It would be all right with tiny models you could swat like a fly, but some are way larger than that. Damn crooks, hundreds of innocent civilians have already suffered from this faulty product, and many more have lost the very roofs over their heads. Unfortunately, under the laws of planet <FromPlanet> we cannot sue, so our only recourse is to buy and recycle what models there are out there. But it's all right, one day we will get it all back -- all of it, to the last credit. By the way, speaking of credits. It isn't your fault that they cheated you, so here's the <Money> cr you have earned in good faith. And don't forget to warn all your friends and family not to buy any dominator kit models. That's for their own good.
Start: Yes, we have a very simple delivery mission for you. No heroics required whatsoever, if that's what you are wondering.

Some time ago, a new toy plant opened on our planet that makes scaled down models. These models of famous pirate and ranger ships sell like there's no tomorrow because they look good and putting them together is great fun. You have to admit, it's really great when all of a sudden out of a pile of small parts there comes one complete whole, something like a space ship. But that's not all! A month or so ago, we opened a new line to produce models of different dominator ships: shtips, smershes, equantors, etc. You know, all those mysterious lines and curves, blinking lights and whatnot. They do look good. Naturally, we make them in all kinds of sizes, from really tiny tabletop pieces to actual sizes. What's even better is that we have this new chip designed specifically for these models, so they behave just like the real things. They can move and even fly. The slogan for the new model line is: "Put the Six Thousand Parts Together Just Right and Get Your Very Own Dominator!"

That's pretty impressive, isn't it? We are flooded with orders, and our own couriers cannot deliver them all, so we have to hire outside contractors, such as yourself, <Player>. If you agree to deliver one of those dominator model kits to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system, we will pay you <Money> cr and also give you a nice discount if you decide to buy a couple of those models for your own use.

71.End: <Player>, we are so happy you have arrived on time. The <clr>Iron Butt<clrEnd> has gone totally crazy and now sics his hunting hellhounds on workers that fail to complete their daily assignments. Go ahead, get your paperwork done and unload. In the meantime, we will transfer the money to your account.
Start: Oh, <Player>, I am so glad you are interested. I have a mission I could give you though I am not sure you would even want it since it is some fairly dirty work. What? Oh, no, no, you misunderstood me. There's no need to kill anyone, you'll just need to make a delivery.

The thing is that the longtime commander-in-chief of our planet's armed forces, General Screameroff, also unofficially known to his numerous fans as Iron Butt, has recently retired. During the retirement ceremony held in his honor, he announced that he would retire with a clean conscience and spend his days at his country estate enjoying fishing and hunting. He has found a great place on planet <ToPlanet> to build his retirement property. The only problem is that it is fairly far away from here. What is even worse, he has bought some construction materials on the cheap here, and now they need to be delivered to the site. We need to do it ASAP, and we could use all the help we could get.

If you, <Player>, agree to deliver a container of construction materials to the <ToStar> system where the site is located, we will pay you <Money> cr. The important part is to make the delivery before <Date>, or we will fall behind schedule and all the contractors will get shot, which, naturally, is something we would like to avoid.
Oh, and one other thing. Your ship will have to be large enough for the container, so you may have to throw out some of the old junk you have in your cargo bay before loading.

End: All right, <Player>, who is this you brought with you? Aha! But of course, this is Blast Shot -- the villain that had been wanted by our law enforcement authorities for committing grave crimes against our economy! Great job, <Player>!
By the way, there is a reward of <Money> cr offered for his capture. I am only too happy to pay you this amount in hard galactic currency. Thanks a lot! Have a pleasant day, <Player>!
Start: Of course he is here, that fracking bambay!

Pardon my French, <Player>, but a few weeks ago I made a rash decision to invite the veteran of the anti-piracy movement, Blast Shot, to come and visit for a few days, and share his experience fighting pirates with us. Man, I should have known better, may Corsairs chop him up into liverwurst!

That weasel turned out to be so nice, that it's been ten days and we still can't send him home. I wish him a lyakusha down his throat! It's not that we aren't flattered to have such a star around, but he gets so passionate while speaking in public, that now my staff are peppering their speech with things like "go to pulsar," "shaved penchecrakus" and other such gems. Those are still fairly harmless phrases -- unlike some of the others he comes up with.

You wouldn't want to know where he's brainwashed them into thinking they should send our President! Thankfully he doesn't know, otherwise he wouldn't hesitate to send at least half of my staff to those places himself. But, there is a solution! Yes, there is one, dog blast his creative bone!

I have just made a deal with planet <ToPlanet>, which is in the <ToStar> system. They'd be all too happy to take Blast Shot off our hands, and perhaps listen to some of the tales of his heroic feats while they're at it. The responsibility of delivering this loud-mouth his new venue would be up to you, <Player>. Upon arrival, the receiving party will pay you <Money> cr.
If you agree, get started ASAP. May solar winds cast you far and fast, doggone it, and back!

End: Many thanks for the prompt delivery, <Player>! These instruments you have brought, they are absolute marvels. Just you listen to that rich sound the percussion drill alone makes! This is amazing! Truly remarkable! Furthermore, you can even do brain surgery with it. Want to see one?

Umm, <Player>, what's that with your face? I am calling my assistant. It looks like we may be having us our first non-faeyan patient. Are you all right, <Player>? Oh, it's about your fee! Sorry for my lack of sensitivity. Yes, of course! Here's your fee, and please do not faint again. In order to beat the dominators, the Coalition needs strong rangers.
Can you walk now? Then go.
Start: As you may be aware, <Player>, faeyans have not a musical bone in their bodies. They can't tell a "fa" from a "sol." Neither can you? My condolences! However, while in your case, <Player>, this affliction may have come from the regular practice of trying to discern by ear what is wrong with your engine, the fae simply do not have the requisite parts of their brains sufficiently developed.
We wish we knew what parts they are. Then we could fix our purple brains using traditional methods. Let's leave it at that, for I have just eaten.

However, one of our faeyan research centers appears to have found a solution to this natural mystery. However, they do need a set of percussion instruments for that. Seeing that we have promised to give our intelligent brethren any assistance possible, I decided to take the initiative here. I called our local hypermarket and asked them to put together a collection of every percussion instrument they may have in stock.

It will be your job to deliver this cargo to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system -- and do it quickly and carefully too. If you can manage that within the next <Day> days, you'll earn yourself <Money> cr. So, are you ready to help your brothers in mind?

End: What is it you brought me, <Player>? Oh, my God, I can't believe it! This is ein-drein! Now we will be able to restore the population of these unique tendrogynous animals! One second, I need to make an important phone call right away.

Chuchjerro, it's me. They just brought in ein-drein. Now we've got an entire complement of these critters. You can go ahead with your advertising campaign and start selling tickets for the show. Don't forget to arrange for live stereocasting. It's not every day duckowiaks are saving their population the natural way, do not agree to anything less than seventy percent of advertising profits.
<Player>, are you still here? Oh, yes, here's your fee. Would you like a pass for the show? No? All right, you can go then.
Start: <Player>, I have a very important and sensitive mission for you. What do you know about duckowiaks? That doesn't surprise me in the slightest. Duckowiaks are herbivorous mammals with six paws and a hard carapace. A few hundred years ago, there were tons of them in the forests of planet <ToPlanet>. But now these unique animals are on the verge of extinction. Despite their remarkable survivability, they have a weak spot that not even omnipotent evolution could improve upon.

I am sure you know that we faeyans are hermaphrodites, and maloqs and humans have two genders. Well, now, duckowiaks are the only species known to science that have ten genders. All right, all right, keep your vivid fantasies in check, <Player>! These unique animals simply cannot survive in their natural habitat any longer. If for no other reason than that there is always going to be one crazy peleng hunter or other around with a plasma gun. Fortunately, that race also has quite adequate scientists advocating for preserving unique flora and fauna for posterity.

They have already managed to find specimens of seven of the ten genders. But in order to preserve the species, all ten are required. So pelengs turned for help to their colleagues from other worlds. And what a smart move that was! To help achieve this noble goal, humans agreed to give up their only beloved beaverakus, and the maloqs sent their drycoon. On our part, we decided to make available to the Peleng Zoological Society the only surviving ein-drein in the Universe. Our only problem is that unlike the maloqs we have no fleet to deliver the animal to where the final stage of this undertaking will be taking place.

You, <Player>, have a unique chance here to do something really useful for science. If you deliver the cage with this animal to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system before <Date>, we will be very grateful and pay you <Money> cr. But don't be late -- time is of the essence here. Our ein-drein isn't exactly a spring chicken any longer and may become infertile any moment. So, what do you say?

75.End: A special cargo, you say? All right, let's see... What do you think it is? Hand-made ceramics from the 25th century? Ranger, how can you possibly be so gullible? Even a total ignoramus would be able to see that this junk is ten years old at the utmost. See, you can even read it on the bottom: Pkhedoc Souvenirs Ltd. Get rid of this junk immediately. Then again, hold on a minute, what's this on the side? Oh, my God, this is a rendering of the legendary Dzag-Dzog fish that is only found in Pkhedoc swamps. Even though there have been over 10 million sightings of it, the fish has never been properly classified and is thus not recognized by official ichthyology. Amazing! This will go straight to a museum, and you are getting a bonus of <Money> cr.
75.Start: Mission? But of course! Have you ever been to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system? You don't remember? If you had, you wouldn't have forgotten it. One of their ministers has a collection of ancient ceramics to kill for. 25th century, hand-made, experimental materials, first ever attempts at nanospraying. Yum! And what do you know, not too long ago, while at this flea market... I mean an antiques auction, I found this cute little piece that would fit right in with his collection. Solid, friendly relations with planet <ToPlanet> are very important for us now, but unfortunately we have had our share of differences lately, so you absolutely must deliver this wonderful work of art to the minister. I hope <Money> cr will provide a sufficient incentive for you to accomplish this mission before <Date>.

76.End: Ranger, you are virtually shining with happiness. And that's not just some kind of a metaphor. That's what the Geiger counter is saying. Man, you and your cacti belong in a lighthouse. You'll shine better than any bulb they may have. So what are we going to do? All right, we can throw the cacti into the bioreactor, which has been craving more fuel lately anyway. And don't you worry, your plants will be warm and comfy in it. But you, <Player>, are a victim of circumstances here if I understand it correctly. You need medical attention, so here's your compensation in the amount of <Money> cr, and go have yourself taken care of. The only string attached, of course, is that you get treated at our own healthcare center.
76.Start: We are very concerned about the quality of healthcare on maloq planets. Did you know that every year electromagnetic radiation emanating from office equipment is sending zero to one maloq to various Coalition hospitals? The condition of these patients may vary. We simply cannot sit and watch how badly our red friends disregard their health, so we have prepared a special humanitarian shipment for planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system -- cactuses. These undemanding plants bred by humans many centuries ago have long served humanity by absorbing harmful electromagnetic radiation. Your help will come in very handy for the residents of planet <ToPlanet>. Oh, yes, the cacti must be watered by <Date>, or they will die, so you need to complete your mission before that date. Once you arrive at <ToPlanet>, you will be paid a bonus of <Money> cr.

End: Oh, come on, ranger, give me that parcel, quick! No, don't you even think of opening it! These damn maloqs play chemists on their own planet and we pay the price. When last year they sent us their Didi Tee anti-dominator powder, our entire star system became swarmed with dominators. That damn magic dust did a better job than a transfactorial beacon would. Only instead of dying in agony the dominators went berserk and started destroying everything in sight until they finally got to our Didi Tee stores. It was only when they destroyed the cache along with the building it was stored in that they calmed down.

For that reason, we now test all experimental maloq chemicals first -- on an uninhabited planet in a different sector of space. You never know with them maloqs -- what if some of their stuff actually works?
Here are your <Money> cr for this delivery -- you have earned them in good faith. It isn't your fault that maloqs have no brains and everyone is afraid to tell them so.
Start: Ranger <Player>, stand by for a mission of utmost importance! You think yo are ready enough? Excellent! Then listen carefully!

As you are well aware, dominators have come to exist through gross negligence on the part of their humanoid creators -- Coalition scientists. They quickly multiplied and went on a regular quest to take over the entire Galaxy. Over time, they have captured many additional stellar systems. Taking over a territory, they continue to multiply there and prepare to capture new, yet unmolested worlds. So, basically, they behave like cockroaches -- the scourge of antiquity. These days single specimens of these horrible pests are kept at zoos on different planets, but in the old times they had entire cities on their knees. Can you imagine that a single apartment could be home to up to a hundred of these disgusting crispy critters?

And now, <Player>, I am going to let you in on a military secret. When dominators were being developed, they used cockroaches as behavioral models -- due to their phenomenal survivability and adaptability to the environment. So you see, those crazy professors hit the spot and created an ideal enemy that is an absolute joy to fight. However, all the other races somehow do not share our enthusiasm. Moreover, they keep asking us to develop a perfect weapon to fight dominators. So now I am going to show it to you. May I present the Bin-Key crayon that took years and millions of credits to develop.

It is to you, ranger, that the honorable job of delivering this experimental sample to its test site falls. It is located on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. If you decide to take this mission on, you need to hurry because the sample will have to be tested before <Date> -- otherwise it may expire and bring about consequences no one can possibly imagine. Don't worry about the money. In fact, you are taking part in the effort to save the entire Galaxy.

End: What is it you've got there, <Player>? A <clr>Jimi Hendrugz'<clrEnd> guitar? The real thing? Well, you can dump it on top of that pile of trash by the exit. Why are you so surprised? Look at it: it's all beat up, the paint is peeling, the strings are all torn. Nope, it doesn't look like quality merchandise at all.

Using our current advanced technologies, we managed to restore this guitar based on photos and records of those years, so in the end it came out even better than the real thing and very pleasing to the eye. Just you look at it shine! By the way, in addition to this guitar, we have also recreated Drinko Starr's drums, the organ of Babach, Pagan Nino's violin, the harp of Harpheus and the two flat stones prehistoric people used to make sounds. So, as you can see, we're on top of this famous musical instruments business. However, this being a holiday today, we will still pay you for this delivery as per the existing contract. And now, why don't you join the festivities? We could even let you play a drum solo...
Wait, where are you going, ranger?!
Start: Ranger, how do you feel about classic rock of the ancient times? Don't feel anything at all since you were not yet born back then? I see. Still, didn't you dream, as a school kid, of putting a band together and becoming a star for the millions? Of winning over a few girlie hearts? Hey, you may have even bought those drums, huh? And even had a go at them for a few weeks before realizing you had no talent whatsoever? No, I never read your file -- and where would I even get it? It's just that it is usually those whose dreams have been crushed by the harsh reality that go on to become rangers. In other words, losers that can't do anything else.

Anyhow, I digress. My apologies if I have offended you somehow. I was only trying to approach the nature of your mission gradually. The crux of the matter is that we on this planet have chanced upon one of the greatest musical relics of all times -- a guitar used by <clr>Jimi Hendrugz<clrEnd> himself. Never mind that you probably never heard the name. He was a cult guitarist and even died young as a real rock 'n" roll idol should -- at the peak of his glory and largely underappreciated. But his guitar is still around.

We learned that it has been migrating from one private collection to another, gradually losing value, and then, some thirty years ago, got stolen while being transported from one planet to another. After that, it was sold to the maloqs for an exorbitant sum. You may wonder why on earth they wanted it to begin with. Well, the sellers positioned it as an exclusive, handmade holder of special combat strings for garroting enemies. The maloqs would soon realize that the guitar was not particularly handy as a string holder since while they were messing with frets and nuts their victim would manage to escape. Disappointed and having finally had it with the piece, the maloqs sold it to us for a real pittance -- <clr>1,000<clrEnd> credits.

We would be happy to keep it, but we really need to prop up our friendly relations with human planet <ToPlanet> located in the <ToStar> system. For that reason, we are giving this priceless relic to them as a goodwill gesture. If you, <Player>, can bring the guitar to them safe and sound, you will be paid <Money> cr. But you'll need to hurry! We would like to have it delivered in time for the music festival that will begin on planet <ToPlanet> in <Day> days. It will be rather symbolic.

End: <Player>, you've finally arrived! Relax, I'm not going to hit you with this sledgehammer. What's that vacuum cleaner you've got there? Was it issued by the gaals? See that opening in the wall with the open door? Put the hose in there. Stop pinching your nose. You think a garbage chute ought to smell like roses? Here, take the hose. I'll turn it on. <Player>, don't let go of it! There, ready. Take out the hose. Now we open the container.
Fluffy, my darling kitty, how did you manage to jump into the garbage chute! ! I've been worried sick all this time. I'm just glad you didn't starve to death - I was worried about that.

Oh, <Player>, you have no idea how worried I was about this cat! Can you imagine? He jumped into the garbage can -- which I then threw out -- and managed to get stuck in this section of the pipe. We didn't want to make a hole in the wall, so we asked the gaals to deliver the appropriate apparatus. While you were brining the equipment, we were feeding the poor animal as best we could. To keep this from happening again, I'll be buying this cat extractor from you. Will <Money> cr be enough? Don't get greedy, <Player>, I can't give you more. Take this amount and leave. I still have to get Fluffy to the veterinarian.
Start: <Player>, you probably know that gaals are number one when it comes to protecting flora and fauna. At our initiative, the Intergalactic Service to Save Living Nature was created, tasked with the preservation of diverse species of non-rational creatures. All of the Coalition races are represented in the ranks of our organization. It was our efforts that averted testing of the maloq neutron bomb, the Fat Bambay, on planet Sanctuary Kuchgun, home to 134,569 endemic species and 251,984 endangered species. And we've also managed to eradicate the peleng virus which was being tested on planet Moreys.

Our planet <FromPlanet> is leading the way in developing special hardware to save protein life forms. It so happens we need a volunteer for this. The head of the government of the human planet <ToPlanet> is asking us to deliver a vacuum extractor for small organisms. Here it is, by the way. What do you mean, it looks like a vacuum cleaner? Then again, if you look inside, the principle of operation is pretty similar.

Let's get back to the mission. People say a most valuable animal ended up in a trap in one of the capital's buildings and that it can only be extracted safely using our hardware. You need to make it within <Day> days, otherwise the people will resort to their own methods, which may injure the precious animal. If you successfully extract the animal from the trap, the employer will happily pay you a fee.

End: It is so nice of you, <Player>, to deliver this gift from the maloqs right on time for our Technomania Day when our great civilization celebrates its achievements in science. Unfortunately, one of our scholars made an inconsiderate comment calling the maloq race a set of 43 genetic mistakes. We now tend to believe that there are way fewer mistakes in that set -- that is, only 12. With the number this low, they may actually be perceived as fairly intelligent creatures. By the way, what is this strange ticking inside the box? It must be an ancient metronome. It's all right, we will improve on it and send it right back to <FromPlanet>.

Thank you again for helping our two civilizations to reconcile! Please accept this <Money> cr as compensation for your services. Please pass our apologies along to the maloqs. We are very grateful for the gift.
8.Start: Arrgh, <Player>, have you heard the news yet? The fae declared the entire maloq race a pack of animals and a mistake of nature! These are blatant lies! The maloqs have already prepared an adequate answer, right on time for some stupid faeyan holiday. Here are your orders: deliver this <clr>surprise gift<clrEnd> to the fae on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system within <Day> days. Do not concern yourself with the ticking inside the gift. Nothing is going to happen until <Date>. You've done some dirty work before, so I am sure you could do it again without asking questions. Those stupid faeyans will even pay you <Money> cr for making the delivery.

80.End: How glad we are to see you, Ranger <Player>! It has been horribly troublesome to perform health procedures for our president and feed him, hanging him by his feet from the ceiling -- especially considering he gave orders with his... Anyway, it doesn't matter. We hope the FREAK will return our leader to his original superior form. Here's your <Money> cr for the timely delivery.
Start: Ranger <Player>, we have an important errand for you!

Our maloq brothers are in dire need of our help. The problem is that their scientific investigations into teleportation devices turned out to be a disaster during the first real-world trial. Specifically, the president of planet Ramgatrue was transported from his home planet to <ToPlanet>. But because the teleporter used involves the molecular reconstruction of the subject -- and for maloqs this technology is experimental and unmanageably difficult -- there was an incident: their leader was assembled incorrectly. Now his armor is inseparable from his skin, his knees are an extension of his chest muscles, and out of his chin... Well, you can see for yourself. We need you to deliver our already time-tested FREAK (Form Restorative Energy Attentive Konstructor) teleporter, which should restore the maloq leader's original form.
You must deliver the teleporter to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system no later than <Date>. You will paid a generous fee of <Money> cr there.

81.End: Oh, Ranger <Player>! The congress was on the verge of collapse, but you arrived just in time and Professor d'Agama is sure to argue in favor your burth or whatever it's called... Thank you for facilitating interracial scientific discourse. An honorarium has already been transferred to your account.
Start: <Player>, you must immediately resolve a diplomatic issue of galactic significance! The earthling Professor Val d'Agama has prepared a report for the Intergalactic Congress of Astronomers (ICA) happening on <ToPlanet>. The report centers around the logic and conformity to law of the preposition that life was spontaneously generated on his home planet. It's simply a stereotypical view about the absurdity of the existence of terrestrial civilizations for a number of reasons: catastrophic climate change that refers to seasonal changes; ice ages; the prevalence of water over land on the planet's surface; freezing at the poles; the presence of precipitation, liquid and solid water; flares on a sun about which Earth rotates, which has an oppressive effect on all life, etc. etc. The professor collected material which has convinced an honorable colleague that even in conditions so incompatible with life the planet could still be inhabited by an enormous number of diverse life forms. But, alas, I forgot the password-protected drive in my office.
You must deliver it to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system by <Date>. The congress will pay you <Money> cr for your services.

End: Oh, <Player>, you're here at last. Gimme that note, quick! What, money first?! We don't have time for arguments or formalities, gimme that! That's it, don't even think about making a move, not with all these bootlickers I got here. One whistle from me, and they'll tear you to pieces.

Don't worry, I'll give you the money, but first let's see what's in that sarcophagus. I have a direct communication channel with the excavation site, so now I'll start reading these phrases aloud to try and open the lock. Okay, so is it "Schizburger"? No? "Mig Bac," "Mueberry Bluffin," "Kitchen McGunnets"? It looks like those screw-ups from the planet <FromPlanet> have given us something completely different from what we need! "Order's up," "Exact change appreciated," "I'm lovin' it," "Next customer, please," "Take this p--" Aaah, <Player>, do you see it?! It started to open! Ahaha, next customer, please! It's opening! Be quick about it, you dunces, what's inside?! Gold?! A whole lot of gold?!! There's... what is that?! Were those inside? A red size-25 shoe and a clown nose? That's all?! Are you trying to play me for a patsy??!

It looks like my subordinates decided to swindle me and keep all the gold for themselves. I need to deal with them immediately, but I'd rather not have any outsiders here while I'm doing that. Don't worry about the money; it's already been transferred to your account. Good luck and see you later.
Start: I got a special task for a tough pirate like you, <Player>. Our buddies from the planet of <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> star system were doing some archaeological excavations and came across an ancient M-shaped monument buried in the ground, with a tomb under it. Inside, they discovered a sarcophagus which they were unable to unseal despite their best efforts. After some scientists examined it, it was discovered that the sarcophagus had a voice lock. This means that it can only be opened with a specific sound, word, or even phrase. Of course, we could try to open it up the old-fashioned way, with a nice pile of explosives, but then there's the chance that we would damage or completely destroy the unknown ancient treasures hidden inside the sarcophagus.

The blockheads have failed to find the correct password on their own, so they've turned to us. We searched through various archives that have been collecting dust since the period of the Coalition's power and picked a few phrases, one of which may turn out to be the key to opening the sarcophagus. If you really want to know what's inside, and you think that <Money> cr. is a sufficient reward for your efforts, fly there and bring them this note. We could use interplanetary communication to send it, but the fewer ears hear about the contents of this piece of paper, the better. Also, you need to do this within <Day> days, or I'm afraid those fools will not be able to resist the temptation to try and open the sarcophagus by force.

83.End: Yeeehhaa! You did it, <Player>! To be honest, you aren't the most interesting participant to show up in the years that this show has been on the air, but you came in first, and that's the main thing. Now get ready to have your mailbox filled with thousands of declarations of love, proposals to multiply your species, and curses from those who supported the other participants. I wish you good luck!
Start: The Penchecrakus Race, <Player>! Never heard of it? It's only the most popular reality show in the last ten years! Here's how it works: ten candidates -- irrespective of their age, sex, occupation, and other social and physiological factors -- are randomly chosen, and every one of them is given a locked card with <Money> credits. In order to activate the card and get the money, you need to be the first to reach the destination. The final goal in this round is the planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> star system. You know, you're extremely lucky that I'm selecting the participants this time. Accept the role before I change my mind.

If you're thinking of asking me about the rules, well, there ain't any. It's a pirate show, you know, and that's why it's so popular. Shoot, destroy, cheat, start a clash between other contestants -- in short, have as much fun as you want! Oh no, I'm actually lying: there is one rule. We're gonna fill your ship with cameras which will give us a constant, clear picture of everything you're doing. You can't turn those cameras off. That's the rule! 'Cause it's a reality show, you know, not just some boring delivery mission! You'll become an idol to billions of viewers. You have a fair shot, with your appearance and your pirate's service record. If you agree, here's your card. Now beat it! Get to the hangar quick! The analysts estimate that your lead rival will reach the destination around <Date>, so you need to outrun him and get there first!

84.End: Good for you, <Player>! You've made it in time. But it wouldn't be tragic even if you had been late. We can't open yet since several of the most valuable exhibits have been stolen from under our very noses. Before all those splendid antique rusty rapiers and golden crowns are returned to us, there's no way the museum can open its doors to visitors. Thank you, anyway.
Start: I got a task for you, <Player>. It's a piece of cake! A new piracy museum is opening on the planet of <ToPlanet>. It will feature the bones of famous pirates, various keepsakes, some jewels that brought fame to the pirates who stole them, ship wreckage, cannonballs, stuffed parrots, and anything else that was successfully salvaged from the old museum after, in a misunderstanding, it was looted by pirates when the <ToStar> system was retaken from the Coalition.

Your mission is to bring the museum its most valuable exhibit: an ancient pirate flag with a skull and crossbones on a black background. It was called the Jolly Rovher, and it was under this flag that Frake, a famous Bambay, made his armed assaults. If you get it here before the opening of the museum, which is scheduled for <Date>, you'll get <Money> cr. from the receivers.
So, do you want to take a short break from fighting and make some money at the same time? If you do, then I'm putting your name on the contract.

End: Well, <Player>, I see that you've arrived and that the capsule you've brought is safe and sound. You weren't delayed and you never tried to open the capsule, which means that you have passed our special test. Congratulations! Now you can open it. Don't be afraid, there's no bomb on it. Open it. Good! And now, meet Bob. Bob's the doll that we use to test our pirates. It can blink, shout "All aboard!" or "Pieces of eight!", or even transmit a signal to our equipment if the capsule is opened before the addressee receives it.

You're dishonorable but committed to our pirate cause. Let me shake your claw, and let no talk of distrust ever come between us. You can trust me when I say that the money promised to you for this task is already in your account.
Start: A job? Yeah, I do have a job, and may I drop dead if it's not a job for a true pirate!

We have one of the Coalition's leaders -- those pompous loudmouths! -- sitting literally in the room right next to us. He is a key figure on the political stage, and the fact that he's in our hands is like having a trump card.

He has to be delivered to the planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> star system. There he'll be hidden so deep that none of the rebels will ever hear of him again. This needs to be done within <Day> days, or the whole plan will go to the Klissan dogs. You are a respectable pirate, <Player>, and you're responsible too, which is quite rare among our lot, so I think you'll be able to cope with this task. The main thing is, don't let any humanoid know what you're doing, even if they say they're fascinated with the romance of piracy!

So he wouldn't try to muddle your brain during the transport -- and these bigwigs really know how to wag their tongues -- we put him in a cryocapsule equipped with a detonating lock in case someone intrudes and tries to open it. So, are you up for it? Or are <Money> cr. not enough money for you? Or maybe you just don't have the guts?

End: Oh, it's a bribe! Well, <Player>, did you know that bribing is considered a crime on our planet?!

Haha, you can relax! We're on a pirate planet. Here, bribes aren't just natural, they're obligatory! If you don't take a bribe for a week, everyone starts looking at you askance, and if no one greases your palm for several months in a row, you're removed from your position! The problem is, you see, no one is offering me a bribe. And I don't know what's wrong! Or even if they do, their offer is so transparent that I don't get it. That's why I have to ask my old friend to send me envelopes from time to time. So, I want to thank you for helping to cover for me, <Player>! You've earned <Money> cr. It's yours by right.
86.Start: I can offer you a bribe, <Player>. No, not you personally. There's nothing to give it to you for. I'm asking you to bring this well-sealed envelope made of dense, non-transparent plastic to the <ToStar> star system and hand it over to a representative from the planet <ToPlanet>. He knows who it is from, so there's no need to clarify anything: just give him the envelope in silence, with a mysterious air, and you'll get <Money> cr. for the delivery.

9.End: Excellent, <Player>! It's about time we stopped the peleng monopoly on breeding ragobam bullfrogs. Hmm... It's rather strange they let us have the device free of charge. Apparently, they never found an efficient enough method to produce this valuable natural resource on planet <FromPlanet>. I think it will suffice to simply increase the radiation yield severalfold, and it will all click into place. We have already transferred your fee of <Money> cr to your account.
Start: My dear lyakusha <Player>, how would you like to pocket <Money> cr for some fairly easy little piece of business? Our planet suffers from the glut of ragobam bullfrogs, they give no hold for food literally. And all of this is because of the experimental <clr>bullfrog breeding device<clrEnd> we have been testing. This is what comes out of any attempts to modify unfinished gaalian projects. A small design mistake has been originally made, and now we cannot even turn the device off since this may cause a terrible disaster -- an explosion of the built-in hypernuclear synthesizer that transforms vacuum power into matter. The explosion itself won't be large, no more than a light bulb going out. However, at least in theory, it may trigger a chain reaction involving every last speck of matter on our planet. This has not been proven to exhaustion, but still we'd rather not take any chances.

On the other hand, we simply cannot put up with the current situation either. There are more and more bullfrogs around every day, and we have no idea how to get rid of them. Our world is tittering on the brink of environmental disaster. The only solution would be to remove this device and take it somewhere far enough from here. Like, to give it to the humans that are eager to start breeding bullfrogs.

So why don't you, my good man, take this device that as you can see is simply raining bullfrogs and deliver it to planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system? Take care of it, and you will not only make yourself a nice chunk of cash but also earn our sincere peleng gratitude. However, you must accomplish it all within <Day> days or your spaceship will simply burst at the seems from all those multiplying bullfrogs.
